10.66.d: देवान हुवे बर्हच्छ्रवसः सवस्तये जयोतिष्क्र्तो अध्वरस्यप्रचेतसः | ये वाव्र्धुः परतरं विश्ववेदसैन्द्रज्येष्ठासो अम्र्ता रताव्र्धः ||
10.66.e: I CALL the Gods of lofty glory for our weal, the makers of the light, well-skilled in sacrifice;  Those who have waxen mightily, Masters of all wealth, Immortal, strengthening Law, the Gods whom Indra leads.

10.66.d: इन्द्रप्रसूता वरुणप्रशिष्टा ये सूर्यस्य जयोतिषो भागमानशुः | मरुद्गणे वर्जने मन्म धीमहि माघोने यज्ञंजनयन्त सूरयः ||
10.66.e: For the strong band of Maruts will we frame a hymn: the chiefs shall bring forth sacrifice for Indra's troop,  Who, sent by Indra and advised by Varuṇa, have gotten for themselves a share of Sūrya's light

10.66.d: इन्द्रो वसुभिः परि पातु नो गयमादित्यैर्नो अदितः शर्मयछ्तु | रुद्रो रुद्रेभिर्देवो मर्ळयाति नस्त्वष्टा नोग्नाभिः सुविताय जिन्वतु ||
10.66.e: May Indra with the Vasus keep our dwelling safe, and Aditi with Ādityas lend us sure defence.  May the God Rudra with the Rudras favour us, and Tvaṣṭar with the Dames further us to success.

10.66.d: अदितिर्द्यावाप्र्थिवी रतं महदिन्द्राविष्णू मरुतःस्वर्ब्र्हत | देवानादित्यानवसे हवामहे वसून रुद्रांसवितारं सुदंससम ||
10.66.e: Aditi, Heaven and Earth, the great eternal Law, Indra, Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the lofty Sky.  We call upon Ādityas, on the Gods, for help, on Vasus, Rudras, Savitar of wondrous deeds.

10.66.d: सरस्वान धीभिर्वरुणो धर्तव्रतः पूषा विष्णुर्महिमावायुरश्विना | बरह्मक्र्तो अम्र्ता विश्ववेदसः शर्म नोयंसन तरिवरूथमंहसः ||
10.66.e: With Holy Thoughts Sarasvān, firm-lawed Varuṇa, great Vāyu, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, and the Aśvins Twain,  Lords of all wealth, Immortal, furtherers of prayer, grant us a triply-guarding refuge from distress.

10.66.d: वर्षा यज्ञो वर्षणः सन्तु यज्ञिया वर्षणो देवाव्र्षणो हविष्क्र्तः | वर्षणा दयावाप्र्थिवी रतावरीव्र्षा पर्जन्यो वर्षणो वर्षस्तुभः ||
10.66.e: Strong be the sacrifice, strong be the Holy Ones, strong the preparers of oblation, strong the Gods.  Mighty be Heaven and Earth, true to eternal Law, strong be Parjanya, strong be they who laud the Strong.

10.66.d: अग्नीषोमा वर्षणा वाजसातये पुरुप्रशस्ता वर्षणा उपब्रुवे | यावीजिरे वर्षणो देवयज्यया ता नः शर्मत्रिवरूथं वि यंसतः ||
10.66.e: To win us strength I glorify the Mighty Twain, Agni and Soma, Mighty Ones whom many laud.  May these vouchsafe us shelter with a triple guard, these whom the strong have served in worship of the Gods.

10.66.d: धर्तव्रताः कषत्रिया यज्ञनिष्क्र्तो बर्हद्दिवा अध्वराणामभिश्रियः | अग्निहोतार रतसापो अद्रुहो.अपो अस्र्जन्ननुव्र्त्रतूर्ये ||
10.66.e: Potent, with firm-fixt laws, arranging sacrifice, visiting solemn rites in splendour of the day,  Obeying Order, these whose priest is Agni, free from falsehood, poured the waters out when Vṛtra died.

10.66.d: दयावाप्र्थिवी जनयन्नभि वरताप ओषधीर्वनिनानियज्ञिया | अन्तरिक्षं सवरा पप्रुरूतये वशं देवासस्तन्वी नि माम्र्जुः ||
10.66.e: The Holy Ones engendered, for their several laws, the heavens and earth, the waters, and the plants and trees.  They filled the firmament with heavenly light for help: the Gods embodied Wish and made it beautiful.

10.66.d: धर्तारो दिव रभवः सुहस्ता वातापर्जन्या महिषस्यतन्यतोः | आप ओषधीः पर तिरन्तु नो गिरो भगो रातिर्वाजिनो यन्तु मे हवम ||
10.66.e: May they who bear up heaven, the Ṛbhus deft of hand, and Vāta and Parjanya of the thundering Bull,  The waters and the plants, promote the songs we sing: come Bhaga, Rati, and the Vaijns to my call.

10.66.d: समुद्रः सिन्धू रजो अन्तरिक्षमज एकपात तनयित्नुरर्णवः | अहिर्बुध्न्यः शर्णवद वचांसि मे विश्वे देवासौत सूरयो मम ||
10.66.e: Sindhu, the sea, the region, and the firmament, the thunder, and the ocean, Aja-Ekapād,  The Dragon of the Deep, shall listen to my words, and all the Deities and Princes shall give ear.

10.66.d: सयाम वो मनवो देववीतये पराञ्चं नो यज्ञं पर णयतसाधुया | आदित्या रुद्रा वसवः सुदानव इमा बरह्मशस्यमानानि जिन्वत ||
10.66.e: May we, be yours, we men, to entertain the Gods: further our sacrifice and give it full success.  Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, givers of good gifts, quicken the holy hymns which we are singing now

10.66.d: दैव्या होतारा परथमा पुरोहित रतस्य पन्थामन्वेमिसाधुया | कषेत्रस्य पतिं परतिवेशमीमहे विश्वान देवानम्र्तानप्रयुछतः ||
10.66.e: I follow with success upon the path of Law the two celestial Hotars, Priests of oldest time.  We pray to him who dwelleth near, Guard of the Field, to all Immortal Gods who never are remiss.

10.66.d: वसिष्ठासः पित्र्वद वाचमक्रत देवानीळाना रषिवत्स्वस्तये | परीता इव जञातयः काममेत्यास्मे देवासो.अवधूनुता वसु ||
10.66.e: Vasiṣṭha's sons have raised their voices, like their sire. Ṛṣi-like praying to the Gods for happiness.  Like friendly-minded kinsmen, come at our desire, O Gods, and shake down treasures on us from above.
Immortal Gods have I, Vasiṣṭha, lauded, Gods set on high above all other beings.  May they this day grant us wide space and freedom: ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

10.67.d: इमां धियं सप्तशीर्ष्णीं पिता न रतप्रजातां बर्हतीमविन्दत | तुरीयं सविज्जनयद विश्वजन्यो.अयास्य उक्थमिन्द्राय शंसन ||
10.67.e: THIS holy hymn, sublime and sevenheaded, sprung from eternal Law, our sire discovered.  Ayasya, friend of all men, hath engendered the fourth hymn as he sang his laud to Indra.

10.67.d: रतं शंसन्त रजु दीध्याना दिवस पुत्रासो असुरस्यवीराः | विप्रं पदमङगिरसो दधाना यज्ञस्य धामप्रथमं मनन्त ||
10.67.e: Thinking aright, praising eternal Order, the sons of Dyaus the Asura, those heroes,  Aṅgirases, holding the rank of sages, first honoured sacrifice's holy statute.

10.67.d: हंसैरिव सखिभिर्वावदद्भिरश्मन्मयानि नहनाव्यस्यन | बर्हस्पतिरभिकनिक्रदद गा उत परास्तौदुच्चविद्वानगायत ||
10.67.e: Girt by his friends who cried with swanlike voices, bursting the stony barriers of the prison,  Bṛhaspati spake in thunder to the cattle, and uttered praise and song when he had found them.

10.67.d: अवो दवाभ्यां पर एकया गा गुहा तिष्ठन्तीरन्र्तस्यसेतौ | बर्हस्पतिस्तमसि जयोतिरिछन्नुदुस्रा आकर्विहि तिस्र आवः ||
10.67.e: Apart from one, away from two above him, he drave the kine that stood in bonds of falsehood.  Bṛhaspati, seeking light amid the darkness, drave forth the bright cows: three he made apparent.

10.67.d: विभिद्या पुरं शयाथेमपाचीं निस्त्रीणि साकमुदधेरक्र्न्तत | बर्हस्पतिरुषसं सूर्यं गामर्कंविवेद सतनयन्निव दयौः ||
10.67.e: When he had cleft the lairs and western castle, he cut off three from him who held the waters.  Bṛhaspati discovered, while he thundered like Dyaus, the dawn, the Sun, the cow, the lightning.

10.67.d: इन्द्रो वलं रक्षितारं दुघानां करेणेव वि चकर्तारवेण | सवेदाञ्जिभिराशिरमिछमानो.अरोदयत पणिमागा अमुष्णात ||
10.67.e: As with a hand, so with his roaring Indra cleft Vala through, the guardian of the cattle.  Seeking the milk-draught with sweatshining comrades he stole the Paṇi's kine and left him weeping.

10.67.d: स ईं सत्येभिः सखिभिः शुचद्भिर्गोधायसं विधनसैरदर्दः | बरह्मणस पतिर्व्र्षभिर्वराहैर्घर्मस्वेदेभिर्द्रविणं वयानट ||
10.67.e: He with bright faithful Friends, winners of booty, hath rent the milker of the cows asunder.  Bṛhaspati with wild boars strong and mighty, sweating with heat, hath gained a rich possession.

10.67.d: ते सत्येन मनसा गोपतिं गा इयानास इषणयन्तधीभिः | बर्हस्पतिर्मिथोवद्यपेभिरुदुस्रिया अस्र्जतस्वयुग्भिः ||
10.67.e: They, longing for the kine, with faithful spirit incited with their hymns the Lord of cattle.  Bṛhaspati freed the radiant cows with comrades self-yoked, averting shame from one another.

10.67.d: तं वर्धयन्तो मतिभिः शिवाभिः सिंअमिव नानदतंसधस्थे | बर्हस्पतिं वर्षणं शूरसातौ भरे-भरे अनुमदेम जिष्णुम ||
10.67.e: In our assembly with auspicious praises exalting him who roareth like a lion,  Maywe, in every fight where heroes conquer, rejoice in strong Bṛhaspati the Victor.

10.67.d: यदा वाजमसनद विश्वरूपमा दयामरुक्षदुत्तराणिसद्म | बर्हस्पतिं वर्षणं वर्धयन्तो नाना सन्तोबिभ्रतो जयोतिरासा ||
10.67.e: When he had won him every sort of booty and gone to heaven and its most lofty mansions,  Men praised Bṛhaspati the Mighty, bringing the light within their mouths from sundry places.

10.67.d: सत्यामाशिषं कर्णुता वयोधै कीरिं चिद धयवथस्वेभिरेवैः | पश्चा मर्धो अप भवन्तु विश्वास्तद्रोदसी शर्णुतं विश्वमिन्वे ||
10.67.e: Fulfil the prayer that begs for vital vigour: aid in your wonted manner even the humble.  Let all our foes be turned and driven backward. Hear this, O Heaven and Earth, ye All-producers.

10.67.d: इन्द्रो मह्ना महतो अर्णवस्य वि मूर्धानमभिनदर्बुदस्य | अहन्नहिमरिणात सप्त सिन्धून देवैर्द्यावाप्र्थिवीप्रावतं नः ||
10.67.e: Indra with mighty strength cleft asunder the head of Arbuda the watery monster,  Slain Ahi, and set free the Seven Rivers. O Heaven and Earth, with all the Gods protect us.

10.68.d: उदप्रुतो न वयो रक्षमाणा वावदतो अभ्रियस्येव घोषाः | गिरिभ्रजो नोर्मयो मदन्तो बर्हस्पतिमभ्यर्का अनावन ||
10.68.e: LIKE birds who keep their watch, plashing in water, like the loud voices of the thundering rain-cloud,  Like merry streamlets bursting from the mountain, thus to Bṛhaspati our hymns have sounded.

10.68.d: सं गोभिराङगिरसो नक्षमाणो भग इवेदर्यमणंनिनाय | जने मित्रो न दम्पती अनक्ति बर्हस्पतेवाजयाशून्रिवाजौ ||
10.68.e: The Son of Aṅgirases, meeting the cattle, as Bhaga, brought in Aryaman among us.  As Friend of men he decks the wife and husband: as for the race, Bṛhaspati, nerve our coursers.

10.68.d: साध्वर्या अतिथिनीरिषिरा सपार्हाः सुवर्णानवद्यरूपाः | बर्हस्पतिः पर्वते भयो वितूर्या निर्गाूपे यवमिव सथिविभ्यः ||
10.68.e: Bṛhaspati, having won them from the mountains, strewed down, like barley out of winnowing- baskets,  The vigorous, wandering cows who aid the pious, desired of all, of blameless form, well-coloured.

10.68.d: आप्रुषायन मधुन रतस्य योनिमवक्षिपन्नर्क उल्कामिवद्योः | बर्हस्पतिरुद्धरन्नश्मनो गा भूम्या उद्नेव वित्वचं बिभेद ||
10.68.e: As the Sun dews with meath the seat of Order, and casts a flaming meteor down from heaven.  So from the rock Bṛhaspati forced the cattle, and cleft the earth's skin as it were with water.

10.68.d: अप जयोतिषा तमो अन्तरिक्षादुद्नः शीपालमिव वाताजत | बर्हस्पतिरनुम्र्श्या वलस्याभ्रमिव वात आ चक्रा गाः ||
10.68.e: Forth from mid air with light he dravc the darkness, as the gale blows a lily from the fiver.  Like the wind grasping at the cloud of Vala, Bṛhaspati gathered to himself the cattle,

10.68.d: यदा वलस्य पीयतो जसुं भेद बर्हस्पतिरग्नितपोभिरर्कैः | दद्भिर्न जिह्वा परिविष्टमाददाविर्निधीन्रक्र्णोदुस्रियाणाम ||
10.68.e: Bṛhaspati, when he with fiery lightnings cleft through the weapon of reviling Vala,  Consumedḥim as tongues cat what teeth have compassed: he threw the prisons of the red cows open.

10.68.d: बर्हस्पतिरमत हि तयदासां नाम सवरीणां सदनेगुहा यत | आण्डेव भित्त्वा शकुनस्य गर्भमुदुस्रियाःपर्वतस्य तमनाजत ||
10.68.e: That secret name borne by the lowing cattle within the cave Bṛhaspati discovered,  And drave, himself, the bright kine from the mountain, like a bird's young after the egg's disclosure.

10.68.d: अश्नापिनद्धं मधु पर्यपश्यन मत्स्यं न दीन उदनिक्षियन्तम | निष टज्जभार चमसं न वर्क्षाद्ब्र्हस्पतिर्विरवेणा विक्र्त्य ||
10.68.e: He looked around on rock-imprisoned sweetness as one who eyes a fish in scanty water.  Bṛhaspati, cleaving through with varied clamour, brought it forth like a bowl from out the timber.

10.68.d: सोषामविन्दत स सवः सो अग्निं सो अर्केण वि बबाधेतमांसि | बर्हस्पतिर्गोवपुषो वलस्य निर्मज्जानं नपर्वणो जभार ||
10.68.e: He found the light of heaven, and fire, and Morning: with lucid rays he forced apart the darkness.  As from a joint, Bṛhaspati took the marrow of Vala as he gloried in his cattle.

10.68.d: हिमेव पर्णा मुषिता वनानि बर्हस्पतिनाक्र्पयद वलो गाः | अनानुक्र्त्यमपुनश्चकार यात सूर्यामासा मिथौच्चरातः ||
10.68.e: As trees for foliage robbed by winter, Vala mourned for the cows Bṛhaspati had taken.  He did a deed ne’er done, ne’er to be equalled, whereby the Sun and Moon ascend alternate.

10.68.d: अभि शयावं न कर्शनेभिरश्वं नक्षत्रेभिः पितरोद्यामपिंशन | रात्र्यां तमो अदधुर्ज्योतिरहन्ब्र्हस्पतिर्भिनदद्रिं विदद गाः ||
10.68.e: Like a dark steed adorned with pearl, the Fathers have decorated heaven With constellations.  They set the light in day, in night the darkness. Bṛhaspati cleft the rock and found the cattle.

10.68.d: इदमकर्म नमो अभ्रियाय यः पूर्वीरन्वानोनवीति | बर्हस्पतिः स हि गोभिः सो अश्वैः स वीरेभिः सन्र्भिर्नो वयो धात ||
10.68.e: This homage have we.offered to the Cloud God who thunders out to many in succession.  May this Bṛhaspati vouchsafe us fulness of life with kine and horses, men, and heroes.

10.69.d: भद्रा अग्नेर्वध्र्यश्वस्य सन्द्र्शो वामी परणीतिःसुरणा उपेतयः | यदीं सुमित्रा विशो अग्र इन्धतेघ्र्तेनाहुतो जरते दविद्युतत ||
10.69.e: Auspicious is the aspect of Vadhryasva's fire good is its guidance, pleasant are its visitings.  When first the people Of Sumitra kindle it, with butter poured thercon it crackles and shines bright.

10.69.d: घर्तमग्नेर्वध्र्यश्वस्य वर्धनं घर्तमन्नं घर्तं वस्य मेदनम | घर्तेनाहुत उर्विया वि पप्रथे सूर्य इवरोचते सर्पिरासुतिः ||
10.69.e: Butter is that which makes Vadhryaiva's fire growstrong: the butter is its food, the butter makes it fat.  It spreads abroad when butter hath been offered it, and balmed with streams of butter shines forth like the Sun.

10.69.d: यत ते मनुर्यदनीकं सुमित्रः समीधे अग्ने तदिदंनवीयः | स रेवच्छोच स गिरो जुषस्व स वाजं दर्षिस इह शरवो धाः ||
10.69.e: Still newest is this face of thine, O Agni, which Manu and Sumitra have enkindled.  So richly shine, accept our songs with favour, so give us strengthening food, so send us glory.

10.69.d: यं तवा पूर्वमीळितो वध्र्यश्वः समीधे अग्ने स इदंजुषस्व | स न सतिपा उत भवा तनूपा दात्रं रक्षस्वयदिदं ते अस्मे ||
10.69.e: Accept this offering, Agni, whom aforetime Vadhryasva, hath entreated and enkindled.  Guard well our homes and ople, guard our bodies, protect thy girt to us which thou hast granted.

10.69.d: भवा दयुम्नी वाध्र्यश्वोत गोपा मा तवा तारीदभिमातिर्जनानाम | शूर इव धर्ष्णुश्च्यवनः सुमित्रः पर नुवोचं वाध्र्यश्वस्य नाम ||
10.69.e: Be splendid, guard us Kinsman of Vadhryasva: let not the enmity of men o’ercome thee,  Like the bold hero Cyavāna, I Sumitra tell forth the title of Vadhryaiva's Kinsman.

10.69.d: समज्र्या पर्वत्या वसूनि दासा वर्त्राण्यार्या जिगेथ | शूर इव धर्ष्णुश्च्यवनो जनानां तवमग्ने पर्तनायून्रभि षयाः ||
10.69.e: All treasures hast thou won, of plains and mountains, and quelled the Dāsas' and Āryas' hatred.  Like the bold hero Cyavāna, O Agni, mayst thou subdue the men who long for battle.

10.69.d: दीर्घतन्तुर्ब्र्हदुक्षायमग्निः सहस्रस्तरीः शतनीथर्भ्वा | दयुमान दयुमत्सु नर्भिर्म्र्ज्यमानः सुमित्रेषु दीदयोदेवयत्सु ||
10.69.e: Deft Agni hath a lengthened thread, tall oxen, a thousand heifers, numberless devices.  Decked by the men, splendid among the splendid, shine brightly forth amid devout Sumitras.

10.69.d: तवे धेनुः सुदुघा जातवेदो.असश्चतेव समना सबर्धुक | तवं नर्भिर्दक्षिणावद्भिरग्ने सुमित्रेभिरिध्यसेदेवयद्भिः ||
10.69.e: Thine is the teeming cow, O Jātavedas, who pours at once her ceaseless flow, Sabardhuk,  Thou. art lit up by men enriched with guerdon, O Agni, by the pious-souled Sumitras.

10.69.d: देवाश्चित ते अम्र्ता जातवेदो महिमानं वाध्र्यश्व पर वोचन | यत सम्प्र्छं मानुषीर्विश आयन तवं नर्भिरजयस्त्वाव्र्धेभिः ||
10.69.e: Even Immortal Gods, O Jātavedas, Vadhryasva's Kinsman, have declared thy grandeur.  When human tribes drew near with supplication thou conqueredst with men whom thou hadst strengthened.

10.69.d: पितेव पुत्रमबिभरुपस्थे तवामग्ने वध्र्यश्वः सपर्यन्जुषाणो अस्य समिधं यविष्ठोत पूर्वानवनोर्व्राधतश्चित ||
10.69.e: Like as a father bears his son, O Agni, Vadhryasva bare thee in his lap and served thee.  Thou, Youngest God, having enjoyed his fuel, didst vanquish those of old though they were mighty.

10.69.d: शश्वदग्निर्वध्र्यश्वस्य शात्रून नर्भिर्जिगायसुतसोमवद्भिः | समनं चिददहश्चित्रभानो.अवव्राधन्तमभिनद वर्धश्चित ||
10.69.e: Vadhryasva's Agni evermore hath vanquished his foes with heroes who had pressed the Soma.  Lord of bright rays, thou burntest up the battle, subduing, as our help, e’en mighty foemen.

10.69.d: अयमग्निर्वध्र्यश्वस्य वर्त्रहा सनकात परेद्धोनमसोपवाक्यः | स नो अजामीन्रुत वा विजामीनभितिष्ठ शर्धतो वाध्र्यश्व ||
10.69.e: This Agni of Vadhryasva, Vṛtra-slayer, lit from of old, must be invoked with homage.  As such assail our enemies, Vadhryasva, whether the foes be strangers or be kinsmen.

10.70.d: इमां मे अग्ने समिधं जुषस्वेळस पदे परति हर्याघ्र्ताचीम | वर्ष्मन पर्थिव्याः सुदिनत्वे अह्नामूर्ध्वोभव सुक्रतो देवयज्या ||
10.70.e: ENJOY, O Agni, this my Fuel, welcome the oil-filled ladle where we pour libation.  Rise up for worship of the Gods, wise Agni, on the earth's height, while days are bright with beauty.

10.70.d: आ देवानामग्रयावेह यातु नराशंसो विश्वरूपेभिरश्वैः | रतस्य पथा नमसा मियेधो देवेभ्यो देवतमःसुषूदत ||
10.70.e: May he who goes before the Gods come hither with steeds whose shapes are varied, Narasarhsa.  May he, most Godlike, speed our offered viands with homage God-ward on the path of Order.

10.70.d: शश्वत्तममीळते दूत्याय हविष्मन्तो मनुष्यासो अग्निम | वहिष्ठैरश्वैः सुव्र्ता रथेना देवान वक्षि निषदेह होता ||
10.70.e: Men with oblations laud most constant Agni, and pray him to perform an envoy's duty.  With lightly-rolling car and best draught-horses, bring the Gods hither and sit down as Hotar.

10.70.d: वि परथतां देवजुष्टं तिरश्चा दीर्घं दराघ्मासुरभि भूत्वस्मे | अहेळता मनसा देव बर्हिरिन्द्रज्येष्ठानुशतो यक्षि देवान ||
10.70.e: May the delight of Gods spread out transversely: may it be with us long in length and fragrant.  O Holy Grass divine, with friendly spirit bring thou the willing Gods whose Chief is Indra.

10.70.d: दिवो वा सानु सप्र्शता वरीयः पर्थिव्या वा मात्रया विश्रयध्वम | उशतीर्द्वारो महिना महद्भिर्देवं रथंरथयुर्धारयध्वम ||
10.70.e: Touch ye the far-extending height of heaven or spring apart to suit the wide earth's measure.  Yearning, ye Doors, with those sublime in greatness, seize eagerly the heavenly Car that cometh.

10.70.d: देवी दिवो दुहितरा सुशिल्पे उषासानक्ता सदतां नियोनौ | आ वां देवास उशती उशन्त उरौ सीदन्तु सुभगेुपस्थे ||
10.70.e: Here in this shrine may Dawn and Night, the Daughters of Heaven, the skilful Goddesses, be seated.  In your wide lap, auspicious, willing Ladies may the Gods seat them with a willing spirit.

10.70.d: ऊर्ध्वो गरावा बर्हदग्निः समिद्धः परिया धामान्यदितेरुपस्थे | पुरोहिताव रत्विजा यज्ञे अस्मिन विदुष्टराद्रविणमा यजेथाम ||
10.70.e: Up stands the stone, high burns the fire enkindled: Aditi's lap contains the Friendly Natures  Ye Two Chief Priests who serve at this our worship, may ye, more skilled, win for us rich possessions.

10.70.d: तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरिदं वरीय आ सीदत चक्र्मा वःस्योनम | मनुष्वद यज्ञं सुधिता हवींषीळा देवीघ्र्तपदी जुषन्त ||
10.70.e: On our wide grass, Three Goddesses be seated: for you have we prepared and made it pleasant.  May Iḷā, she whose foot drops oil, the Goddess, taste, man-like, sacrifice and well-set presents.

10.70.d: देव तवष्टर्यद ध चारुत्वमानड यदङगिरसामभवः सचाभूः | स देवानां पाथ उप पर विद्वानुशन यक्षि दरविणोदः सुरत्नः ||
10.70.e: Since thou, God Tvaṣṭar, hast made beauty perfect, since hou hast been the Aṅgirases' Companion,  Willing, most wealthy, Giver of possessions, grant us the Gods’ assembly, thou who knowest.

10.70.d: वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षिविद्वान | सवदाति देवः कर्णवद धवींष्यवतान्द्यावाप्र्थिवी हवं मे ||
10.70.e: Well-knowing, binding with thy cord, bring hither, Lord of the Wood, the Deities' assembly.  The God prepare and season our oblations may Heaven and Earth be gracious to my calling.

10.70.d: आग्ने वह वरुणमिष्टये न इन्द्रं दिवो मरुतोन्तरिक्षात | सीदन्तु बर्हिर्विश्व आ यजत्राः सवाहादेवा अम्र्ता मादयन्ताम ||
10.70.e: Agni, bring hither Varuṇa to help us, Indra from heaven, from air's mid-realm the Maruts.  On sacred grass all Holy ones be seated and let the Immortal Gods rejoice in Svāhā.

10.71.d: बर्हस्पते परथमं वाचो अग्रं यत परैरत नामधेयन्दधानाः | यदेषां शरेष्ठं यदरिप्रमासीत्प्रेणा तदेषां निहितं गुहाविः ||
10.71.e: WHEN-men, Bṛhaspati, giving names to objects, sent out Vāk's first and earliest utterances,  All that was excellent and spotless, treasured within them, was disclosed through their affection.

10.71.d: सक्तुमिव-तित-उना पुनन्तो यत्र धीरा मनसा वाचमक्रत | अत्रा सखायः सख्यानि जानते भद्रैषांलक्ष्मीर्निहिताधि वाचि ||
10.71.e: Where, like men cleansing corn-flour in a cribble, the wise in spirit have created language,  Friends see and recognize the marks of friendship: their speech retains the blessed sign imprinted.

10.71.d: यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन तामन्वविन्दन्न्र्षिषुप्रविष्टाम | तामाभ्र्त्या वयदधुः पुरुत्रा तां सप्तरेभा अभि सं नवन्ते ||
10.71.e: With sacrifice the trace of Vāk they foIlowed, and found her harbouring within the Ṛṣis.  They brought her, dealt her forth in many places: seven singers make her tones resound in concert.

10.71.d: उत तवः पश्यन न ददर्श वाचमुत तवः शर्ण्वन नश्र्णोत्येनाम | उतो तवस्मै तन्वं वि सस्रे जायेव पत्यौशती सुवासाः ||
10.71.e: One man hath ne’er seen Vāk, and yet he seeth: one man hath hearing but hath never heard her.  But to another hath she shown her beauty as a fond well-dressed woman to her husband.

10.71.d: उत तवं सख्ये सथिरपीतमाहुर्नैनं हिन्वन्त्यपिवाजिनेषु | अधेन्वा चरति माययैष वाचं शुश्रुवानफलामपुष्पाम ||
10.71.e: One man they call a laggard, dull in friendship: they never urge him on to deeds of valour.  He wanders on in profitless illusion: the Voice he heard yields neither fruit,nor blossom.

10.71.d: यस्तित्याज सचिविदं सखायं न तस्य वाच्यपि भागोस्ति | यदीं शर्णोत्यलकं शर्णोति नहि परवेद सुक्र्तस्यपन्थाम ||
10.71.e: No part in Vāk hath he who hath abandoned his own dear friend who knows the truth of friendship.  Even if he hears her still in vain he listens: naught knows he of the path of righteous action.

10.71.d: अक्षण्वन्तः कर्णवन्तः सखायो मनोजवेष्वसमाबभूवुः | आदघ्नास उपकक्षास उ तवे हरदा इव सनात्वा उत्वे दद्र्श्रे ||
10.71.e: Unequal in the quickness of their spirit are friends endowed alike with eyes and hearing.  Some look like tanks that reach the mouth or shoulder, others like pools of water fit to bathe in.

10.71.d: हर्दा तष्टेषु मनसो जवेषु यद बराह्मणाः संयजन्तेसखायः | अत्राह तवं वि जहुर्वेद्याभिरोहब्रह्माणो विचरन्त्यु तवे ||
10.71.e: When friendly Brahmans sacrifice together with mental impulse which the heart hath fashioned,  They leave one far behind through their attainments, and some who count as Brahmans wander elsewhere.

10.71.d: इमे ये नार्वां न परश्चरन्ति न बराह्मणासो नसुतेकरासः | त एते वाचमभिपद्य पापया सिरीस्तन्त्रं तन्वते अप्रजज्ञयः ||
10.71.e: Those men who step not back and move not forward, nor Brahmans nor preparers of libations,  Having attained to Vāk in sinful fashion spin out their thread in ignorance like spinsters.

10.71.d: सर्वे नन्दन्ति यशसागतेन सभासाहेन सख्या सखायः | किल्बिषस्प्र्त पितुषणिर्ह्येषामरं हितो भवतिवाजिनाय ||
10.71.e: All friends are joyful in the friend who cometh in triumph, having conquered in assembly.  He is their blame-averter, food-provider prepared is he and fit for deed of vigour.

10.71.d: रचां तवः पोषमास्ते पुपुष्वान गायत्रं तवो गायतिशक्वरीषु | बरह्मा तवो वदति जातविद्यां यज्ञस्यमात्रां वि मिमीत उ तवः ||
10.71.e: One plies his constant task reciting verses. one sings the holy psalm in Sakvari measures.  One more, the Brahman, tells the lore of being, and one lays down the rules of sacrificing.

10.72.d: देवानां नु वयं जाना पर वोचाम विपन्यया | उक्थेषुशस्यमानेषु यः पश्यादुत्तरे युगे ||
10.72.e: LET US with tuneful skill proclaim these generations of the Gods,  That one may see them when these hymns are chanted in a future age.

10.72.d: बरह्मणस पतिरेता सं कर्मार इवाधमत | देवानाम्पूर्व्ये युगे.असतः सदजायत ||
10.72.e: These Brahmaṇaspati produced with blast and smelting, like a Smith,  Existence, in an earlier age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang.

10.72.d: देवानां युगे परथमे.असतः सदजायत | तदाशा अन्वजायन्त तदुत्तानपदस परि ||
10.72.e: Existence, in the earliest age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang.  Thereafter were the regions born. This sprang from the Productive Power.

10.72.d: भूर्जज्ञ उत्तानपदो भुव आशा अजायन्त | अदितेर्दक्षोजायत दक्षाद वदितिः परि ||
10.72.e: Earth sprang from the Productive Power the regions from the earth were born.  Dakṣa was born of Aditi, and Aditi was Dakṣa's Child.

10.72.d: अदितिर्ह्यजनिष्ट दक्ष या दुहिता तव | तां देवान्वजायन्त भद्रा अम्र्तबन्धवः ||
10.72.e: For Aditi, O Dakṣa, she who is thy Daughter, was brought forth.  After her were the blessed Gods born sharers of immortal life.

10.72.d: यद देवा अदः सलिले सुसंरब्धा अतिष्ठत | अत्रा वोन्र्त्यतामिव तीव्रो रेणुरपायत ||
10.72.e: When ye, O Gods, in yonder deep closeclasping one another stood,  Thence, as of dancers, from your feet a thickening cloud of dust arose.

10.72.d: यद देवा यतयो यथा भुवनान्यपिन्वत | अत्रा समुद्रा गूळमा सूर्यमजभर्तन ||
10.72.e: When, O ye Gods, like Yatis, ye caused all existing things to grow,  Then ye brought Sūrya forward who was lying hidden in the sea.

10.72.d: अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्वस परि | देवानुपप्रैत सप्तभिः परा मार्ताण्डमास्यत ||
10.72.e: Eight are the Sons of Adid who from her body sprang to life.  With seven she went to meet the Gods she cast Martanda far away.

10.72.d: सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुप परैत पूर्व्यं युगम | परजायै मर्त्यवे तवत पुनर्मार्ताण्डमाभरत ||
10.72.e: So with her Seven Sons Aditi went forth to meet the earlier age.  She brought Martanda thitherward to spring to life and die again.

10.73.d: जनिष्था उग्रः सहसे तुराय मन्द्र ओजिष्ठोबहुलाभिमानः | अवर्धन्निन्द्रं मरुतश्चिदत्र मातायद वीरं दधनद धनिष्ठा ||
10.73.e: THOU wast born mighty for victorious valour, exulting, strongest, full of pride and courage.  There, even there, the Maruts strengthened Indra when. his most rapid Mother stirred the Hero.

10.73.d: दरुहो निषत्ता पर्शनी चिदेवैः पुरू शंसेन वाव्र्धुष्ट इन्द्रम | अभीव्र्तेव ता महापदेन धवान्तात परपित्वादुदरन्त गर्भाः ||
10.73.e: There with fiend's ways e’en Pṛśni was seated: with much laudation they exalted Indra.  As if encompassed by the Mighty-footed, from darkness, near at hand, forth came the Children.

10.73.d: रष्वा ते पादा पर यज्जिगास्यवर्धन वाजा उत ये चिदत्र | तवमिन्द्र सालाव्र्कान सहस्रमासन दधिषे अश्विनावव्र्त्याः ||
10.73.e: High are thy feet when on thy way thou goest: the strength thou foundest here hath lent thee vigour.  Thousand hyenas in thy mouth thou holdest. O Indra, mayst thou turn the Aśvins hither.

10.73.d: समना तूर्णिरुप यासि यज्ञमा नासत्या सख्यायवक्षि | वसाव्यामिन्द्र धारयः सहस्राश्विना शूर ददतुर्मघानि ||
10.73.e: Speeding at once to sacrifice thou comest for friendship thou art bringing both Nāsatyas.  Thou hadst a thousand treasures in possession. The Aśvins, O thou Hero, gave thee riches.

10.73.d: मन्दमान रतादधि परजायै सखिभिरिन्द्र इषिरेभिरर्थम | आभिर्हि माया उप दस्युमागान मिहः परतम्रा अवपत तमांसि ||
10.73.e: Glad, for the race that rests on holy Order, with friends who hasten to their goal, hath Indra  With these his magic powers assailed the Dasyu: he cast away the gloomy mists, the darkness.

10.73.d: सनामाना चिद धवसयो नयस्मा अवाहन्निन्द्र उषसोयथानः रष्वैरगछः सखिभिर्निकामैः साकम्प्रतिष्ठा हर्द्या जघन्थ ||
10.73.e: Two of like name for him didst thou demolish, as Indra striking down the car of Uṣas.  With thy beloved lofty Friends thou camest, and with the assurance of thine heart thou slewest.

10.73.d: तवं जघन्थ नमुचिं मखस्युं दासं कर्ण्वान रषयेविमायम | तवं चकर्थ मनवे सयोनान पथो देवत्राञ्जसेवयानान ||
10.73.e: War-loving Namuci thou smotest, robbing the Dāsa of his magic for the Ṛṣi.  For man thou madest ready pleasant pathways, paths leading as it were directly God-ward.

10.73.d: तवमेतानि पप्रिषे वि नामेशान इन्द्र दधिषे गभस्तौ | अनु तवा देवाः शवसा मदन्त्युपरिबुध्नान वनिनश्चकर्थ ||
10.73.e: These names of thine thou hast fulfilled completely: as Lord, thou boldest in thine arm, O Indra.  In thee, through thy great might, the Gods are joyful: the roots of trees hast thou directed upward.

10.73.d: चक्रं यदस्याप्स्वा निषत्तमुतो तदस्मै मध्विच्चछद्यात | पर्थिव्यामतिषितं यदूधः पयो गोष्वदधा ओषधीषु ||
10.73.e: May the sweet Soma juices make him happy to cast his quoit that lies in depth of waters.  Thou from the udder which o’er earth is fastened hast poured the milk into the kine and herbage.

10.73.d: अश्वादियायेति यद वदन्त्योजसो जातमुत मन्य एनम | मन्योरियाय हर्म्येषु तस्थौ यतः परजज्ञ इन्द्रो अस्य वेद ||
10.73.e: When others call him offspring of the Courser, my meaning is that Mighty Power produced him.  He came from Manyu and remained in houses: whence he hath sprung is known to Indra only.

10.73.d: वयः सुपर्णा उप सेदुरिन्द्रं परियमेधा रषयोनाधमानाः | अप धवान्तमूर्णुहि पूर्धि चक्षुर्मुमुग्ध्यस्मान निधयेव बद्धान ||
10.73.e: Like birds of beauteous wing the Priyamedhas, Ṛṣis, imploring, have come nigh to Indra:  Dispel the darkness and fill full our vision deliver us as men whom snares entangle.

10.74.d: वसूनां वा चर्क्र्ष इयक्षन धिया वा यज्ञैर्वारोदस्योः | अर्वन्तो वा ये रयिमन्तः सातौ वनुं वा येसुश्रुणं सुश्रुतो धुः ||
10.74.e: I AM prepared to laud with song or worship the Noble Ones who are in earth and heaven,  Or Coursers who have triumphed in, the contest, or those who famed, have won the prize with glory.

10.74.d: हव एषामसुरो नक्षत दयां शरवस्यता मनसा निंसतक्षा | चक्षाणा यत्र सुविताय देवा दयौर्न वारेभिःक्र्णवन्त सवैः ||
10.74.e: Their call, the call of Gods, went up to heaven: they kissed the ground with glory-seeking spirit,  There where the Gods look on for happy fortune, and like the kindly heavens bestow their bounties.

10.74.d: इयमेषामम्र्तानां गीः सर्वताता ये कर्पणन्त रत्नम | धियं च यज्ञं च साधन्तस्ते नो धान्तु वसव्यमसामि ||
10.74.e: This is the song of those Immortal Beings who long for treasures in their full perfection.  May these, completing prayers and sacrifices, bestow upon us wealth where naught is wanting.

10.74.d: आ तत त इन्द्रायवः पनन्तभि य ऊर्वं गोमन्तन्तित्र्त्सान | सक्र्त्स्वं ये पुरुपुत्रां महीं सहस्रधाराम्ब्र्हतीं दुदुक्षन ||
10.74.e: Those living men extolled thy deed, O Indra, those who would fain burst through the stall of cattle,  Fain to milk her who bare but once, great, lofty, whose Sons are many and her streams past number.

10.74.d: शचीव इन्द्रमवसे कर्णुध्वमनानतं दमयन्तं पर्तन्यून | रभुक्षणं मघवानं सुव्र्क्तिं भर्ता यो वज्रं नर्यम्पुरुक्षुः ||
10.74.e: Sacivan, win to your assistance Indra who never bends, who overcomes his foemen.  Ṛbhukṣan, Maghavan, the hymn's upholder, who, rich in food, bears man's kind friend, the thunder.

10.74.d: यद वावान पुरुतमं पुराषाळ आ वर्त्रहेन्द्रो नामान्यप्राः | अचेति परासहस पतिस्तुविष्मान यदीमुश्मसिकर्तवे करत तत ||
10.74.e: Since he who won of old anew hath triumphed, Indra hath earned his name of Vṛtra-slaycr.  He hath appeared, the mighty Lord of Conquest. What we would have him do let him accomplish.

10.75.d: पर सु व आपो महिमानमुत्तमं कारुर्वोचाति सदनेविवस्वतः | पर सप्त-सप्त तरेधा हि चक्रमुः परस्र्त्वरीणामति सिन्धुरोजसा ||
10.75.e: THE singer, O ye Waters in Vivasvān's place, shall tell your grandeur forth that is beyond compare.  The Rivers have come forward triply, seven and seven. Sindhu in might surpasses all the streams that flow.

10.75.d: पर ते.अरदद वरुणो यातवे पथः सिन्धो यद वाजानभ्यद्रवस्त्वम | भूम्या अधि परवता यासि सानुना यदेषामग्रं जगतामिरज्यसि ||
10.75.e: Varuṇa cut the channels for thy forward course, O Sindhu, when thou rannest on to win the race.  Thou speedest o’er precipitous ridges of the earth, when thou art Lord and Leader of these moving floods.

10.75.d: दिवि सवनो यतते भूम्योपर्यनन्तं शुष्ममुदियर्तिभानुना | अभ्रादिव पर सतनयन्ति वर्ष्टयः सिन्धुर्यदेति वर्षभो न रोरुवत ||
10.75.e: His roar is lifted up to heaven above the earth: he puts forth endless vigour with a flash of light.  Like floods of rain that fall in thunder from the cloud, so Sindhu rushes on bellowing like a bull.

10.75.d: अभि तवा सिन्धो शिशुमिन न मातरो वाश्रा अर्षन्तिपयसेव धेनवः | राजेव युध्वा नयसि तवमित सिचौ यदासामग्रं परवतामिनक्षसि ||
10.75.e: Like mothers to their calves, like milch kine with their milk, so, Sindhu, unto thee the roaring rivers run.  Thou leadest as a warrior king thine army's wings what time thou comest in the van of these swift streams.

10.75.d: इमं मे गङगे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि सतेमं सचता परुष्ण्या | असिक्न्या मरुद्व्र्धे वितस्तयार्जीकीये शर्णुह्यासुषोमया ||
10.75.e: Favour ye this my laud, O Gan!gā, Yamunā, O Sutudri, Paruṣṇī and Sarasvatī:  With Asikni, Vitasta, O Marudvrdha, O Ārjīkīya with Susoma hear my call.

10.75.d: तर्ष्टामया परथमं यातवे सजूः ससर्त्वा रसयाश्वेत्या तया | तवं सिन्धो कुभया गोमतीं करुमुम्मेहत्न्वा सरथं याभिरीयसे ||
10.75.e: First with Trstama thou art eager to flow forth, with Rasā, and Susartu, and with Svetya here,  With Kubha; and with these, Sindhu and Mehatnu, thou seekest in thy course Krumu and Gomati.

10.75.d: रजीत्येनी रुशती महित्वा परि जरयांसि भरते रजांसि | अदब्धा सिन्धुरपसामपस्तमाश्वा न चित्रावपुषीव दर्शता ||
10.75.e: Flashing and whitely-gleaming in her mightiness, she moves along her ample volumes through the realms,  Most active of the active, Sindhu unrestrained, like to a dappled mare, beautiful, fair to see.

10.75.d: सवश्वा सिन्धुः सुरथा सुवासा हिरण्ययी सुक्र्तावाजिनीवती | ऊर्णावती युवतिः सीलमावत्युताधि वस्तेसुभगा मधुव्र्धम ||
10.75.e: Rich in good steeds is Sindhu, rich in cars and robes, rich in gold, nobly-fashioned, rich in ample wealth.  Blest Silamavati and young Urnavati invest themselves with raiment rich in store of sweets.

10.75.d: सुखं रथं युयुजे सिधुरश्विनं तेन वाजं सनिषदस्मिन्नाजौ | महान हयस्य महिमा पनस्यते.अदब्धस्यस्वयशसो विरप्शिनः ||
10.75.e: Sindhu hath yoked her car, light-rolling, drawn by steeds, and with that car shall she win booty in this fight.  So have I praised its power, mighty and unrestrained, of independent glory, roaring as it runs.

10.76.d: आ व रञ्जस ऊर्जां वयुष्टिष्विन्द्रं मरुतो रोदसीनक्तन | उभे यथा नो अहनी सचाभुवा सदः-सदोवरिवस्यात उद्भिदा ||
10.76.e: I GRASP at you when power and strength begin to dawn: bedew ye, Indra and the Maruts, Heaven and Earth,  That Day and Night, in every hall of sacrifice, may wait on us and bless us when they first spring forth.

10.76.d: तदु शरेष्ठं सवनं सुनोतनातयो न हस्तयतो अद्रिःसोतरि | विदद धयर्यो अभिभूति पौंस्यं महो राये चित्तरुते यदर्वतः ||
10.76.e: Press the libation out, most excellent of all: the Pressing-stone is grasped like a hand-guided steed.  So let it win the valour that subdues the foe, and the fleet courser's might that speeds to ample wealth.

10.76.d: तदिद धयस्य सवनं विवेरपो यथा पुरा मनवेगातुमश्रेत | गोर्णसि तवाष्ट्रे अश्वनिर्णिजि परेमध्वरेष्वध्वरानशिश्रयुः ||
10.76.e: Juice that this Stone pours out removes defect of ours, as in old time it brought prosperity to man.  At sacrifices they established holy rites on Tvaṣṭar's milk-blent juice bright with the hue of steeds.

10.76.d: अप हत रक्षसो भङगुरावत सकभायत निरतिंसेधतामतिम | आ नो रयिं सर्ववीरं सुनोतन देवाव्यम्भरत शलोकमद्रयः ||
10.76.e: Drive ye the treacherous demons far away from us: keep Nirrti afar and banish Penury.  Pour riches forth for us with troops of hero sons, and bear ye up, O Stones, the song that visits Gods.

To you who are more mighty than the heavens themselves, who, finishing your task with more than Vibhvan's speed,  More rapidly than Vāyu seize the Soma juice, better than Agni give us food, to you I sing.

10.76.d: भुरन्तु नो यशसः सोत्वन्धसो गरावाणो वाचा दिवितादिवित्मता | नरो यत्र दुहते काम्यं मध्वाघोषयन्तोभितो मिथस्तुरः ||
10.76.e: Stirred be the glorious Stones: let it press out the juice, the Stone with heavenly song that reaches up to heaven,  There where the men draw forth the meath for which they long, sending their voice around in rivalry of speed.

10.76.d: सुन्वन्ति सोमं रथिरासो अद्रयो निरस्य रसं गविषोदुहन्ति ते | दुहन्त्यूधरुपसेचनाय कं नरो हव्य नामर्जयन्त आसभिः ||
10.76.e: The Stones press out the Soma, swift as car-borne men, and, eager for the spoil, drain forth the sap thereof  To fill the beaker, they exhaust the udder's store, as the men purify oblations with their lips.

10.76.d: एते नरः सवपसो अभूतन य इन्द्राय सुनुथ सोममद्रयः | वामं-वामं वो दिव्याय धाम्ने वसु-वसु वः पार्थिवयसुन्वते ||
10.76.e: Ye, present men, have been most skilful in your work, even ye, O Stones who pressed Soma for Indra's drink.  May all ye have of fair go to the Heavenly Race, and all your treasure to the earthly worshipper.

10.77.d: अभ्रप्रुषो न वाचा परुषा वसु हविष्मन्तो न यज्ञाविजानुषः | सुमारुतं न बरह्माणमर्हसे गणमस्तोष्येषां न शोभसे ||
10.77.e: As with their voice from cloud they sprinkle treasure so are the wise man's liberal sacrifices.  I praise their Company that merits worship as the good Martits' priest to pay them honour.

10.77.d: शरिये मर्यासो अञ्जीन्रक्र्ण्वत सुमरुतं न पूर्विरतिक्षपः | दिवस पुत्रास एता न येतिर आदित्यासस्ते अक्रन वाव्र्धुः ||
10.77.e: The youths have wrought their ornaments for glory through many nights,—this noble band of Maruts.  Like stags the Sons of Dyatis have striven onward, the Sons of Aditi grown strong like pillars.

10.77.d: पर ये दिवः पर्थिव्य न बर्हणा तमना रिरिच्रे अभ्रान्न सूर्यः | पाजस्वन्तो न वीराः पनस्यवो रिशादसो नमर्या अभिद्यवः ||
10.77.e: They who extend beyond the earth and heaven, by their own mass, as from the cloud spreads Sūrya;  Like mighty Heroes covetous of glory, like heavenly gallants who destroy the wicked.

10.77.d: युष्माकं बुध्ने अपां न यामनि विथुर्यति न महीश्रथर्यति | विश्वप्सुर्यज्ञो अर्वागयं सु वःप्रयस्वन्तो न सत्राच आ गत ||
10.77.e: When ye come nigh, as in the depth of waters, the earth is loosened, as it were, and shaken.  This your all-feedin sacrifice approaches: come all united, fraught, as ’twere with viands.

10.77.d: यूयं धूर्षु परयुजो न रश्मिभिर्ज्योतिष्मन्तो न भासाव्युष्टिषु | शयेनासो न सवयशसो रिशादसः परवासोन परसितासः परिप्रुषः ||
10.77.e: Ye are like horses fastened to the chariot poles, luminous with your beams, with splendour as at dawn;  Like self-bright falcons, punishers of wicked men, like hovering birds urged forward, scattering rain around.

10.77.d: पर यद वहध्वे मरुतः पराकाद यूयं महःसंवरणस्य वस्वः | विदानासो वसवो राध्यस्याराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोत ||
10.77.e: When ye come forth, O Maruts, from the distance, from the great treasury of rich possessions,  Knowing, O Vasus, boons that should be granted, even from afar drive back the men who hate us.

10.77.d: य उद्र्चि यज्ञे अध्वरेष्ठा मरुद्भ्यो न मानुषो ददाशत | रेवत स वयो दधते सुवीरं स देवानामपि गोपीथेस्तु ||
10.77.e: He who, engaged in the rite's final duty brings, as a man, oblation to the Maruts,  Wins him life's wealthy fulness, blest with heroes: he shall be present, too, where Gods drink Soma.

10.77.d: ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमा आदित्येन नाम्नाशम्भविष्ठाः | ते नो.अवन्तु रथतूर्मनीषां महश्चयामन्नध्वरे चकानाः ||
10.77.e: For these are helps adored at sacrifices, bringing good fortune by their name Ādityas.  Speeding on cars let them protect our praises, delighting in our sacrifice and worship.

10.78.d: विप्रासो न मन्मभिः सवाध्यो देवाव्यो न यज्ञैःस्वप्नसः | राजानो न चित्राः सुसन्द्र्शः कषितीनां नमर्या अरेपसः ||
10.78.e: Ye by your hymns are like high-thoughted singers, skilful, inviting Gods with sacrifices;  Fair to behold, like Kings, with bright adornment, like spotless gallants, leaders of the people:

10.78.d: अग्निर्न ये भाजसा रुक्मवक्षसो वातासो न सवयुजःसद्यूतयः | परज्ञातारो न जयेष्ठाः सुनीतयःसुशर्माणो न सोमा रतं यते ||
10.78.e: Like fire with flashing flame, breast-bound with chains of gold, like tempest-blasts, self-moving, swift to lend your aid;  As best of all foreknowers, excellent to guide, like Somas, good to guard the man who follows Law.

10.78.d: वातासो न ये धुनयो जिगत्नवो.अग्नीनां न जिह्वाविरोकिणः | वर्मण्वन्तो न योधाः शिमीवन्तः पितॄणांन शंसाः सुरातयः ||
10.78.e: Shakers of all, like gales of wind they travel, like tongues of burning fires in their effulgence.  Mighty are they as warriors clad in armour, and, like the Fathers' prayers, Most Bounteous Givers.

10.78.d: रथानां न ये.अराः सनाभयो जिगीवांसो न शूराभिद्यवः | वरेयवो न मर्या घर्तप्रुषो.अभिस्वर्तारोर्कं न सुष्टुभः ||
10.78.e: Like spokes of car-wheels in one nave united, ever victorious like heavenly Heroes,  Shedding their precious balm like youthful suitors, they raise their voice and chant their psalm as singers.

10.78.d: अश्वासो न ये जयेष्ठास आशवो दिधिषवो न रथ्यःसुदानवः | आपो न निम्नैरुदभिर्जिगत्नवो विश्वरूपाङगिरसो न सामभिः ||
10.78.e: They who are fleet to travel like the noblest steeds, long to obtain the prize like bounteous charioteers,  Like waters speeding on with their precipitous floods, like omniform Aṅgirases with Sāma-hymns.

10.78.d: गरावाणो न सूरयः सिन्धुमातर आदर्दिरासो अद्रयो नविश्वहा | शिशूला न करीळयः सुमातरो महाग्रामो नयामन्नुत तविषा ||
10.78.e: Born from the stream, like press-stones are the Princes, for ever like the stones that crush in pieces;  Sons of a beauteous Dame, like playful children, like a great host upon the march with splendour.

10.78.d: उषसां न केतवो.अध्वरश्रियः शुभंयवो नाञ्जिभिर्व्यश्वितन | सिन्धवो न ययियो भराजद्र्ष्टयः परावतो नयोजनानि ममिरे ||
10.78.e: Like rays of Dawn, the visitors of sacrifice, they shine with ornaments as eager to be bright.  Like rivers hasting on, glittering with their spears, from far away they measure out the distances.

10.78.d: सुभागान नो देवाः कर्णुता सुरत्नानस्मान सतोतॄन मरुतोवाव्र्धानाः | अधि सतोत्रस्य सख्यस्य गात सनाद धि वोरत्नधेयानि सन्ति ||
10.78.e: Gods, send us happiness and make us wealthy, letting us singers prosper, O ye Maruts.  Bethink you of our praise and of our friendship: ye from of old have riches to vouchsafe us.

10.79.d: अपश्यमस्य महतो महित्वममर्त्यस्य मर्त्यासु विक्षु | नाना हनू विभ्र्ते सं भरेते असिन्वती बप्सती भूर्यत्तः ||
10.79.e: I HAVE beheld the might of this Great Being. Immortal in the midst of tribes of mortals.  His jaws now open and now shut together: much they devour, insatiately chewing.

10.79.d: गुहा शिरो निहितं रधगक्षी असिन्वन्नत्ति जिह्वयावनानि | अत्राण्यस्मै पड्भिः सं भरन्त्युत्तानहस्तानमसाधि विक्षु ||
10.79.e: His eyes are turned away, his head is hidden: unsated with his tongue he eats the fuel.  With hands upraised, with reverence in the houses, for him they quickly bring his food together.

10.79.d: पर मातुः परतरं गुह्यमिछन कुमारो न वीरुधःसर्पदुर्वीः | ससं न पक्वमविदच्छुचन्तंरिरिह्वांसं रिप उपस्थे अन्तः ||
10.79.e: Seeking, as ’twere, his Mother's secret bosom, he, like a child, creeps on through wide-spread bushes.  One he finds glowing like hot food made ready, and kissing deep within the earth's recmes.

10.79.d: तद वां रतं रोदसी पर बरवीमि जायमानो मातरा गर्भोत्ति | नाहं देवस्य मर्त्यश्चिकेताग्निरङग विचेताः सप्रचेताः ||
10.79.e: This holy Law I tell you, Earth and Heaven: the Infant at his birth dovours his Parents.  No knowledge of the God have I, a mortal. Yea, Agni knoweth best, for he hath wisdom.

10.79.d: यो अस्मा अन्नं तर्ष्वादधात्याज्यैर्घ्र्तैर्जुहोतिपुष्यति | तस्मै सहस्रमक्षभिर्वि चक्षे.अग्ने विश्वतःप्रत्यंं असि तवम ||
10.79.e: This man who quickly gives him food, who offers his gifts of oil and butter and supports him, -  Him with his thousand eyes he closely looks on: thou showest him thy face from all sides, Agni.

10.79.d: किं देवेषु तयज एनश्चकर्थाग्ने पर्छामि नु तवामविद्वान | अक्रीळन करीळन हरिरत्तवे.अदन वि पर्वशश्चकर्त गामिवासिः ||
10.79.e: Agni, hast thou committed sin or treason among the Gods? In ignorance I ask thee.  Playing, not playing, he gold-hued and toothless, hath cut his food up as the knife a victim.

10.79.d: विषूचो अश्वान युयुजे वनेजा रजीतिभी रशनाभिर्ग्र्भीतान | चक्षदे मित्रो वसुभिः सुजातः समान्र्धेपर्वभिर्वाव्र्धानः ||
10.79.e: He born in wood hath yoked his horses rushing in all directions, held with reins that glitter.  The well-born friend hath carved his food with Vasus: in all his limbs he hath increased and prospered.

10.80.d: अग्निः सप्तिं वाजम्भरं ददात्यग्निर्वीरं शरुत्यंकर्मनिष्ठाम | अग्नी रोदसी वि चरत समञ्जन्नग्निर्नारीं वीरकुक्षिं पुरन्धिम ||
10.80.e: AGNI bestows the fleet prize-winning courser: Agni, the hero famed and firm in duty.  Agni pervades and decks the earth and heaven, and fills the fruitful dame who teems with heroes.

10.80.d: अग्नेरप्नसः समिदस्तु भद्राग्निर्मही रोदसी आ विवेश | अग्निरेकं चोदयत समत्स्वग्निर्व्र्त्राणि दयते पुरूणि ||
10.80.e: Blest be the wood that feeds the active Agni: within the two great worlds hath Agni entered.  Agni impels a single man to battle, and with him rends in pieces many a foeman.

10.80.d: अग्निर्ह तयं जरतः कर्णमावाग्निरद्भ्यो निरदहज्जरूथम | अग्निरत्रिं घर्म उरुष्यदन्तरग्निर्न्र्मेधम्प्र जयास्र्जत सम ||
10.80.e: Agni rejoiced the car of him who praised lim, and from the waters burnt away jarutha.  Agni saved Atri in the fiery cavem, and made Nrmedha rich with troops of children.

10.80.d: अग्निर्दाद दरविणं वीरपेशा अग्निरषिं यः सहस्रासनोति | अग्निर्दिवि हव्यमा ततानाग्नेर्धामानिविभ्र्ता पुरुत्रा ||
10.80.e: Agni hath granted wealth that decks the hero, and sent the sage who wins a thousand cattle.  Agni hath made oblations rise to heaven: to every place are Agni's laws extended.

10.80.d: अग्निमुक्थैरषयो वि हवयन्ते.अग्निं नरो यामनिबाधितासः | अग्निं वयो अन्तरिक्षे पतन्तो.अग्निः सहस्रापरि याति गोनाम ||
10.80.e: With songs of praise the Ṛṣis call on Agni; on Agni, heroes worsted in the foray.  Birds flying in the region call on Agni around a thousand cattle Agni wanders.

10.80.d: अग्निं विश ईळते मानुषीर्या अग्निं मनुषो नहुषो विजाताः | अग्निर्गान्धर्वीं पथ्यां रतस्याग्नेर्गव्यूतिर्घ्र्त आ निषत्ता ||
10.80.e: Races of human birth pay Agni worship, men who have sprung from Nahus' line adore him.  Stablished in holy oil is Agni's pasture, on the Gandharva path of Law and Order.

10.80.d: अग्नये बरह्म रभवस्ततक्षुरग्निं महामवोचामा सुव्र्क्तिम | अग्ने पराव जरितारं यविष्ठाग्ने महि दरविणमायजस्व ||
10.80.e: The Ṛbhus fabricated prayer for Agni, and we with mighty hymns have called on Agni.  Agni, Most Youthful God, protect the singer: win us by worship, Agni, great possessions.

10.81.d: य इमा विश्वा भुवनानि जुह्वद रषिर्होता नयसीदत्पिता नः | स आशिषा दरविणमिछमानः परथमछदवराना विवेश ||
10.81.e: HE who sate down as Hotar-priest, the Ṛṣi, our Father, offering up all things existing,—  He, seeking through his wish a great possession, came among men on earth as archetypal.

10.81.d: किं सविदासीदधिष्ठनमारम्भणं कतमत सवित्कथासीत | यतो भूमिं जनयन विश्वकर्म वि दयामौर्णोन महिना विश्वचक्षाः ||
10.81.e: What was the place whereon he took his station? What was it that supported him? How was it?  Whence Visvakarman, seeing all, producing the earth, with mighty power disclosed the heavens.

10.81.d: विश्वतश्चक्षुरुत विश्वतोमुखो विश्वतोबाहुरुतविश्वतस्पात | सं बाहुभ्यां धमति सं पतत्रैर्द्यावाभूमी जनयन देव एकः ||
10.81.e: He who hath eyes on all sides round about him, a mouth on all sides, arms and feet on all sides,  He, the Sole God, producing earth and heaven, weldeth them, with his arms as wings, together.

10.81.d: किं सविद वनं क उ स वर्क्ष आस यतो दयावाप्र्थिवीनिष्टतक्षुः | मनीषिणो मनसा पर्छतेदु तद यदध्यतिष्ठद भुवनानि धारयन ||
10.81.e: What was the tree, what wood in sooth produced it, from which they fashioned out the earth and heaven?  Ye thoughtful men inquire within your spirit whereon he stood when he established all things.

10.81.d: या ते धामानि परमाणि यावमा या मध्यमाविश्वकर्मन्नुतेमा | शिक्षा सखिभ्यो हविषि सवधावःस्वयं यजस्व तन्वं वर्धानः ||
10.81.e: Nine highest, lowest, sacrificial natures, and these thy mid-most here, O Visvakarman,  Teach thou thy friends at sacrifice, O Blessed, and come thyself, exalted, to our worship.

10.81.d: विश्वकर्मन हविषा वाव्र्धानः सवयं यजस्व पर्थिवीमुत दयाम | मुह्यन्त्वन्ये अभितो जनास इहास्माकं मघवासूरिरस्तु ||
10.81.e: Bring thou thyself, exalted with oblation, O Visvakarman, Earth and Heaven to worship.  Let other men around us live in folly here let us have a rich and liberal patron.

10.81.d: वाचस पतिं विश्वकर्माणमूतये मनोजुवं वाजे अद्याहुवेम | स नो विश्वानि हवनानि जोषद विश्वशम्भूरवसेसाधुकर्मा ||
10.81.e: Let us invoke to-day, to aid our labour, the Lord of Speech, the thought-swift Visvakarman.  May he hear kindly all our invocations who gives all bliss for aid, whose works are righteous.

10.82.d: चक्षुषः पिता मनसा हि धीरो घर्तमेने अजनन्नन्नमाने | यदेदन्ता अदद्र्हन्त पूर्व आदिद्द्यावाप्र्थिवी अप्रथेताम ||
10.82.e: THE Father of the eye, the Wise in spirit, created both these worlds submerged in fatness.  Then when the eastern ends were firmly fastened, the heavens and the earth were far extended.

10.82.d: विश्वकर्मा विमना आद विहाया धाता विधाता परमोतसन्द्र्क | तेषामिष्टानि समिषा मदन्ति यत्रासप्तर्षीन पर एकमाहुः ||
10.82.e: Mighty in mind and power is Visvakarman, Maker, Disposer, and most lofty Presence.  Their offerings joy in rich juice where they value One, only One, beyond the Seven Ṛṣis.

10.82.d: यो नः पिता जनिता यो विधाता धामानि वेद भुवनानिविश्वा | यो देवानां नामधा एक एव तं सम्प्रश्नम्भुवना यन्त्यन्या ||
10.82.e: Father who made us, he who, as Disposer, knoweth all races and all things existing,  Even he alone, the Deities' narne-giver,him other beings seek for information.

10.82.d: त आयजन्त दरविणं समस्मा रषयः पूर्वे जरितारो नभूना | असूर्ते सूर्ते रजसि निषत्ते ये भूतानिसमक्र्ण्वन्निमानि ||
10.82.e: To him in sacrifice they offered treasures,—Ṛṣis of old, in numerous troops, as singers,  Who, in the distant, near, and lower region, made ready all these things that have existence.

10.82.d: परो दिवा पर एना पर्थिव्या परो देवेभिरसुरैर्यदस्ति | कं सविद गर्भं परथमं दध्र आपो यत्र देवाःसमपश्यन्त विश्वे ||
10.82.e: That which is earlier than this earth and heaven, before the Asuras and Gods had being,—  What was the germ primeval which the waters received where all the Gods were seen together?

10.82.d: तमिद गर्भं परथमं दध्र आपो यत्र देवाःसमगछन्त विश्वे | अजस्य नाभावध्येकमर्पितंयस्मिन विश्वानि भुवनानि तस्थुः ||
10.82.e: The waters, they received that germ primeval wherein the Gods were gathefed all together.  It rested set upon the Unborn's navel, that One wherein abide all things existing.

10.82.d: न तं विदाथ य इमा जजानायद युष्माकमन्तरम्बभूव | नीहारेण पराव्र्ता जल्प्या चासुत्र्प उक्थशासश्चरन्ति ||
10.82.e: Ye will not find him who produced these creatures: another thing hath risen up among you.  Enwrapt in misty cloud, with lips that stammer, hymn-chanters wander and are discontented.

10.83.d: यस्ते मन्यो.अविधद वज्र सायक सह ओजः पुष्यति विश्वमानुषक | साह्याम दासमार्यं तवया युजा सहस्क्र्तेनसहसा सहस्वता ||
10.83.e: HE who hath reverenced thee, Manyu, destructive bolt, breeds for himself forthwith all conquering energy.  Ārya and Dāsa will we conquer with thine aid, with thee the Conqueror, with conquest conquest-sped.

10.83.d: मन्युरिन्द्रो मन्युरेवास देवो मन्युर्होता वरुणोजातवेदाः | मन्युं विश ईळते मानुषीर्याः पाहि नोमन्यो तपसा सजोषाः ||
10.83.e: Manyu was Indra, yea, the God, was Manyu, Manyu was Hotar, Varuṇa, Jātavedas.  The tribes of human lineage worship Manyu. Accordant with thy fervour, Manyu, guard us.

10.83.d: अभीहि मन्यो तवसस्तवीयान तपसा युजा वि जहि शत्रून | अमित्रहा वर्त्रहा दस्युहा च विश्वा वसून्या भरात्वं नः ||
10.83.e: Come hither, Manyu, mightier tham the mighty; chase, with thy fervour for ally, our foemen.  Slayer of foes, of Vṛtra, and of Dasyu, bring thou to us all kinds of wealth and treasure.

10.83.d: तवं हि मन्यो अभिभूत्योजाः सवयम्भूर्भामोभिमातिषाहः | विश्वचर्षणिः सहुरिः सहावानस्मास्वोजः पर्तनासु धेहि ||
10.83.e: For thou art, Manyu, of surpassing vigour, fierce, queller of the foe, and self-existent,  Shared by all men, victorious, subduer: vouchsafe to us superior strengith in battles.

10.83.d: अभागः सन्नप परेतो अस्मि तव करत्वा तविषस्यप्रचेतः | तं तवा मन्यो अक्रतुर्जिहीळाहं सवा तनूर्बलदेयाय मेहि ||
10.83.e: I have departed, still without a portion, wise God! according to thy will, the Mighty.  I, feeble man, was wroth thee, O Manyu I am myself; come thou to give me vigour.

10.83.d: अयं ते अस्म्युप मेह्यर्वां परतीचीनः सहुरे विश्वधायः | मन्यो वज्रिन्नभि मामा वव्र्त्स्व हनाव दस्यून्रुतबोध्यापेः ||
10.83.e: Come hither. I am all thine own; advancing turn thou to me, Victorious, All-supporter!  Come to me, Manyu, Wielder of the Thunder: bethink thee of thy friend, and slay the Dasyus.

10.83.d: अभि परेहि दक्षिणतो भवा मे.अधा वर्त्राणि जङघनावभूरि | जुहोमि ते धरुणं मध्वो अग्रमुभा उपांशुप्रथमा पिबाव ||
10.83.e: Approach, and on my right hand hold thy station: so shall we slay a multitude of foemen.  The best of meath I offer to support thee: may we be first to drink thereof in quiet.

10.84.d: तवया मन्यो सरथमारुजन्तो हर्षमाणासो धर्षितामरुत्वः | तिग्मेषव आयुधा संशिशाना अभि पर यन्तुनरो अग्निरूपाः ||
10.84.e: BORNE on with thee, O Manyu girt by Maruts, let our brave men, impetuous, bursting forward,  March on, like flames of fire in form, exulting, with pointed arrows, sharpening their weapons.

10.84.d: अग्निरिव मन्यो तविषितः सहस्व सेनानीर्नः सहुरे हूतेधि | हत्वाय शत्रून वि भजस्व वेद ओजो मिमानो वि मर्धोनुदस्व ||
10.84.e: Flashing like fire, be thou, O conquering Manyu, invoked, O Victor, as our army's leader.  Slay thou our foes, distribute their possessions: show forth thy vigour, scatter those who hate us.

10.84.d: सहस्व मन्यो अभिमातिमस्मे रुजन मर्णन परम्र्णन परेहिशत्रून | उग्रं ते पाजो नन्वा रुरुध्रे वशी वशंनयस एकज तवम ||
10.84.e: O Manyu, overcome thou our assailant on! breaking, slaying, crushing down the foemen.  They have not hindered thine impetuous vigour: Mighty, Sole born! thou makest them thy subjects.

10.84.d: एको बहूनामसि मन्यवीळितो विशं-विशं युधये संशिशाधि | अक्र्त्तरुक तवया युजा वयं दयुमन्तं घोषंविजयाय कर्ण्महे ||
10.84.e: Alone or many thou art worshipped, Manyu: sharpen the spirit of each clan for battle.  With thee to aid, O thou of perfect splendour, we will uplift the glorious shout for conquest.

10.84.d: विजेषक्र्दिन्द्र इवानवब्रवो.अस्माकं मन्यो अधिपा भवेह | परियं ते नाम सहुरे गर्णीमसि विद्मा तमुत्सं यताबभूथ ||
10.84.e: Unyielding bringing victory like Indra, O Manyu, be thou here our Sovran Ruler.  To thy dear name, O Victor, we sing praises: we know the spring from which thou art come hither.

10.84.d: आभूत्या सहजा वज्र सायक सहो बिभर्ष्यभिभूतौत्तरम | करत्वा नो मन्यो सह मेद्येधि महाधनस्य पुरुहूतसंस्र्जि ||
10.84.e: Twin-born with power, destructive bolt of thunder, the highest conquering might is thine, Subduer!  Be friendly to its in thy spirit, Manyu, O Much-invoked, in shock of mighty battle.

10.84.d: संस्र्ष्टं धनमुभयं समाक्र्तमस्मभ्यं दत्तांवरुणश्च मन्युः | भियं दधाना हर्दयेषु शत्रवःपराजितासो अप नि लयन्ताम ||
10.84.e: For spoil let Varuṇa and Manyu give us the wealth of both sides gathered and collected;  And let our enemies with stricken spirits, o’erwhelmed with terror, slink away defeated.

10.85.d: सत्येनोत्तभिता भूमिः सूर्येणोत्तभिता दयौः | रतेनादित्यास्तिष्ठन्ति दिवि सोमो अधि शरितः ||
10.85.e: TRUTH is the base that bears the earth; by Sūrya are the heavens sustained.  By Law the Ādityas stand secure, and Soma holds his place in heaven.

10.85.d: सोमेनादित्या बलिनः सोमेन पर्थिवी मही | अथोनक्षत्राणामेषामुपस्थे सोम आहितः ||
10.85.e: By Soma are the Ādityas strong, by Soma mighty is the earth.  Thus Soma in the midst of all these constellations hath his place.

10.85.d: सोमं मन्यते पपिवन यत सम्पिंषन्त्योषधिम | सोमं यम्ब्रह्माणो विदुर्न तस्याश्नाति कश्चन ||
10.85.e: One thinks, when they have brayed the plant, that he hath drunk the Soma's juice;  Of him whom Brahmans truly know as Soma no one ever tastes.

10.85.d: आछद्विधानैर्गुपितो बार्हतैः सोम रक्षितः | गरव्णामिच्छ्र्ण्वन तिष्ठसि न ते अश्नाति पार्थिवः ||
10.85.e: Soma, secured by sheltering rules, guarded by hymns in Brhati,  Thou standest listening to the stones none tastes of thee who dwells on earth.

10.85.d: यत तवा देव परपिबन्ति तत आ पयायसे पुनः | वायुःसोमस्य रक्षिता समानां मास आक्र्तिः ||
10.85.e: When they begin to drink thee then, O God, thou swellest out again.  Vāyu is Soma's guardian God. The Moon is that which shapes the years.

10.85.d: रैभ्यासीदनुदेयी नाराशंसि नयोचनी | सूर्यायाभद्रमिद वासो गाथयैति परिष्क्र्तम ||
10.85.e: Raibhi was her dear bridal friend, and Narasamsi led her home.  Lovely was Sūrya's robe: she came to that which Gatha had adorned.

10.85.d: चित्तिरा उपबर्हणं चक्षुरा अभ्यञ्जनम | दयौर्भूमिःकोश आसीद यदयात सूर्या पतिम ||
10.85.e: Thought was the pillow of her couch, sight was the unguent for her eyes:  Her treasury was earth and heaven.ẉhen Sūrya went unto her Lord.

10.85.d: सतोमा आसन परतिधयः कुरिरं छन्द ओपशः | सूर्यायाश्विना वराग्निरासीत पुरोगवः ||
10.85.e: Hymns were the cross-bars of the pole, Kurira-metre decked the car:  The bridesmen were the Aśvin Pair Agni was leader of the train.

10.85.d: सोमो वधूयुरभवदश्विनास्तामुभा वरा | सूर्यांयत पत्ये शंसन्तीं मनसा सविताददात ||
10.85.e: Soma was he who wooed the maid: the groomsmen were both Aśvins, when  The Sun-God Savitar bestowed his willing Sūrya on her Lord.

10.85.d: मनो अस्या अन आसीद दयौरासीदुत छदिः | शुक्रावनड्वाहवास्तां यदयात सूर्या बर्हम ||
10.85.e: Her spirit was the bridal car; the covering thereof was heaven:  Bright were both Steers that drew it when Sūrya approached her husband's, home.

10.85.d: रक्सामाभ्यामभिहितौ गावौ ते सामनावितः | शरोत्रं तेचक्रे आस्तां दिवि पन्थाश्चराचारः ||
10.85.e: Thy Steers were steady, kept in place by holy verse and Sāma-hymn:  All car were thy two chariot wheels: thy path was tremulous in the sky,

10.85.d: शुची ते चक्रे यात्या वयानो अक्ष आहतः | अनोमनस्मयं सूर्यारोहत परयति पतिम ||
10.85.e: Clean, as thou wentest, were thy wheels wind, was the axle fastened there.  Sūrya, proceeding to her Lord, mounted a spirit-fashioried car.

10.85.d: सूर्याया वहतुः परागात सविता यमवास्र्जत | अघासुहन्यन्ते गावो.अर्जुन्योः पर्युह्यते ||
10.85.e: The bridal pomp of Sūrya, which Savitar started, moved along.  In Magha days are oxen slain, in Arjuris they wed the bride.

10.85.d: यदश्विना पर्छमानावयातं तरिचक्रेण वहतुंसूर्यायाः | विश्वे देवा अनु तद वामजानन पुत्रःपितरावव्र्णीत पूषा ||
10.85.e: When on your three-wheeled chariot, O Aśvins, ye came as wooers unto Sūrya's bridal,  Then all the Gods agreed to your proposal Pūṣan as Son elected you as Fathers.

10.85.d: यदयातं शुभस पती वरेयं सूर्यामुप | कवैकंचक्रं वामासीत कव देष्ट्राय तस्थथुः ||
10.85.e: O ye Two Lords of lustre, then when ye to Sūrya's wooing came,  Where was one chariot wheel of yours? Where stood ye for die Sire's command?

10.85.d: दवे ते चक्रे सूर्ये बरह्माण रतुथ विदुः | अथैकंचक्रं यद गुहा तदद्धातय इद विदुः ||
10.85.e: The Brahmans, by their seasons, know, O Sūrya, those two wheels of thine:  One kept concealed, those only who are skilled in highest truths have learned.

10.85.d: सूर्यायै देवेभ्यो मित्राय वरुणाय च | ये भूतस्यप्रचेतस इदं तेभ्यो.अकरं नमः ||
10.85.e: To Sūrya and the Deities, to Mitra and to Varuṇa.  Who know aright the thing that is, this adoration have I paid.

10.85.d: पूर्वापरं चरतो माययैतौ शिशू करिळन्तौ परि यतोध्वरम | विश्वान्यन्यो भुवनाभिचष्ट रतुन्रन्योविदधज्जायते पुनः ||
10.85.e: By their own power these Twain in close succession move;  They go as playing children round the sacrifice.  One of the Pair beholdeth all existing things; the other ordereth seasons and is born again.

10.85.d: नवो-नवो भवति जायमानो.अह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रम | भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन पर चन्द्रमास्तिरतेदीर्घमयुः ||
10.85.e: He, born afresh, is new and new for ever ensign of days he goes before the Mornings  Coming, he orders f6r the Gods their portion. The Moon prolongs the days of our existence.

10.85.d: सुकिंशुकं शल्मलिं विश्वरूपं हिरण्यवर्णं सुव्र्तंसुचक्रम | आ रोह सूर्ये अम्र्तस्य लोकं सयोनं पत्ये वहतुंक्र्णुष्व ||
10.85.e: Mount this, all-shaped, gold-hued, with strong wheels, fashioned of Kimsuka and Salmali, light-rolling,  Bound for the world of life immortal, Sūrya: make for thy lord a happy bridal journey.

10.85.d: उदीर्ष्वातः पतिवती हयेषा विश्वावसुं नमसागीर्भिरीळे | अन्यामिछ पित्र्षदं वयक्तां स ते भागोजनुषा तस्य विद्धि ||
10.85.e: Rise up from hence: this maiden hath a husband. I laud Visvavasu with hymns and homage.  Seek in her father's home another fair one, and find the portion from of old assigned thee.

10.85.d: उदीर्ष्वातो विश्वावसो नमसेळा महे तवा | अन्यामिछप्रफर्व्यं सं जायां पत्या सर्ज ||
10.85.e: Rise up from hence, Visvavasu: with reverence we worship thee.  Seek thou another willing maid, and with her husband leave the bride.

10.85.d: अन्र्क्षरा रजवः सन्तु पन्था येभिः सखायो यन्ति नोवरेयम | समर्यमा सं भगो नो निनीयात सं जस्पत्यंसुयममस्तु देवाः ||
10.85.e: Straight in direction be the path:s, and thornless, whereon our fellows travel to the wooing.  Let Aryaman and Bhaga lead us: perfect, O Gods, the union of the wife and husband.

10.85.d: पर तवा मुञ्चामि वरुणस्य पाशाद येन तवाबध्नात सवितासुशेवः | रतस्य योनौ सुक्र्तस्य लोके.अरिष्टां तवा सहपत्या दधामि ||
10.85.e: Now from the noose of Varuṇa I free thee, wherewith Most Blessed Savitar hath bound thee.  In Law's seat, to the world of virtuous action, I give thee up uninjured with thy consort.

10.85.d: परेतो मुञ्चामि नामुतः सुबद्धाममुतस करम | यथेयमिन्द्र मीढ्वः सुपुत्रा सुभगासति ||
10.85.e: Hence, and not thence, I send these free. I make thee softly fettered there.  That, Bounteous Indra, she may live blest in her fortune and her sons.

10.85.d: पूषा तवेतो नयतु हस्तग्र्ह्याश्विना तवा पर वहतांरथेन | गर्हान गछ गर्हपत्नी यथासो वशिनी तवंविदथमा वदासि ||
10.85.e: Let Pūṣan take thy hand and hence conduct thee; may the two Aśvins on their car transport thee.  Go to the house to be the household's mistress and speak as lady ito thy gathered people.

10.85.d: इह परियं परजया ते सं रध्यतामस्मिन गर्हे गार्हपत्यायजाग्र्हि | एना पत्या तन्वं सं सर्जस्वाधा जिव्री विदथमा वदाथः ||
10.85.e: Happy be thou and prosper witlh thy children here: be vigilant to rule thy household in this home.  Closely unite thy body with this; man, thy lord. So shall ye, full of years, address your company.

10.85.d: नीललोहितं भवति कर्त्यासक्तिर्व्यज्यते | एधन्ते अस्याज्ञातयः पतिर्बन्धेषु बध्यते ||
10.85.e: Her hue is blue and red: the fienod who clingeth close is driven off.  Well thrive the kinsmen of this bride the husband is bourid fast in bonds.

10.85.d: परा देहि शामुल्यं बरह्मभ्यो वि भजा वसु | कर्त्यैषापद्वती भूत्व्या जाया विशते पतिम ||
10.85.e: Give thou the woollen robe away: deal treasure to the Brahman priests.  This female fiend hath got her feet, and as a wife attends her lord.

10.85.d: अश्रीरा तनूर्भवति रुशती पापयामुया | पतिर्यद्वध्वो वाससा सवमङगमभिधित्सते ||
10.85.e: Unlovely is his body when it glistens with this wicked fiend,  What time the husband wraps about his limbs the garment of his wife.

10.85.d: ये वध्वश्चन्द्रं वहतुं यक्ष्मा यन्ति जनादनु | पुनस्तान यज्ञिया देवा नयन्तु यत आगताः ||
10.85.e: Consumptions, from her people, which follow the bride's resplendent train,—  These let the Holy Gods again bear to the place from which they came.

10.85.d: मा विदन परिपन्थिनो य आसीदन्ति दम्पती | सुगेभिर्दुर्गमतीतामप दरान्त्वरातयः ||
10.85.e: Let not the highway thieves who lie in ambush find the wedded pair.  By pleasant ways let them escape the danger, and let foes depart.

10.85.d: सुमङगलीरियं वधूरिमां समेत पश्यत | सौभाग्यमस्यै दत्त्वायाथास्तं वि परेतन ||
10.85.e: Signs of good fortune mark the bride come all of you and look at her.  Wish her prosperity, and then return unto your homes again.

10.85.d: तर्ष्टमेतत कटुकमेतदपाष्ठवद विषवन नैतदत्तवे | सूर्यां यो बरह्मा विद्यात स इद वाधूयमर्हति ||
10.85.e: Pungent is this, and bitter this, filled, as it were, with arrow-barbs, Empoisoned andṇot fit for use.  The Brahman who knows Sūrya well deserves the garment of the bride.

10.85.d: आशसनं विशसनमथो अधिविकर्तनम | सूर्यायः पश्यरूपाणि तानि बरह्मा तु शुन्धति ||
10.85.e: The fringe, the cloth that decks her head, and then the triply parted robe,—  Behold the hues which Sūrya wears these doth the Brahman purify.

10.85.d: गर्भ्णामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तं मया पत्या जरदष्टिर्यथासः | भगो अर्यमा सविता पुरन्धिर्मह्यं तवादुर्गार्हपत्याय देवाः ||
10.85.e: I take thy hand in mine for happy fortune that thou mayst reach old age with me thy husband.  Gods, Aryaman, Bhaga, Savitar, Purandhi, have given thee to be my household's mistress.

10.85.d: तां पूषञ्छिवतमामेरयस्व यस्यां बीजं मनुष्यावपन्ति | या न ऊरू उशती विश्रयाते यस्यामुशन्तःप्रहराम शेपम ||
10.85.e: O Pūṣan, send her on as most auspicious, her who shall be the sharer of my pleasures;  Her who shall twine her loving arms about me, and welcome all my love and mine embraces.

10.85.d: तुभ्यमग्रे पर्यवहन सूर्यां वहतुना सह | पुनःपतिभ्यो जायां दा अग्ने परजया सह ||
10.85.e: For thee, with bridal train, they, first, escorted Sūrya to her home.  Give to the husband in return, Agni, the wife with progeny.

10.85.d: पुनः पत्नीमग्निरदादायुषा सह वर्चसा | दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जीवाति शरदः शतम ||
10.85.e: Agni hath given the bride again with splendour and with ample life.  Long lived be he who is her lord; a hundred autumns let him live.

10.85.d: सोमः परथमो विविदे गन्धर्वो विविद उत्तरः | तर्तीयोग्निष टे पतिस्तुरीयस्ते मनुष्यजाः ||
10.85.e: Soma obtained her first of all; next the Gandharva was her lord.  Agai was thy third husband: now one bornof woman is thy fourth.

10.85.d: सोमो ददद गन्धर्वाय गन्धर्वो दददग्नये | रयिं चपुत्रांश्चादादग्निर्मह्यमथो इमाम ||
10.85.e: Soma to the Gandharva, and to Agni the Gandharva gave:  And Agni hath bestowed on me riches and sons and this my spouse.

10.85.d: इहैव सतं मा वि यौष्टं विश्वमायुर्व्यश्नुतम | कॄळन्तौ पुत्रैर्नप्त्र्भिर्मोदमानौ सवे गर्हे ||
10.85.e: Be ye not parted; dwell ye here reach the full time of human life.  With sons and grandsons sport and play, rejoicing in your own abode.

10.85.d: आ नः परजां हनयतु परजापतिराजरसाय समनक्त्वर्यमा | अदुर्मङगलीः पतिलोकमा विश शं नो भवद्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे ||
10.85.e: So may Prajāpati bring children forth to us; may Aryaman adorn us till old age come nigh.  Not inauspicious enter thou thy husband's house: bring blessing to our bipeds and our quadrupeds.

10.85.d: अघोरचक्षुरपतिघ्न्येधि शिवा पशुभ्यः सुमनाःसुवर्चाः | वीरसूर्देवकामा सयोना शं नो भव दविपदेशं चतुष्पदे ||
10.85.e: Not evil-eyed, no slayer of thy husband, bring weal to cattle, radiant, gentlehearted;  Loving the Gods, delightful, bearing heroes, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.

10.85.d: इमां तवमिन्द्र मीढ्वः सुपुत्रां सुभगां कर्णु | दशास्यां पुत्राना धेहि पतिमेकादशं कर्धि ||
10.85.e: O Bounteous Indra, make this bride blest in her sons and fortunate.  Vouchsafe to her ten sons, and make her husband the eleventh man.

10.85.d: सम्राज्ञी शवशुरे भव सम्राज्ञी शवश्र्वां भव | ननान्दरि सम्राज्ञी भव सम्राज्ञी अधि देव्र्षु ||
10.85.e: Over thy husband's father and thy husband's mother bear full sway.  Over the sister of thy lord, over his brothers rule supreme.

10.85.d: समञ्जन्तु विश्वे देवाः समापो हर्दयानि नौ | सम्मातरिश्वा सं धाता समु देष्ट्री दधातु नौ ||
10.85.e: So may the Universal Gods, so may the Waters join our hearts.  May Mātariśvan, Dhātar, and Destri together bind us close.

10.86.d: वि हि सोतोरस्र्क्षत नेन्द्रं देवममंसत | यत्रामदद्व्र्षाकपिरर्यः पुष्टेषु मत्सखा विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: MEN have abstained from pouring juice they count not Indra as a God.  Where at the votary's store my friend Vrsakapi hath drunk his fill. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: परा हीन्द्र धावसि वर्षाकपेरति वयथिः | नो अह परविन्दस्यन्यत्र सोमपीतये विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Thou, Indra, heedless passest by the ill Vrsakapi hath wrought;  Yet nowhere else thou findest place wherein to drink the Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: किमयं तवां वर्षाकपिश्चकार हरितो मर्गः | यस्मािरस्यसीदु नवर्यो वा पुष्टिमद वसु विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: What hath he done to injure thee, this tawny beast Vrsakapi,  With whom thou art so angry now? What is the votary's foodful store? Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: यमिमं तवं वर्षाकपिं परियमिन्द्राभिरक्षसि | शवा नवस्य जम्भिसअदपि कर्णे वरहयुर्विश्वस्मदिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Soon may the hound who hunts the boar seize him and bite him in the car,  O Indra, that Vrsakapi whom thou protectest as a friend, Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: परिया तष्टानि मे कपिर्व्यक्ता वयदूदुषत | शिरो नवस्य राविषं न सुगं दुष्क्र्ते भुवं विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Kapi hath marred the beauteous things, all deftly wrought, that were my joy.  In pieces will I rend his head; the sinner's portion sball be woo. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: न मत सत्री सुभसत्तरा न सुयाशुतरा भुवत | न मत्प्रतिच्यवीयसी न सक्थ्युद्यमीयसी विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: No Dame hath ampler charms than 1, or greater wealth of love's delights.  None with more ardour offers all her beauty to her lord's embrace. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: उवे अम्ब सुलाभिके यथेवाङग भविष्यति | भसन मे अम्बसक्थि मे शिरो मे वीव हर्ष्यति विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Mother whose love is quickly wibn, I say what verily will be.  My,breast, O Mother, and my head and both my hips seem quivering. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: किं सुबाहो सवङगुरे पर्थुष्टो पर्थुजाघने | किं शूरपत्निनस्त्वमभ्यमीषि वर्षाकपिं विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Dame with the lovely hands and arms, with broad hair-plaits add ample hips,  Why, O thou Hero's wife, art thou angry with our Vrsakapi? Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: अवीरामिव मामयं शरारुरभि मन्यते | उताहमस्मिवीरिणीन्द्रपत्नी मरुत्सखा विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: This noxious creature looks on me as one bereft of hero's love,  Yet Heroes for my sons have I, the Maruts’ Friend and Indra's Queen. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: संहोत्रं सम पुरा नारी समनं वाव गछति | वेधार्तस्य वीरिणीन्द्रपत्नी महीयते विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: From olden time the matron goes to feast and general sacrifice.  Mother of Heroes, Indra's Queen, the rite's ordainer is extolled. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: इन्द्राणीमासु नारिषु सुभगामहमश्रवम | नह्यस्यापरं चन जरसा मरते पतिर्विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: So have I heard Indrāṇī called most fortunate among these Dames,  For never shall her Consort die in future time through length of days. Supreme is Indra overall.

10.86.d: नाहमिन्द्राणि रारण सख्युर्व्र्षाकपेरते | यस्येदमप्यं हविः परियं देवेषु गछति विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Never, Indralni, have I joyed without my friend Vrsakapi,  Whose welcome offering here, made pure with water, goeth to the Gods. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: वर्षाकपायि रेवति सूपुत्र आदु सुस्नुषे | घसत त इन्द्रौक्षणः परियं काचित्करं हविर्विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Wealthy Vrsakapayi, blest with sons and consorts of thy sons,  Indra will eat thy bulls, thy dear oblation that effecteth much. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: उक्ष्णो हि मे पञ्चदश साकं पचन्ति विंशतिम | उताहमद्मि पीव इदुभा कुक्षी पर्णन्ति मे विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Fifteen in number, then, for me a score of bullocks they prepare,  And I devour the fat thereof: they fill my belly full with food. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: वर्षभो न तिग्मश्र्ङगो.अन्तर्यूथेषु रोरुवत | मन्थस्तैन्द्र शं हर्दे यं ते सुनोति भावयुर्विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Like as a bull with pointed horn, loud bellowing amid the herds,  Sweet to thine heart, O Indra, is the brew which she who tends thee pours. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: न सेशे यस्य रम्बते.अन्तरा सक्थ्या कप्र्त | सेदीशेयस्य रोमशं निषेदुषो विज्र्म्भते विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: He who is impotent, deserves no progeny, but he whose endowment can reach the depths of the womb.  Supreme Indra is above all.

10.86.d: न सेशे यस्य रोमशं निषेदुषो विज्र्म्भते | सेदीशेयस्य रम्बते.अन्तरा सक्थ्या कप्र्द विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: He who is impotent deserves no progeny, but he whose endowment can reach the depths of the womb.  Supreme Indra is above all!

10.86.d: अयमिन्द्र वर्षाकपिः परस्वन्तं हतं विदत | असिंसूनां नवं चरुमादेधस्यान आचितं विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: O Indra this Vrsakapi hath found a slain wild animal,  Dresser, and new-made pan, and knife, and wagon with a load of wood. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: अयमेमि विचाकशद विचिन्वन दासमार्यम | पिबामिपाकसुत्वनो.अभि धीरमचाकशं विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Distinguishing the Dāsa and the Ārya, viewing all, I go.  I look upon the wise, and drink the simple votary's Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: धन्व च यत कर्न्तत्रं च कति सवित ता वि योजना | नेदीयासो वर्षाकपे.अस्तमेहि गर्हानुप विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरह ||
10.86.e: The desert plains and steep descents, how many leagues in length they spread!  Go to the nearest houses, go unto thine home, Vrsakapi. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: पुनरेहि वर्षाकपे सुविता कल्पयावहै | य एषस्वप्ननंशनो.अस्तमेषि पथ पुनर्विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Turn thee again Vrsakapi: we twain will bring thee happiness.  Thou goest homeward on thy way along this path which leads to sleep. Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: यदुदञ्चो वर्षाकपे गर्हमिन्द्राजगन्तन | कव सय पुल्वघोम्र्गः कमगञ जनयोपनो विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
10.86.e: When, Indra and Vrsakapi, ye travelled upward to your home,  Where was that noisome beast, to whom went it, the beast that troubles man? Supreme is Indra over all.

10.86.d: पर्शुर्ह नाम मानवि साकं ससूव विंश तिम | भद्रम्भल तयस्या अभूद यस्या उदरममयद विश्वस्मादिन्द्रौत्तरः ||
10.86.e: Daughter of Manu, Parsu bare a score of children at a birth.  Her portion verily was bliss although her burthen caused her grief.

10.87.d: रक्षोहणं वाजिनमा जिघर्मि मित्रं परथिष्ठमुपयामि शर्म | शिशानो अग्निः करतुभिः समिद्धः स नोदिवा स रिषः पातु नक्तम ||
10.87.e: I BALM with oil the mighty Rakṣas-slayer; to the most famous Friend I come for shelter  Enkindled, sharpened by our rites, may Agni protect us in the day and night from evil.

10.87.d: अयोदंष्ट्रो अर्चिषा यातुधानानुप सप्र्श जातवेदःसमिद्धः | आ जिह्वया मुरदेवान रभस्व करव्यादो वर्क्त्व्यपि धत्स्वासन ||
10.87.e: O Jātavedas with the teeth of iron, enkindled with thy flame attack the demons.  Seize with thy longue the foolish gods' adorers: rend, put within thy mouth the raw-flesh caters.

10.87.d: उभोभयाविन्नुप धेहि दंष्ट्रा हिंस्रः शिशानो.अवरम्परं च | उतान्तरिक्षे परि याहि राजञ जम्भैः सन्धेह्यभि यातुधानान ||
10.87.e: Apply thy teeth, the upper and the lower, thou who hast both, enkindled and destroying.  Roam also in the air, O King, around us, and with thy jaws assail the wicked spirits.

10.87.d: यज्ञैरिषूः संनममानो अग्ने वाचा शल्यानशनिभिर्दिहानः | ताभिर्विध्य हर्दये यातुधानान परतीचो बाहून्प्रति भंध्येषाम ||
10.87.e: Bending thy shafts through sacrifices, Agni, whetting their points with song as if with whetstones,  Pierce to the heart therewith the Yātudhānas, and break their arms uplifed to attack thee.

10.87.d: अग्ने तवचं यातुधानस्य भिन्धि हिंस्राशनिर्हरसाहन्त्वेनम | पर पर्वाणि जातवेदः शर्णीहि करव्यात्क्रविष्णुर्वि चिनोतु वर्क्णम ||
10.87.e: Pierce through the Yātudhāna's skin, O Agni; let the destroying dart with fire consume him.  Rend his joints, Jātavedas, let the cater of flesh, flesh-seeking, track his mangled body.

10.87.d: यत्रेदानीं पश्यसि जातवेदस्तिष्ठन्तमग्न उत वाचरन्तम | यद वान्तरिक्षे पथिभिः पतन्तं तमस्ताविध्य शर्वा शिशानः ||
10.87.e: Where now thou seest Agni Jātavedas, one of these demons standing still or roaming,  Or flying on those paths in air's midregion, sharpen the shaft and as an archer pierce him.

10.87.d: उतालब्धं सप्र्णुहि जातवेद आलेभानाद रष्टिभिर्यातुधानात | अग्ने पूर्वो नि जहि शोशुचान आमादःक्ष्विङकास्तमदन्त्वेनीः ||
10.87.e: Tear from the evil spirit, Jātavedas, what he hath seized and with his spears hath captured.  Blazing before him strike him down, O Agni; let spotted carrion-eating kites devour him.

10.87.d: इह पर बरूहि यतमः सो अग्ने यो यातुधानो य इदंक्र्णोति | तमा रभस्व समिधा यविष्ठ नर्चक्षसश्चक्षुषे रन्धयैनम ||
10.87.e: Here tell this forth, O Agni: whosoever is, he himself, or acteth as, a demon,  Him grasp, O thou Most Youthful, with thy fuel. to the Mati-seer's eye give him as booty.

10.87.d: तीक्ष्णेनाग्ने चक्षुषा रक्ष यज्ञं पराञ्चं वसुभ्यःप्र णय परचेतः | हिंस्रं रक्षांस्यभि शोशुचानम्मा तवा दभन यातुधाना नर्चक्षः ||
10.87.e: With keen glance guard the sacrifice, O Agni: thou Sage, conduct it onward to the Vasus.  Let not the fiends, O Man-beholder, harm thee burning against the Rākṣasas to slay them.

10.87.d: नर्चक्षा रक्षः परि पश्य विक्षु तस्य तरीणि परतिश्र्णीह्यग्रा | तस्याग्ने पर्ष्टीर्हरसा शर्णीहि तरेधामूलं यातुधानस्य वर्श्च ||
10.87.e: Look on the fiend mid men, as Man-beholder: rend thou his three extremities in pieces.  Demolish with thy flame his ribs, O Agni, the Yātudhāna's root destroy thou triply.

10.87.d: तरिर्यातुधानः परसितिं त एत्व रतं यो अग्ने अन्र्तेन हन्ति | तमर्चिषा सफूर्जयञ जातवेदः समक्षमेनं गर्णतेनि वरंधि ||
10.87.e: Thrice, Agni, let thy noose surround the demon who with his falsehood injures Holy Order.  Loud roaring with thy flame, O Jātavedas, crush him and cast him down before the singer.

10.87.d: तदग्ने चक्षुः परति धेहि रेभे शफारुजं येनपश्यसि यातुधानम | अथर्ववज्ज्योतिषा दैव्येन सत्यन्धूर्वन्तमचितं नयोष ||
10.87.e: Lead thou the worshipper that eye, O Agni, wherewith thou lookest on the hoof-armed demon.  With light celestial in Atharvan's manner burn up the foot who ruins truth with falsehood.

10.87.d: यदग्ने अद्य मिथुना शपातो यद वाचस्त्र्ष्टं जनयन्तरेभाः | मन्योर्मनसः शरव्या जायते या तया विध्यह्र्दये यातुधानान ||
10.87.e: Agni, what curse the pair this day have uttered, what heated word the worshippers have spoken,  Each arrowy taunt sped from the angry spirit,—pierce to the heart therewith the Yātudhānas.

10.87.d: परा शर्णीहि तपसा यातुधानान पराग्ने रक्षो हरसाश्र्णीहि | परार्चिषा मूरदेवाञ्छ्र्णीहि परासुत्र्पो अभिशोशुचानः ||
10.87.e: With fervent heat exterminate the demons; destroy the fiends with burning flame, O Agni.  Destroy with fire the foolish gods' adorers; blaze and destrepy the insatiable monsters.

10.87.d: पराद्य देवा वर्जिनं शर्णन्तु परत्यगेनं शपथा यन्तुत्र्ष्टाः | वाचास्तेनं शरव रछन्तु मर्मन विश्वस्यैतुप्रसितिं यातुधानः ||
10.87.e: May Gods destroy this day the evil-doer may each hot curse of his return and blast him.  Let arrows pierce the liar in his vitals, and Visva's net enclose the Yātudhāna.

10.87.d: यः पौरुषेयेण करविषा समङकते यो अश्वेयेन पशुनायातुधानः | यो अघ्न्याया भरति कषीरमग्ने तेषांशीर्षाणि हरसापि वर्श्च ||
10.87.e: The fiend who smears himself with flesh of cattle, with flesh of horses and of human bodies,  Who steals the milch-cow's milk away, O Agni,—tear off the heads of such with fiery fury.

10.87.d: संवत्सरीणं पय उस्रियायास्तस्य माशीद यातुधानोन्र्चक्षः | पीयूषमग्ने यतमस्तित्र्प्सात तं परत्यञ्चमर्चिषा विध्य मर्मन ||
10.87.e: The cow gives milk each year, O Man-regarder: let not the Yātudhāna ever taste it.  If one would glut him with the biesting, Agni, pierce with thy flame his vitals as he meets thee.

10.87.d: विषं गवां यातुधानाः पिबन्त्वा वर्श्च्यन्तामदितयेदुरेवाः | परैनान देवः सविता ददातु परा भागमोषधीनां जयन्ताम ||
10.87.e: Let the fiends drink the poison of the cattle; may Aditi cast off the evildoers.  May the God Savitar give them up to ruin, and be their share of plants and herbs denied them.

10.87.d: सनादग्ने मर्णसि यातुधानान न तवा रक्षांसि पर्तनासुजिग्युः | अनु दह सहमूरान करव्यादो मा ते हेत्या मुक्षतदैव्यायाः ||
10.87.e: Agni, from days of old thou slayest demons: never shall Rākṣasas in fight o’ercome thee.  Burn up the foolish ones, the flesh-devourers: let none of them escape thine heavenly arrow.

10.87.d: तवं नो अग्ने अधरादुदक्तात तवं पश्चादुत रक्षापुरस्तात | परति ते ते अजरासस्तपिष्ठा अघशंसंशोशुचतो दहन्तु ||
10.87.e: Guard us, O Agni, from above and under, protect us fl-om behind us and before us;  And may thy flames, most fierce and never wasting, glowing with fervent heat, consume the sinner.

10.87.d: पश्चात पुरस्तादधरादुदक्तात कविः काव्येन परि पाहिराजन | सखे सखायमजरो जरिम्णे.अग्ने मर्तानमर्त्यस्त्वं नः ||
10.87.e: From rear, from front, from under, from above us, O King, protect us as a Sage with wisdom.  Guard to old age thy friend, O Friend, Eternal: O Agni, as Immortal, guard us mortals.

10.87.d: परि तवाग्ने पुरं वयं विप्रं सहस्य धीमहि | धर्षद्वर्णं दिवे-दिवे हन्तारं भङगुरावताम ||
10.87.e: We set thee round us as a fort, victorious Agni, thee a Sage,  Of hero lineage, day by day, destroyer of our treacherous foes.

10.87.d: विषेण भङगुरावतः परति षम रक्षसो दह | अग्नेतिग्मेन शोचिषा तपुरग्राभिरषटिभिः ||
10.87.e: Burn with thy poison turned against the treacherous brood of Rākṣasas,  O Agni, with thy sharpened glow, with lances armed with points of flame.

10.87.d: परत्यग्ने मिथुन दह यातुधाना किमीदिना | सं तवाशिशामि जाब्र्ह्यदब्धं विप्र मन्मभिः ||
