10.87.e: Burn thou the paired Kimīdins, brun, Agni, the Yātudhāna pairs.  I sharpen thee, Infallible, with hymns. O Sage, be vigilant.

10.87.d: परत्यग्ने हरसा हरः शर्णीहि विश्वतः परति | यातुधानस्य रक्षसो बलं वि रुज वीर्यम ||
10.87.e: Shoot forth, O Agni, with thy flame demolish them on every side.  Break thou the Yātudhāna's strength, the vigour of the Rākṣasa.

10.88.d: हविष पान्तमजरं सवर्विदि दिविस्प्र्श्याहुतं जुष्टमग्नौ | तस्य भर्मणे भुवनाय देवा धर्मणे कंस्वधया पप्रथन्त ||
10.88.e: DEAR, ageless sacrificial drink is offered in light-discovering, heaven-pervading Agni.  The Gods spread forth through his Celestial Nature, that he might bear the world up and sustain it.

10.88.d: गीर्णं भुवनं तमसपगूळमाविः सवरभवज्जातेग्नौ | तस्य देवाः पर्थिवि दयौरुतापो.अरणयन्नोषधीः सख्ये अस्य ||
10.88.e: The world was swallowed and concealed in darkness: Agni was born, and light became apparent.  The Deities, the broad earth, and the heavens, and plants, and waters gloried in his friendship.

10.88.d: देवेभिर्न्विषितो यज्ञियेभिरग्निं सतोषाण्यजरम्ब्र्हन्तम | यो भानुना पर्थिविं दयामुतेमामाततानरोदसी अन्तरिक्षम ||
10.88.e: Inspired by Gods who claim our adoration, I now will laud Eternal Lofty Agni,  Him who hath spread abroad the earth with lustre, this heaven, and both the worlds, and air's mid-region.

10.88.d: यो होतासीत परथमो देवजुष्टो यं समञ्जन्नाज्येनाव्र्णानः | स पतत्रीत्वरं सथ जगद यच्छ्वात्रमग्निरक्र्नोज्जातवेदः ||
10.88.e: Earliest Priest whom all the Gods accepted, and chose him, and anointed him with butter,  He swiftly made all things that fly, stand, travel, all that hath motion, Agni Jātavedas.

10.88.d: यज्जतवेदो भुवनस्य मूर्धन्नतिष्ठो अग्ने सह रोचनेन | तं तवहेम मतिभिर्गीर्भिरुक्थैः स यज्ञियो अभवोरोदसिप्राः ||
10.88.e: Because thou, Agni, Jātavedas, stoodest at the world's head with thy refulgent splendour,  We sent thee forth with hymns and songs and praises: thou filledst heaven and earth, God meet for worship.

10.88.d: मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सुर्यो जायतेप्रातरुद्यन | मयामु तु यज्ञियानामेतमपो यत्तूर्णिश्चरति परजानन ||
10.88.e: Head of the world is Agni in the night-time; then, as the Sun, at morn springs up and rises.  Then to his task goes the prompt Priest foreknowing the wondrous power of Gods who must be honoured.

10.88.d: दर्शेन्यो यो महिना समिद्धो.अरोचत दिवियोनिर्विभावा | तस्मिन्नग्नौ सूक्तवाकेन देवा हविर्विश्व अजुहवुस्तनूपाः ||
10.88.e: Lovely is he who, kindled in his greatness, hath shone forth, seated in the heavens, refulgent.  With resonant hymns all Gods who guard our bodies have offered up oblation in this Agni.

10.88.d: सूक्तवकं परथममादिदग्निमादिद धविरजनयन्तदेवाः | स एषां यज्ञो अभवत तनूपस्तं दयौर्वेदतं परिथिवि तमापः ||
10.88.e: First the Gods brought the hymnal into being; then they engendered Agni, then oblation.  He was their sacrifice that guards our bodies: him the heavens know, the earth, the waters know him.

10.88.d: यं देवासो अजनयन्ताग्निं यस्मिन्नाजुहवुर्भुवनानिविश्वा | सो अर्चिषा पर्थिवीं दयामुतेमां रजूयमानोतपन महित्वा ||
10.88.e: He, Agni, whom the Gods have generated, in whom they offered up all worlds and creatures,  He with his bright glow heated earth and heaven, urging himself right onward in his grandeur.

10.88.d: सतोमेन हि दिवि देवासो अग्निमजीजनञ्छक्तिभीरोदसिप्राम | तमू अक्र्ण्वन तरेधा भुवे कं स ओषधीःपचति विश्वरूपाः ||
10.88.e: Then by the laud the Gods engendered Agni in heaven, who fills both worlds through strength and vigour.  They made him to appear in threefold essence: he ripens plants of every form and nature.

10.88.d: यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्ञियासो दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयम | यदा चरिष्णू मिथुनावभूतामादित परापश्यन्भुवनानि विश्वा ||
10.88.e: What time the Gods, whose due is worship, set him as Sūrya, Son of Aditi, in heaven,  When the Pair, ever wandering, sprang to being, all creatures that existed looked upon them.

10.88.d: विश्वस्मा अग्निं भुवनाय देवा वैश्वानरं केतुमह्नामक्र्ण्वन | आ यस्ततानोषसो विभातीरपो ऊर्णोति तमोर्चिषा यन ||
10.88.e: For all the world of life the Gods made Agni Vaiśvānara to be the days' bright Banner,—  Him who hath spread abroad the radiant Mornings, and, coming with his light, unveils the darkness.

10.88.d: वैश्वानरं कवयो यज्ञियासो.अग्निं देवा अजनयन्नजुर्यम | नक्षत्रं परत्नममिनच्चरिष्णु यक्षस्याध्यक्षन्तविषं बर्हन्तम ||
10.88.e: The wise and holy Deities engendered Agni Vaiśvānara whom age ne’er touches.  The Ancient Star that wanders on for ever, lofty and. strong, Lord of the Living Being.

10.88.d: वैश्वानरं विश्वहा दीदिवांसं मन्त्रैरग्निं कविमछा वदामः | यो महिम्ना परिबभूवोर्वी उतावस्तादुतदेवः परस्तात ||
10.88.e: We call upon the Sage with holy verses, Agni Vaiśvānara the ever-beaming,  Who hath surpassed both heaven and earth in greatness: he is a God below, a God above us.

10.88.d: दवे सरुती अश्र्णवं पितॄणामहं देवानामुतमर्त्यानाम | ताभ्यामिदं विश्वमेजत समेति यदन्तरापितरं मातरं च ||
10.88.e: I have heard mention of two several pathways, ways of the Fathers and of Gods and mortals.  On these two paths each moving creature travels, each thing between the Father and the Mother.

10.88.d: दवे समीची बिभ्र्तश्चरन्तं शीर्षतो जातं मनसाविम्र्ष्टम | स परत्यं विश्वा भुवनानि तस्थावप्रयुछन्तरणिर्भ्राजमानः ||
10.88.e: These two united paths bear him who journeys born from the head and pondered with the spirit  He stands directed to all things existing, hasting, unresting in his fiery splendour.

10.88.d: यत्रा वदेते अवरः परश्च यज्ञन्योः कतरो नौ वि वेद | आ शेकुरित सधमादं सखायो नक्षन्त यज्ञं कैदं वि वोचत ||
10.88.e: Which of us twain knows where they speak together, upper and lower of the two rite-leaders?  Our friends have helped to gather our assembly. They came to sacrifice; who will announce it?

10.88.d: कत्यग्नयः कति सूर्यासः कत्युषासः कत्यु सविदापः | नोपस्पिजं वः पितरो वदामि पर्छामि वः कवयोविद्मने कम ||
10.88.e: How many are the Fires and Suns in number? What is the number of the Dawns and Waters?  Not jestingly I speak to you, O Fathers. Sages, I ask you this for information.

10.88.d: यावन्मात्रमुषसो न परतीकं सुपर्ण्यो वसतेमातरिश्वः | तावद दधात्युप यज्ञमायन बराह्मणोहोतुरवरो निषीदन ||
10.88.e: As great as is the fair-winged Morning's presence to him who dwells beside us, Mātariśvan!  Is what the Brahman does when he approaches to sacrifice and sits below the Hotar.

10.89.d: इन्द्रं सतवा नर्तमं यस्य मह्ना विबबाधे रोचना वि जमोन्तान | आ यः पप्रौ चर्षणीध्र्द वरोभिः परसिन्धुभ्यो रिरिचानो महित्वा ||
10.89.e: I WILL extol the most heroic Indra who with his might forced earth and sky asunder;  Who hath filled all with width as man's Upholder, surpassing floods and rivers in his greatness.

10.89.d: स सूर्यः पर्युरू वरांस्येन्द्रो वव्र्त्याद रथ्येवचक्रा | अतिष्ठन्तमपस्यं न सर्गं कर्ष्णा तमांसित्विष्या जघान ||
10.89.e: Sūrya is he: throughout the wide expanses shall Indra turn him, swift as car-wheels, hither,  Like a stream resting not but ever active he hath destroyed, with light, the black-hued darkness.

10.89.d: समानमस्मा अनपाव्र्दर्च कष्मया दिवो असमं बरह्मनव्यम | वि यः पर्ष्ठेव जनिमान्यर्य इन्द्रश्चिकाय नसखायमीषे ||
10.89.e: To him I sing a holy prayer, incessant new, matchless, common to the earth and heaven,  Who marks, as they were backs, all living creatures: ne’er doth he fail a friend, the noble Indra.

10.89.d: इन्द्राय गिरो अनिशितसर्गा अपः परेरयं सगरस्य बुध्नात | यो अक्षेणेव चक्रिया शचीभिर्विष्वक तस्तम्भप्र्थिवीमुत दयाम ||
10.89.e: I will send forth my songs in flow unceasing, like water from the ocean's depth, to Indra.  Who to his car on both its sides securely hath fixed the earth and heaven as with an axle.

10.89.d: आपान्तमन्युस्त्र्पलप्रभर्मा धुनिः शिमीवाञ्छरुमान्र्जीषी | सोमो विश्वान्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिन्द्रम्प्रतिमानानि देभुः ||
10.89.e: Rousing with draughts, the Shaker, rushing onward, impetuous, very strong, armed as with arrows  Is Soma; forest trees and all the bushes deceive not Indra with their offered likeness.

10.89.d: न यस्य दयावाप्र्थिवी न धन्व नान्तरिक्षं नाद्रयःसोमो अक्षाः | यदस्य मन्युरधिनीयमानः सर्णाति वीळुरुजति सथिराणि ||
10.89.e: Soma hath flowed to him whom naught can equal, the earth, the heavens, the firmament, the mountains,—  When heightened in his ire his indignation shatters the firm and breaks the strong in pieces.

10.89.d: जघान वर्त्रं सवधितिर्वनेव रुरोज पुरो अरदन नसिन्धून | बिभेद गिरिं नवमिन न कुम्भमा गा इन्द्रोक्र्णुत सवयुग्भिः ||
10.89.e: As an axe fells the tree so be slew Vṛtra, brake down the strongholds and dug out the rivers.  He cleft the mountain like a new-made pitcher. Indra brought forth the kine with his Companions.

10.89.d: तवं ह तयद रणया इन्द्र धीरो.असिर्न पर्व वर्जिनाश्र्णासि | पर ये मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम युजं न जनामिनन्ति मित्रम ||
10.89.e: Wise art thou, Punisher of guilt, O Indra. The sword lops limbs, thou smitest down the sinner,  The men who injure, as it were a comrade, the lofty Law of Varuṇa and Mitra.

10.89.d: पर ये मित्रं परार्यमणं दुरेवाः पर संगिरः परवरुणं मिनन्ति | नयमित्रेषु वधमिन्द्र तुम्रं वर्षन्व्र्षाणमरुषं शिशीहि ||
10.89.e: Men who lead evil lives, who break agreements, and injure Varuṇa, Aryaman and Mitra,—  Against these foes, O Mighty Indra, sharpen, as furious death, thy Bull of fiery colour.

10.89.d: इन्द्रो दिव इन्द्र ईशे पर्थिव्या इन्द्रो अपामिन्द्र इत्पर्वतानाम | इन्द्रो वर्धामिन्द्र इन मेधिराणामिन्द्रःक्षेमे योगे हव्य इन्द्रः ||
10.89.e: Indra is Sovran Lord of Earth and Heaven, Indra is Lord of waters and of mountains.  Indra is Lord of prosperers and sages Indra must be invoked in rest and effort.

10.89.d: पराक्तुभ्य इन्द्रः पर वर्धो अहभ्यः परान्तरिक्षात परसमुद्रस्य धासेः | पर वातस्य परथसः पर जमो अन्तात्प्र सिन्धुभ्यो रिरिचे पर कषितिभ्यः ||
10.89.e: Vaster than days and nights, Giver of increase, vaster than firmament and flood of ocean,  Vaster than bounds of earth and wind's extension, vaster than rivers and our lands is Indra.

10.89.d: पर शोशुचत्या उषसो न केतुरसिन्वा ते वर्ततामिन्द्रहेतिः | अश्मेव विध्य दिव आ सर्जानस्तपिष्ठेन हेषसाद्रोघमित्रान ||
10.89.e: Forward, as herald of refulgent Morning, let thine insatiate arrow fly, O Indra.  And pierce, as ’twere a stone launched forth from heaven, with hottest blaze the men who love deception.

10.89.d: अन्वह मासा अन्विद वनान्यन्वोषधीरनु पर्वतासः | अन्विन्द्रं रोदसी वावशाने अन्वापो अजिहतजायमानम ||
10.89.e: Him, verily, the moons, the mountains followed, the tall trees followed and the plants and herbage.  Yearning with love both Worlds approached, the Waters waited on Indra when he first had being.

10.89.d: कर्हि सवित सा त इन्द्र चेत्यासदघस्य यद भिनदो रक्षेषत | मित्रक्रुवो यच्छसने न गावः पर्थिव्या आप्र्गमुया शयन्ते ||
10.89.e: Where was the vengeful dart when thou, O Indra, clavest the demon ever beat on outrage?  When fiends lay there upon the ground extended like cattle in the place of immolation?

10.89.d: शत्रूयन्तो अभि ये नस्ततस्रे महि वराधन्त ओगणासैन्द्र | अन्धेनामित्रास्तमसा सचन्तां सुज्योतिषो अक्तवस्तानभि षयुः ||
10.89.e: Those who are set in enmity against us, the Ogaṇas, O Indra, waxen mighty,—  Let blinding darkness follow those our foemen, while these shall have bright shining nights to light them.

10.89.d: पुरूणि हि तवा सवना जनानां बरह्माणि मन्दन गर्णताम्र्षीणाम | इमामाघोषन्नवसा सहूतिं तिरो विश्वानर्चतो याह्यर्वां ||
10.89.e: May plentiful libations of the people, and singing Ṛṣis’ holy prayers rejoice thee.  Hearing with love this common invocation, come unto us, pass by all those who praise thee.

10.89.d: एवा ते वयमिन्द्र भुञ्जतीनां विद्याम सुमतीनांनवानाम | विद्याम वस्तोरवसा गर्णन्तो विश्वामित्रा उतत इन्द्र नूनम ||
10.89.e: O Indra, thus may we be made partakers of thy new favours that shall bring us profit.  Singing with love, may we the Viśvāmitras win daylight even now through thee, O Indra.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

10.90.d: सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात | सभूमिं विश्वतो वर्त्वात्यतिष्ठद दशाङगुलम ||
10.90.e: A THOUSAND heads hath Puruṣa, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet.  On every side pervading earth he fills a space ten fingers wide.

10.90.d: पुरुष एवेदं सर्वं यद भूतं यच्च भव्यम | उताम्र्तत्वस्येशानो यदन्नेनातिरोहति ||
10.90.e: This Puruṣa is all that yet hath been and all that is to be;  The Lord of Immortality which waxes greater still by food.

10.90.d: एतावानस्य महिमातो जयायांश्च पूरुषः | पादो.अस्यविश्वा भूतानि तरिपादस्याम्र्तं दिवि ||
10.90.e: So mighty is his greatness; yea, greater than this is Puruṣa.  All creatures are one-fourth of him, three-fourths eternal life in heaven.

10.90.d: तरिपादूर्ध्व उदैत पुरुषः पादो.अस्येहाभवत पुनः | ततो विष्वं वयक्रामत साशनानशने अभि ||
10.90.e: With three-fourths Puruṣa went up: one-fourth of him again was here.  Thence he strode out to every side over what cats not and what cats.

10.90.d: तस्माद विराळ अजायत विराजो अधि पूरुषः | स जातोत्यरिच्यत पश्चाद भूमिमथो पुरः ||
10.90.e: From him Virāj was born; again Puruṣa from Virāj was born.  As soon as he was born he spread eastward and westward o’er the earth.

10.90.d: यत पुरुषेण हविषा देवा यज्ञमतन्वत | वसन्तोस्यासीदाज्यं गरीष्म इध्मः शरद धविः ||
10.90.e: When Gods prepared the sacrifice with Puruṣa as their offering,  Its oil was spring, the holy gift was autumn; summer was the wood.

10.90.d: तं यज्ञं बर्हिषि परौक्षन पुरुषं जातमग्रतः | तेन देवा अयजन्त साध्या रषयश्च ये ||
10.90.e: They balmed as victim on the grass Puruṣa born in earliest time.  With him the Deities and all Sādhyas and Ṛṣis sacrificed.

10.90.d: तस्माद यज्ञात सर्वहुतः सम्भ्र्तं पर्षदाज्यम | पशून्तांश्चक्रे वायव्यानारण्यान गराम्याश्च ये ||
10.90.e: From that great general sacrifice the dripping fat was gathered up.  He formed the creatures of-the air, and animals both wild and tame.

10.90.d: तस्माद यज्ञात सर्वहुत रचः सामानि जज्ञिरे | छन्दांसिजज्ञिरे तस्माद यजुस्तस्मादजायत ||
10.90.e: From that great general sacrifice Ṛcas and Sāma-hymns were born:  Therefrom were spells and charms produced; the Yajus had its birth from it.

10.90.d: तस्मादश्वा अजायन्त ये के चोभयादतः | गावो हजज्ञिरे तस्मात तस्माज्जाता अजावयः ||
10.90.e: From it were horses born, from it all cattle with two rows of teeth:  From it were generated kine, from it the goats and sheep were born.

10.90.d: यत पुरुषं वयदधुः कतिधा वयकल्पयन | मुखं किमस्य कौ बाहू का ऊरू पादा उच्येते ||
10.90.e: When they divided Puruṣa how many portions did they make?  What do they call his mouth, his arms? What do they call his thighs and feet?

10.90.d: बराह्मणो.अस्य मुखमासीद बाहू राजन्यः कर्तः | ऊरूतदस्य यद वैश्यः पद्भ्यां शूद्रो अजायत ||
10.90.e: The Brahman was his mouth, of both his arms was the Rājanya made.  His thighs became the Vaiśya, from his feet the Śūdra was produced.

10.90.d: चन्द्रमा मनसो जातश्चक्षोः सूर्यो अजायत | मुखादिन्द्रश्चाग्निश्च पराणाद वायुरजायत ||
10.90.e: The Moon was gendered from his mind, and from his eye the Sun had birth;  Indra and Agni from his mouth were born, and Vāyu from his breath.

10.90.d: नाभ्या आसीदन्तरिक्षं शीर्ष्णो दयौः समवर्तत | पद्भ्यां भूमिर्दिशः शरोत्रात तथा लोकानकल्पयन ||
10.90.e: Forth from his navel came mid-air the sky was fashioned from his head  Earth from his feet, and from his car the regions. Thus they formed the worlds.

10.90.d: सप्तास्यासन परिधयस्त्रिः सप्त समिधः कर्ताः | देवायद यज्ञं तन्वाना अबध्नन पुरुषं पशुम ||
10.90.e: Seven fencing-sticks had he, thrice seven layers of fuel were prepared,  When the Gods, offering sacrifice, bound, as their victim, Puruṣa.

10.90.d: यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवास्तानि धर्माणि परथमान्यासन | ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचन्त यत्र पूर्वे साध्याःसन्ति देवाः ||
10.90.e: Gods, sacrificing, sacrificed the victim these were the earliest holy ordinances.  The Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.

10.91.d: सं जाग्र्वद्भिर्जरमाण इध्यते दमे दमूना इषयन्निळस पदे | विश्वस्य होता हविषो वरेण्यो विभुर्विभावासुषखा सखीयते ||
10.91.e: BRISK, at the place of Iḷā, hymned by men who wake, our own familiar Friend is kindled in the house;  Hotar of all oblation, worthy of our choice, Lord, beaming, trusty friend to one who loveth him.

10.91.d: स दर्शतश्रीरतिथिर्ग्र्हे-गर्हे वने-वने शिश्रियेतक्ववीरिव | जनं-जनं जन्यो नाति मन्यते विश आक्षेति विश्यो विशं विशम ||
10.91.e: He, excellent in glory, guest in every house, finds like a swift-winged bird a home in every tree.  Benevolent to men, he scorns no living man: Friend to the tribes of men he dwells with every tribe.

10.91.d: सुदक्षो दक्षैः करतुनासि सुक्रतुरग्ने कविः काव्येनासिविश्ववित | वसुर्वसूनां कषयसि तवमेक इद दयावा चयानि पर्थिवी च पुष्यतः ||
10.91.e: Most sage with insight, passing skilful with thy powers art thou, O Agni, wise with wisdom, knowing all.  As Vasu, thou alone art Lord of all good things, of all the treasures that the heavens and earth produce.

10.91.d: परजानन्नग्ने तव योनिं रत्वियमिळायास पदे घर्तवन्तमासदः | आ ते चिकित्र उषसामिवेतयो.अरेपसः सूर्यस्येवरश्मयः ||
10.91.e: Foreknowing well, O Agni, thou in Iḷā's place hast occupied thy regular station balmed with oil.  Marked are thy comings like the comings of the Dawns, the rays of him who shineth spotless as the Sun.

10.91.d: तव शरियो वर्ष्यस्येव विद्युतश्चित्राश्चिकित्र उषसांन केतवः | यदोषधीरभिस्र्ष्टो वनानि च परिस्वयं चिनुषे अन्नमास्ये ||
10.91.e: Thy glories are, as lightnings from the rainy cloud, marked, many-hued, like heralds of the Dawns’ approach,  When, loosed to wander over plants and forest trees, thou crammest by thyself thy food into thy mouth.

10.91.d: तमोषधीर्दधिरे गर्भं रत्वियं तमापो अग्निंजनयन्त मातरः | तमित समानं वनिनश्च वीरुधोऽनतर्वतीश्च सुवते च विश्वहा ||
10.91.e: Him, duly coming as their germ, have plants received: this Agni have maternal Waters brought to life.  So in like manner do the forest trees and plants bear him within them and produce him evermore.

10.91.d: वातोपधूत इषितो वशाननु तर्षु यदन्ना वेविषद्वितिष्ठसे | आ ते यतन्ते रथ्यो यथा पर्थक छर्धांस्यग्ने अजराणि धक्षतः ||
10.91.e: When, sped and urged by wind, thou spreadest thee abroad, swift piercing through thy food according to thy will,  Thy never-ceasing blazes, longing to consume, like men on chariots, Agni, strive on every side.

10.91.d: मेधाकारं विदथस्य परसाधनमग्निं होतारम्परिभूतमं मतिम | तमिदर्भे हविष्या समानमित्तमिन महे वर्णते नान्यं तवत ||
10.91.e: Agni, the Hotar-priest who fills the assembly full, Waker of knowledge, chief Controller of the thought,—  Him, yea, none other than thyself, doth man elect at sacrificial offerings great and small alike.

10.91.d: तवामिदत्र वर्णते तवायवो होतारमग्ने विदथेषुवेधसः | यद देवयन्तो दधति परयाण्सि ते हविष्मन्तोमनवो वर्क्तबर्हिषः ||
10.91.e: Here, Agni, the arrangers, those attached to thee, elect thee as their Priest in sacred gatherings,  When men with strewn clipt grass and sacrificial gifts offer thee entertainment, piously inclined.

10.91.d: तवाग्ने होत्रं तव पोत्रं रत्वियं तव नेष्ट्रं तवमग्निद रतायतः | तव परशास्त्रं तवमध्वरीयसि बरह्माचासि गर्हपतिश्च नो दमे ||
10.91.e: Thine is the Herald's task and Cleanser's duly timed; Leader art thou, and Kindler for the pious man.  Thou art Director, thou the ministering Priest: thou art the Brahman, Lord and Master in our home.

10.91.d: यस्तुभ्यमग्ने अम्र्ताय मर्त्यः समिधा दाशदुत वाहविष्क्र्ति | तस्य होता भवसि यासि दूत्यमुप बरूषेयजस्यध्वरीयसि ||
10.91.e: When mortal man presents to thee Immortal God, Agni, his fuel or his sacrificial gift,  Then thou art his Adhvaryu, Hotar, messenger, callest the Gods and orderest the sacrifice.

10.91.d: इमा अस्मै मतयो वाचो अस्मदान रचो गिरः सुष्टुतयःसमग्मत | वसूयवो वसवे जातवेदसे वर्द्धासु चिद वर्धनोयासु चाकनत ||
10.91.e: From us these hymns in concert have gone forth to him, these. holy words, these Ṛcas, songs and eulogies,  Eager for wealth, to Jātavedas fain for wealth: when they have waxen strong they please their Strengthener.

10.91.d: इमां परत्नाय सुष्टुतिं नवीयसीं वोचेयमस्मा उशतेश्र्णोतु नः | भूया अन्तरा हर्द्यस्य निस्प्र्शे जायेवपत्य उशती सुवासाः ||
10.91.e: This newest eulogy will I speak forth to him, the Ancient One who loves it. May he hear our voice.  May it come near his heart and make it stir with love, as a fond well-dressed matron clings about her lord.

10.91.d: यस्मिन्नश्वास रषभास उक्षणो वशा मेषावस्र्ष्टास आहुताः | कीलालपे सोमप्र्ष्ठाय वेधसेह्र्दा मतिं जनये चारुमग्नये ||
10.91.e: He in whom horses, bulls, oxen, and barren cows, and rams, when duly set apart, are offered up,—  To Agni, Soma-sprinkled, drinker of sweet juice, Disposer, with my heart I bring a fair hymn forth.

10.91.d: अहाव्यग्ने हविरास्ये ते सरुचीव घर्तं चम्वीव सोमः | वाजसनिं रयिमस्मे सुवीरं परशस्तं धेहि यशसम्ब्र्हन्तम ||
10.91.e: Into thy mouth is poured the offering, Agni, as Soma into cup, oil into ladle.  Vouchsafe us wealth. strength-winning, blest with heroes, wealth lofty, praised by men, and full of splendour.

10.92.d: यज्ञस्य वो रथ्यं विश्पतिं विशां होतारमक्तोरतिथिं विभावसुम | शोचञ्छुष्कासु हरिणीषु जर्भुरद्व्र्षा केतुर्यजतो दयामशायत ||
10.92.e: I PRAISE your Charioteer of sacrifice, the Lord of men, Priest of the tribes, refulgent, Guest of night.  Blazing amid dry plants, snatching amid the green, the Strong, the Holy Herald hath attained to heaven.

10.92.d: इममञ्जस्पामुभये अक्र्ण्वत धर्माणमग्निं विदथस्यसाधनम | अक्तुं न यह्वमुषसः पुरोहितं तनूनपातमरुषस्य निंसते ||
10.92.e: Him, Agni, Gods and men have made their chief support, who drinks the fatness and completes the sacrifice.  With kisses they caress the Grandson of the Red, like the swift ray of light, the Household Priest of Dawn.

10.92.d: बळ अस्य नीथा वि पणेश्च मन्महे वया अस्य परहुताासुरत्तवे | यदा घोरासो अम्र्तत्वमाशतादिज्जनस्यदैव्यस्य चर्किरन ||
10.92.e: Yea, we discriminate his and the niggard's ways: his branches evermore are sent forth to consume.  When his terrific flames have reached the Immortal's world, then men remember and extol the Heavenly Folk.

10.92.d: रतस्य हि परसितिर्द्यौरुरु वयचो नमो मह्यरमतिःपनीयसी | इन्द्रो मित्रो वरुणः सं चिकित्रिरे.अथो भगःसविता पूतदक्षसः ||
10.92.e: For then the net of Law, Dyaus, and the wide expanse, Earth, Worship, and Devotion meet for highest praise,  Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra were of one accord, and Savitar and Bhaga, Lords of holy might.

10.92.d: पर रुद्रेण ययिना यन्ति सिन्धवस्तिरो महीमरमतिन्दधन्विरे | येभिः परिज्मा परियन्नुरु जरयो वि रोरुवज्जठरे विश्वमुक्षते ||
10.92.e: Onward, with ever-roaming Rudra, speed the floods: over Aramati the Mighty have they run.  With them Parijman, moving round his vast domain, loud bellowing, bedews all things that are within.

10.92.d: कराणा रुद्रा मरुतो विश्वक्र्ष्टयो दिवः शयेनासोसुरस्य नीळयः | तेभिश्चष्टे वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमेन्द्रोदेवेभिरर्वशेभिरर्वशः ||
10.92.e: Straightway the Rudras, Maruts visiting all men, Falcons of Dyaus, home-dwellers with the Asura,—  Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman look on with these, and the swift-moving Indra with swift-moving Gods.

10.92.d: इन्द्रे भुजं शशमानास आशत सूरो दर्शीके वर्षणश्च पौंस्ये | पर ये नवस्यार्हणा ततक्षिरे युजं वज्रंन्र्षदनेषु कारवः ||
10.92.e: With Indra have they found enjoyment, they who toil, in the light's beauty, in the very Strong One's strength;  The singers who in men's assemblies forged for him, according to his due, his friend the thunderbolt.

10.92.d: सूरश्चिदा हरितो अस्य रीरमदिन्द्रादा कश्चिद भयतेतवीयसः | भीमस्य वर्ष्णो जठरादभिश्वसो दिवे-दिवेसहुरि सतन्नबाधितः ||
10.92.e: Even the Sun's Bay Coursers hath lie held in check: each one fears Indra as the mightiest of all.  Unhindered, from the air's vault thunders day by day the loud triumphant breathing of the fearful Bull.

10.92.d: सतोमं वो अद्य रुद्राय शिक्वसे कषयद्वीराय नमसादिदिष्टन | येभिः शिवः सववानेवयावभिर्दिवःसिषक्ति सवयशा निकामभिः ||
10.92.e: With humble adoration show this day your song of praise to mighty Rudra, Ruler of the brave:  With whom, the Eager Ones, going their ordered course, he comes from heaven Self-bright, auspicious, strong to guard.

10.92.d: ते हि परजाया अभरन्त वि शरवो बर्हस्पतिर्व्र्षभःसोमजामयः | यज्ञैरथर्वा परथमो वि धारयद देवादक्षैर्भ्र्गवः सं चिकित्रिरे ||
10.92.e: For these have spread abroad the fame of human kind, the Bull Bṛhaspati and Soma's brotherhood.  Atharvan first by sacrifices made men sure: through skill the Bhṛgus were esteemed of all as Gods.

10.92.d: ते हि दयावाप्र्थिवी भूरिरेतसा नराशंसश्चतुरङगोयमो.अदितिः | देवस्त्वष्टा दरविणोदा रभुक्षणः पररोदसी मरुतो विष्णुरर्हिरे ||
10.92.e: For these, the Earth and Heaven with their abundant seed, four-bodied Narāśaṁsa, Yama, Aditi,  God Tvaṣṭar Wealth-bestower, the Ṛbhukṣaṇas, Rodasī, Maruts, Viṣṇu, claim and merit praise.

10.92.d: उत सय न उशिजामुर्विया कविरहिः शर्णोतु बुध्न्योहवीमनि | सूर्यामासा विचरन्ता दिविक्षिता धियाशमीनहुषी अस्य बोधतम ||
10.92.e: And may he too give car, the Sage, from far away, the Dragon of the Deep, to this our yearning call.  Ye Sun and Moon who dwell in heaven and move in turn, and with your thought, O Earth and Sky, observe this well.

10.92.d: पर नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्यो.अपां नपादवतुवायुरिष्टये | आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि शरुतम ||
10.92.e: Dear to all Gods, may Pūṣan guard the ways we go, the Waters’ child and Vāyu help us to success.  Sing lauds for your great bliss to Wind, the breath of all: ye Aśvins prompt to hear, hear this upon your way.

10.92.d: विशामासामभयानामधिक्षितं गीर्भिरु सवयशसंग्र्णीमसि | गनाभिर्विश्वाभिरदितिमनर्वणमक्तोर्युवानं नर्मणा अधा पतिम ||
10.92.e: With hymns of praise we sing him who is throned as Lord over these fearless tribes, the Self-resplendent One.  We praise Night's youthful Lord benevolent to men, the foeless One, the free, with all celestial Dames.

10.92.d: रेभदत्र जनुषा पूर्वो अङगिरा गरावाण ऊर्ध्वा अभिचक्षुरध्वरम | येभिर्विहाया अभवद विचक्षणःपाथः सुमेकं सवधितिर्वनन्वति ||
10.92.e: By reason of his birth here Aṅgiras first sang: the pressing-stones upraised beheld the sacrifice-  The stones through which the Sage became exceeding vast, and the sharp axe obtains in fight the beauteous place.

10.93.d: महि दयावाप्र्थिवी भूतमुर्वी नारी यह्वी न रोदसीसदं नः | तेभिर्नः पातं सह्यस एभिर्नः पातंशूषणि ||
10.93.e: MIGHTY are ye, and far-extended, Heaven and Earth: both Worlds are evermore to us like two young Dames.  Guard us thereby from stronger foe; guard us hereby to give us strength.

10.93.d: यज्ञे-यज्ञे स मर्त्यो देवान सपर्यति | यः सुम्नैर्दीर्घश्रुत्तम आविवासत्येनान ||
10.93.e: In each succeeding sacrifice that mortal honoureth the Gods,  He who, most widely known and famed for happiness, inviteth them.

10.93.d: विश्वेषामिरज्यवो देवानां वार्महः | विश्वे हिविश्वमहसो विश्वे यज्ञेषु यज्ञियाः ||
10.93.e: Ye who are Rulers over all, great is your sovran power as Gods.  Ye all possess all majesty: all must be served in sacrifice.

10.93.d: ते घा राजानो अम्र्तस्य मन्द्रा अर्यमा मित्रो वरुणःपरिज्मा | कद रुद्रो नर्णां सतुतो मरुतः पूषणो भगः ||
10.93.e: These are the joyous Kings of Immortality, Parijman, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa.  What else is Rudra, praised of men? the Maruts, Bhaga, Pūṣaṇa?

10.93.d: उत नो नक्तमपां वर्षण्वसू सूर्यामासा सदनायसधन्या | सचा यत साद्येषामहिर्बुध्नेषु बुध्न्यः ||
10.93.e: Come also to our dwelling, Lords of ample wealth, common partakers of our waters, Sun and Moon,  When the great Dragon of the Deep hath settled down upon their floors.

10.93.d: उत नो देवावश्विना शुभस पती धामभिर्मित्रावरुणाुरुष्यताम | महः स राय एषते.अति धन्वेव दुरिता ||
10.93.e: And let the Aśvins, Lords of splendour, set us free,—both Gods, and, with their Laws, Mitra and Varuṇa.  Through woes, as over desert lands, he speeds to ample opulence.

10.93.d: उत नो रुद्रा चिन मर्ळतामश्विना विश्वे देवासो रथस्पतिर्भगः | रभुर्वाज रभुक्षणः परिज्मा विश्ववेदसः ||
10.93.e: Yea, let the Aśvins Twain he gracious unto us, even Rudras, and all Gods, Bhaga, Rathaspati;  Parijman, Ṛbhu, Vāja, O Lords of all wealth Ṛbhukṣaṇas.

10.93.d: रभुरभुक्षा रभुर्विधतो मद आ ते हरी जूजुवानस्यवाजिना | दुष्टरं यस्य साम चिद रधग यज्ञो नमानुषः ||
10.93.e: Prompt is Ṛbhukṣan, prompt the worshipper's strong drink: may thy fleet Bay Steeds, thine who speedest on, approach.  Not mans but God's is sacrifice whose psalm is unassailable.

10.93.d: कर्धी नो अह्रयो देव सवितः स च सतुषे मघोनाम | सहो नैन्द्रो वह्निभिर्न्येषां चर्षणीनां चक्रं रश्मिं नयोयुवे ||
10.93.e: O God Savitar, harmed by none, lauded, give us a place among wealthy princes.  With his Car-steeds at once 'hath our Indra guided the reins and the car of these men.

10.93.d: ऐषु दयावाप्र्थिवी धातं महदस्मे वीरेषु विश्वचर्षणिश्रवः | पर्क्षं वाजस्य सातये पर्क्षं रायोततुर्वणे ||
10.93.e: To these men present here, O Heaven and Earth, to us grant lofty fame extending over all mankind.  Give us a steed to win us strength, a steed with wealth for victory.

10.93.d: एतं शंसमिन्द्रास्मयुष टवं कूचित सन्तं सहसावन्नभिष्टये सदा पाह्यभिष्टये | मेदतां वेदता वसो ||
10.93.e: This speaker, Indra—for thou art our Friend—wherever he may be, guard thou, Victor! for help, ever for help  Thy wisdom, Vasu! prosper him.

10.93.d: एतं मे सतोमं तना न सूर्ये दयुतद्यामानं वाव्र्धन्तन्र्णाम | संवननं नाश्व्यं तष्टेवानपच्युतम ||
10.93.e: So have they strengthened this mine hymn which seems to take its bright path to the Sun, and reconciles the men:  Thus forms a carpenter the yoke of horses, not to be displaced.

10.93.d: वावर्त येषां राया युक्तैषां हिरण्ययी | नेमधितान पौंस्या वर्थेव विष्टान्ता ||
10.93.e: Whose chariot-seat hath come again laden with wealth and bright with gold,  Lightly, with piercing ends, as ’twere two ranks of heroes ranged for fight.

10.93.d: पर तद दुःशीमे पर्थवाने वेने पर रामे वोचमसुरेमघवत्सु | ये युक्त्वाय पञ्च शतास्मयु पथा विश्राव्येषाम ||
10.93.e: This to Duḥśīma Pṛthavāna have I sung, to Vena, Rama, to the nobles, and the King.  They yoked five hundred, and their love of us was famed upon their way.

10.93.d: अधीन नवत्र सप्ततिं च सप्त च | सद्यो दिदिष्ट तान्वःसद्यो दिदिष्ट पार्थ्यः सद्यो दिदिष्ट मायवः ||
10.93.e: Besides, they showed us seven-and-seventy horses here.  Tānva at once displayed his gift, Pārthya at once displayed his gift; and straightway Māyava showed his.

10.94.d: परैते वदन्तु पर वयं वदाम गरावभ्यो वाचं वदतावदद्भ्यः | यदद्रयः पर्वताः साकमाशवः शलोकंघोषं भरथेन्द्राय सोमिनः ||
10.94.e: LET these speak loudly forth; let us speak out aloud: to the loud speaking Pressing-stones address the speech;  When, rich with Soma juice, Stones of the mountain, ye, united, swift to Indra bring the sound of praise.

10.94.d: एते वदन्ति शतवत सहस्रवदभि करन्दन्ति हरितेभिरासभिः | विष्ट्वी गरावाणः सुक्र्तः सुक्र्त्यया होतुश्चित पूर्वे हविरद्यमाशत ||
10.94.e: They speak out like a hundred, like a thousand men: they cry aloud to us with their green-tinted mouths,  While, pious Stones, they ply their task with piety, and, even before the Hotar, taste the offered food.

10.94.d: एते वदन्त्यविदन्नना मधु नयूङखयन्ते अधि पक्वामिषि | वर्क्षस्य शाखामरुणस्य बप्सतस्ते सूभर्वाव्र्षभाः परेमराविषुः ||
10.94.e: Loudly they speak, for they have found the savoury meath: they make a humming sound over the meat prepared.  As they devour the branch of the Red-coloured Tree, these, the well-pastured Bulls, have uttered bellowings.

10.94.d: बर्हद वदन्ति मदिरेण मन्दिनेन्द्रं करोशन्तो.अविदन्ननामधु | संरभ्या धीराः सवस्र्भिरनर्तिषुराघोषयन्तः पर्थिवीमुपब्दिभिः ||
10.94.e: They cry aloud, with strong exhilarating drink, calling on Indra now, for they have found the meath.  Bold, with the sisters they have danced, embraced by them, making the earth reecho with their ringing sound.

10.94.d: सुपर्णा वाचमक्रतोप दयव्याखरे कर्ष्णा इषिरानर्तिषुः | नयं नि यन्त्युपरस्य निष्क्र्तं पुरू रेतोदधिरे सूर्यश्वितः ||
10.94.e: The Eagles have sent forth their cry aloft in heaven; in the sky's vault the dark impetuous ones have danced.  Then downward to the nether stone's fixt place they sink, and, splendid as the Sun, effuse their copious stream.

10.94.d: उग्रा इव परवहन्तः समायमुः साकं युक्ता वर्षणोबिभ्रतो धुरः | यच्छ्वसन्तो जग्रसाना अराविषुःश्र्ण्व एषां परोथथो अर्वतामिव ||
10.94.e: Like strong ones drawing, they have put forth all their strength: the Bulls, harnessed together, bear the chariot-poles.  When they have bellowed, panting, swallowing their food, the sound of their loud snorting is like that of steeds.

10.94.d: दशावनिभ्यो दशकक्ष्येभ्यो दशयोक्त्रेभ्यो दशयोजनेभ्यः | दशाभीशुभ्यो अर्चताजरेभ्यो दश धुरो दश युक्तावहद्भ्यः ||
10.94.e: To these who have ten workers and a tenfold girth, to these who have ten yoke-straps and ten binding thongs,  To these who bear ten reins, the eternal, sing ye praise, to these who bear ten car-poles, ten when they are yoked.

10.94.d: ते अद्रयो दशयन्त्रास आशवस्तेषामाधानं पर्येतिहर्यतम | त ऊ सुतस्य सोम्यस्यान्धसो.अंशोः पीयूषम्प्रथमस्य भेजिरे ||
10.94.e: These Stones with ten conductors, rapid in their course, with lovely revolution travel round and round.  They have been first to drink the flowing Soma juice, first to enjoy the milky fluid of the stalk.

10.94.d: ते सोमादो हरी इन्द्रस्य निंसते.अंशुं दुहन्तो अध्यासतेगवि | तेभिर्दुग्धं पपिवान सोम्यं मध्विन्द्रो वर्धतेप्रथते वर्षायते ||
10.94.e: These Soma-eaters kiss Indra's Bay-coloured Steeds: draining. the stalk they sit upon the ox's hide.  Indra, when he hath drunk Soma-meath drawn by them, waxes in strength, is famed, is mighty as a Bull.

10.94.d: वर्षा वो अंशुर्न किला रिषाथनेलावन्तः सदमित्स्थनाशिताः | रैवत्येव महसा चारव सथन यस्यग्रावाणो अजुषध्वमध्वरम ||
10.94.e: Strong is your stalk; ye, verily, never shall be harmed; ye have refreshment, ye are ever satisfied.  Fair are ye, as it were, through splendour of his wealth, his in whose sacrifice, O Stones, ye find delight.

10.94.d: तर्दिला अत्र्दिलासो अद्रयो.अश्रमणा अश्र्थिता अम्र्त्यवः | अनातुरा अजरा सथामविष्णवः सुपीवसो अत्र्षितात्र्ष्णजः ||
10.94.e: Bored deep, but not pierced through with holes, are ye, O Stones, not loosened, never weary, and exempt from death,  Eternal, undiseased, moving in sundry ways, unthirsting, full of fatness, void of all desire.

10.94.d: धरुवा एव वः पितरो युगे-युगे कषेमकामासः सदसो नयुञ्जते | अजुर्यासो हरिषाचो हरिद्रव आ दयां रवेणप्र्थिवीमशुश्रवुः ||
10.94.e: Your fathers, verily, stand firm from age to age: they, loving rest, are not dissevered from their seat.  Untouched by time, ne’er lacking green plants and green trees, they with their voice have caused the heavens and earth to hear.

10.94.d: तदिद वदन्त्यद्रयो विमोचने यामन्नञ्जस्पा इव घेदुपब्दिभिः | वपन्तो बीजमिव धान्याक्र्तः पर्ञ्चन्तिसोमं न मिनन्ति बप्सतः ||
10.94.e: This, this the Stones proclaim, what time they are disjoined, and when with ringing sounds they move and drink the balm.  Like tillers of the ground when they are sowing seed, they mix the Soma, nor, devouring, minish it.

10.94.d: सुते अध्वरे अधि वाचमक्रता करीळयो न मातरन्तुदन्तः | वि षू मुञ्चा सुषुवुषो मनीषां वि वर्तन्तामद्रयश्चायमानाः ||
10.94.e: They have raised high their voice for juice, for sacrifice, striking the Mother earth as though they danced thereon.  So loose thou too his thought who hath effused the sap, and let the Stones which we are honouring be disjoined.

10.95.d: हये जाये मनसा तिष्ठ घोरे वचांसि मिश्राक्र्णवावहै नु | न नौ मन्त्रा अनुदितास एते मयस करन्परतरे चनाहन ||
10.95.e: Ho there, my consort! Stay, thou fierce-souled lady, and let us reason for a while together.  Such thoughts as these of ours, while yet unspoken in days gone by have never brought us comfort.

10.95.d: किमेता वाचा कर्णवा तवाहं पराक्रमिषमुषसामग्रियेव | पुरूरवः पुनरस्तं परेहि दुरापना वातैवाहमस्मि ||
10.95.e: What am I now to do with this thy saying? I have gone from thee like the first of Mornings.  Purūravas, return thou to thy dwelling: I, like the wind, am difficult to capture.

10.95.d: इषुर्न शरिय इषुधेरसना गोषाः शतसा न रंहिः | अवीरे करतौ वि दविद्युतन नोरा न मायुं चितयन्तधुनयः ||
10.95.e: Like a shaft sent for glory from the quiver, or swift-steed winning cattle winning hundreds.  The lightning seemed to flash, as cowards planned it. The minstrels bleated like a lamb in trouble.

10.95.d: सा वसु दधती शवशुराय वय उषो यदि वष्ट्यन्तिग्र्हात | अस्तं ननक्षे यस्मिञ्चाकन दिवा नक्तंश्नथिता वैतसेन ||
10.95.e: Giving her husband's father life and riches, from the near dwelling, when her lover craved her,  She sought the home wherein she found her pleasure, accepting day and night her lord's embraces.

10.95.d: तरिः सम माह्नः शनथयो वैतसेनोत सम मे.अव्यत्यैप्र्णासि | पुरूरवो.अनु ते केतमायं राजा मे वीर तन्वस्तदासीः ||
10.95.e: Thrice in the day didst thou embrace thy consort, though coldly she received thy fond caresses.  To thy desires, Purūravas, I yielded: so wast thou king, O hero, of my body.

10.95.d: या सुजूर्णिः शरेणिः सुम्नापिर्ह्रदेचक्षुर्न गरन्थिनीचरण्युः | ता अञ्जयो.अरुणयो न सस्रुः शरिये गावो नधेनवो.अनवन्त ||
10.95.e: The maids Sujirni, Sreni, Sumne-api, Charanyu, Granthini, and Hradecaksus,—  These like red kine have hastened forth, the bright ones, and like milch-cows have lowed in emulation.

10.95.d: समस्मिञ जायमान आसत गना उतेमवर्धन नद्यःस्वगूर्ताः | महे यत तवा पुरूरवो रणायावर्धयन्दस्युहत्याय देवाः ||
10.95.e: While he was born the Dames sate down together, the Rivers with free kindness gave him nurture;  And then, Purūravas, the Gods increased thee for mighty battle, to destroy the Dasyus.

10.95.d: सचा यदासु जहतीष्वत्कममानुषीषु मानुषो निषेवे | अप सम मत तरसन्ती न भुज्युस्ता अत्रसन रथस्प्र्शोनाश्वाः ||
10.95.e: When I, a mortal, wooed to mine embraces these heavenly nymphs who laid aside their raiment,  Like a scared snake they fled from me in terror, like chariot horses when the car has touched them.

10.95.d: यदासु मर्तो अम्र्तासु निस्प्र्क सं कषोणीभिः करतुभिर्नप्र्ङकते | ता आतयो न तन्वः शुम्भत सवा अश्वासो नक्रीळयो दन्दशानाः ||
10.95.e: When, loving these Immortal Ones, the mortal hath converse with the nymphs as they allow him.  Like swans they show the beauty of their bodies, like horses in their play they bite and nibble.

10.95.d: विद्युन न या पतन्ती दविद्योद भरन्ती मे अप्या काम्यानि | जनिष्टो अपो नर्यः सुजातः परोर्वशी तिरत दीर्घमायुः ||
10.95.e: She who flashed brilliant as the falling lightning brought me delicious presents from the waters.  Now from the flood be born a strong young hero May Uruvasi prolong her life for ever

10.95.d: जज्ञिष इत्था गोपीथ्याय हि दधाथ तत पुरूरवो मोजः | अशासं तवा विदुषी सस्मिन्नहन न म आश्र्णोःकिमभुग वदासि ||
10.95.e: Thy birth hath made me drink from earthly milch-kine: this power, Purūravas, hast thou vouchsafed me.  I knew, and, warned thee, on that day. Thou wouldst not hear me. What sayest thou, when naught avails thee?

10.95.d: कदा सूनुः पितरं जात इछाच्चक्रन नाश्रु वर्तयद्विजानन | को दम्पती समनसा वि यूयोदध यदग्निःश्वशुरेषु दीदयत ||
10.95.e: When will the son be born and seek his father? Mourner-like, will he weep when first he knows him?  Who shall divide the accordant wife and husband, while fire is shining with thy consort's parents?

10.95.d: परति बरवाणि वर्तयते अश्रु चक्रन न करन्ददाध्येशिवायै | पर तत ते हिनवा यत ते अस्मे परेह्यस्तं नहिमूर मापः ||
10.95.e: I will console him when his tears are falling: he shall not weep and cry for care that blesses.  That which is thine, between us, will I send thee. Go home again, thou fool;ṭhou hast not won me.

10.95.d: सुदेवो अद्य परपतेदनाव्र्त परावतं परमां गन्तवा उ | अधा शयीत निरतेरुपस्थे.अधैनं वर्का रभसासोद्युः ||
10.95.e: Thy lover shall flee forth this day for ever, to seek, without return, the farthest distance.  Then let his bed be in Destruction's bosom, and there let fierce rapacious wolves devour him.

10.95.d: पुरूरवो मा मर्था मा पर पप्तो मा तवा वर्कासो अशिवास उक्षन | न वै सत्रैणानि सख्यानि सन्ति सालाव्र्काणांह्र्दयान्येता ||
10.95.e: Nay, do not die, Purūravas, nor vanish: let not the evil-omened wolves devour thee.  With women there can be no lasting friendship: hearts of hyenas are the hearts of women.

10.95.d: यद विरूपाचरं मर्त्येष्ववसं रात्रीः शरदश्चतस्रः | घर्तस्य सतोकं सक्र्दह्न आश्नां तादेवेदन्तात्र्पाणा चरामि ||
10.95.e: When amid men in altered shape I sojourned, and through four autumns spent the nights among them,  I tasted once a day a drop of butter; and even now with that am I am contented.

10.95.d: अन्तरिक्षप्रां रजसो विमानीमुप शिक्षाम्युर्वशींवसिष्ठः | उप तवा रातिः सुक्र्तस्य तिष्ठान नि वर्तस्वह्र्दयं तप्यते मे ||
10.95.e: I, her best love, call Urvasi to meet me, her who fills air and measures out the region.  Let the gift brought by piety approach thee. Turn thou to me again: my heart is troubled.

10.95.d: इति तवा देवा इम आहुरैळ यथेमेतद भवसिम्र्त्युबन्धुः | परजा ते देवान हविषा यजाति सवर्ग उ तवमपि मादयासे ||
10.95.e: Thus speak these Gods to thee, O son of Iḷā: As death hath verily got thee for his subject,  Thy sons shall serve the Gods with their oblation, and thou, moreover, shalt rejoice in Svarga.

10.96.d: पर ते महे विदथे शंसिषं हरी पर ते वन्वे वनुषोहर्यतं मदम | घर्तं न यो हरिभिश्चारु सेचत आ तवाविशन्तु हरिवर्पसं गिरः ||
10.96.e: In the great synod will I laud thy two Bay Steeds: I prize the sweet strong drink of thee the Warrior-God,  His who pours lovely oil as ’twere with yellow drops. Let my songs enter thee whose form hath golden tints.

10.96.d: हरिं हि योनिमभि ये समस्वरन हिन्वन्तो हरी दिव्यंयथा सदः | आ यं पर्णन्ति हरिभिर्न धेनव इन्द्रायशूषं हरिवन्तमर्चत ||
10.96.e: Ye who in concert sing unto the goldhued place, like Bay Steeds driving onward to the heavenly seat,  For Indra laud ye strength allied with Tawny Steeds, laud him whom cows content as ’twere with yellow drops.

10.96.d: सो अस्य वज्रो हरितो य आयसो हरिर्निकामो हरिरागभस्त्योः | दयुम्नी सुशिप्रो हरिमन्युसायक इन्द्रे नि रूपाहरिता मिमिक्षिरे ||
10.96.e: His is that thunderbolt, of iron, goldenhued, gold-coloured, very dear, and yellow in his arms;  Bright with strong teeth, destroying with its tawny rage. In Indra are set fast all forms of golden hue.

10.96.d: दिवि न केतुरधि धायि हर्यतो विव्यचद वज्रो हरितो नरंह्या | तुददहिं हरिशिप्रो य आयसः सहस्रशोकाभवद धरिम्भरः ||
10.96.e: As if a lovely ray were laid upon the sky, the golden thunderbolt spread out as in a race.  That iron bolt with yellow jaw smote Ahi down. A thousand flames had he who bore the tawny-hued.

10.96.d: तवं-तवमहर्यथा उपस्तुतः पूर्वेभिरिन्द्र हरिकेशयज्वभिः | तवं हर्यसि तव विश्वमुक्थ्यमसामि राधोहरिजात हर्यतम ||
10.96.e: Thou, thou, when praised by men who sacrificed of old. hadst pleasure in their lauds, O Indra golden-haired.  All that befits thy song of praise thou welcornest, the perfect pleasant gift, O Golden-hued from birth.

10.96.d: ता वज्रिणं मन्दिनं सतोम्यं मद इन्द्रं रथे वहतोहर्यता हरी | पुरूण्यस्मै सवनानि हर्यत इन्द्रायसोमा हरयो दधन्विरे ||
10.96.e: These two dear Bays bring hither Indra on his car, Thunder-armed, joyous, meet for laud, to drink his fill.  Many libations flow for him who loveth them: to Indra have the gold-hued Soma juices run.

10.96.d: अरं कामाय हरयो दधन्विरे सथिराय हिन्वन हरयो हरीतुरा | अर्वद्भिर्यो हरिभिर्जोषमीयते सो अस्य कामंहरिवन्तमानशे ||
10.96.e: Tle gold-hued drops have flowed to gratify his wish: the yellow dro s have urged the swift Bays to the Strong.  He who speeds on with Bay Steeds even as he lists hath satisfied his longing for the golden drops.

10.96.d: हरिश्मशारुर्हरिकेश आयसस्तुरस्पेये यो हरिपावर्धत | अर्वद्भिर्यो हरिभिर्वाजिनीवसुरति विश्वादुरिता पारिषद धरी ||
10.96.e: At the swift draught the Soma-drinker waxed in might, the Iron One with yellow beard and yellow hair.  He, Lord of Tawny Coursers, Lord of fleet-foot Mares, will bear his Bay Steeds safely over all distress.

10.96.d: सरुवेव यस्य हरिणी विपेततुः शिप्रे वाजाय हरिणीदविध्वतः | पर यत कर्ते चमसे मर्म्र्जद धरी पीत्वामदस्य हयतस्याधसः ||
10.96.e: His yellow-coloured jaws, like ladles move apart, what time, for strength, he makes the yellow-tinted stir,  When, while the bowl stands there, he grooms his Tawny Steeds, when he hath drunk strong drink, the sweet juice that he loves.

10.96.d: उत सम सद्म हर्यतस्य पस्त्योरत्यो न वाजं हरिवानचिक्रदत | मही चिद धि धिषणाहर्यदोजसा बर्हद वयोदधिषे हर्यतश्चिदा ||
10.96.e: Yea, to the Dear One's seat in homes of heaven and earth the Bay Steeds' Lord hath whinnied like a horse for food.  Then the great wish hath seized upon him mightily, and the Beloved One hath gained high power of life,

10.96.d: आ रोदसी हर्यमाणो महित्वा नव्यं-नव्यं हर्यसि मन्मनु परियम | पर पस्त्यमसुर हर्यतं गोराविष्क्र्धि हरयेसूर्याय ||
10.96.e: Thou, comprehending with thy might the earth and heaven, acceptest the dear hymn for ever new and new.  O Asura, disclose thou and make visible the Cow's beloved home to the bright golden Sun.

10.96.d: आ तवा हर्यन्तं परयुजो जनानां रथे वहन्तु हरिशिप्रमिन्द्र | पिबा यथा परतिभ्र्तस्य मध्वो हर्यन यज्ञंसधमादे दशोणिम ||
10.96.e: O Indra, let the eager wishes of the folk bring thee, delightful, golden-visored, on thy car,  That, pleased with sacrifice wherein ten fingers toil, thou mayest, at the feast, drink of our offered meath.

10.96.d: अपाः पूर्वेषां हरिवः सुतानामथो इदं सवनंकेवलं ते | ममद्धि सोमं मधुमन्तमिन्द्र सत्रा वर्षञ्जठर आ वर्षस्व ||
10.96.e: Juices aforetime, Lord of Bays, thou drankest; and thine especially is this libation.  Gladden thee, Indra, with the meath-rich Soma: pour it down ever, Mighty One! within thee.

10.97.d: या ओषधीः पूर्वा जाता देवेभ्यस्त्रियुगं पुरा | मनैनु बभ्रूणामहं शतं धामानि सप्त च ||
10.97.e: HERBS that sprang up in time of old, three ages earlier than the Gods,—  Of these, whose hue is brown, will I declare the hundred powers and seven.

10.97.d: शतं वो अम्ब धामानि सहस्रमुत वो रुहः | अधाशतक्रत्वो यूयमिमं मे अगदं कर्त ||
10.97.e: Ye, Mothers, have a hundred homes, yea, and a thousand are your growths.  Do ye who have a thousand powers free this my patient from disease.

10.97.d: ओषधीः परति मोदध्वं पुष्पवतीः परसूवरीः | अश्वािव सजित्वरीर्वीरुधः पारयिष्ण्वः ||
10.97.e: Be glad and joyful in the Plants, both blossoming and bearing fruit,  Plants that will lead us to success like mares who conquer in the race.

10.97.d: ओषधीरिति मातरस्तद वो देवीरुप बरुवे | सनेयमश्वंगां वास आत्मानं तव पूरुष ||
10.97.e: Plants, by this name I speak to you, Mothers, to you the Goddesses:  Steed, cow, and garment may I win, win back thy very self, O man.

10.97.d: अश्वत्थे वो निषदनं पर्णे वो वसतिष कर्ता | गोभाज इत्किलासथ यत सनवथ पूरुषम ||
10.97.e: The Holy Fig tree is your home, your mansion is the Parna tree:  Winners of cattle shali ye be if ye regain for me this man.

10.97.d: यत्रौषधीः समग्मत राजानः समिताविव | विप्रः सौच्यते भिषग रक्षोहामीवचातनः ||
10.97.e: He who hath store of Herbs at hand like Kings amid a crowd of men,—  Physician is that sage's name, fiend-slayer, chaser of disease.

10.97.d: अश्वावतीं सोमावतीमूर्जयन्तीमुदोजसम | आवित्सिसर्वा ओषधीरस्मा अरिष्टतातये ||
10.97.e: Herbs rich in Soma, rich in steeds, in nourishments, in strengthening power,—  All these have I provided here, that this man may be whole again.

10.97.d: उच्छुष्मा ओषधीनां गावो गोष्ठादिवेरते | धनंसनिष्यन्तीनामात्मानं तव पूरुष ||
10.97.e: The healing virtues of the Plants stream forth like cattle from the stall,—  Plants that shall win me store of wealth, and save thy vital breath, O man.

10.97.d: इष्क्र्तिर्नाम वो माताथो यूयं सथ निष्क्र्तीः | सीराःपतत्र्णी सथन यदामयति निष कर्थ ||
10.97.e: Reliever is your mother's name, and hence Restorers are ye called.  Rivers are ye with wings that fly: keep far whatever brings disease.

10.97.d: अति विश्वाः परिष्ठा सतेन इव वरजमक्रमुः | ओषधीःप्राचुच्यवुर्यत किं च तन्वो रपः ||
10.97.e: Over all fences have they passed, as steals a thief into the fold.  The Plants have driven from the frame whatever malady was there.

10.97.d: यदिमा वाजयन्नहमोषधीर्हस्त आदधे | आत्मायक्ष्मस्य नश्यति पुरा जीवग्र्भो यथा ||
10.97.e: When, bringing back the vanished strength, I hold these herbs within my hand,  The spirit of disease departs ere he can seize upon the life.

10.97.d: यस्यौषधीः परसर्पथाङगम-अञ्गं परुष-परुः | ततोयक्ष्मं वि बाधध्व उग्रो मध्यमशीरिव ||
10.97.e: He through whose frame, O Plants, ye creep member by member, joint by joint,—  From him ye drive away disease like some strong arbiter of strife.

10.97.d: साकं यक्ष्म पर पत चाषेण किकिदीविना | साकंवातस्य धराज्या साकं नश्य निहाकया ||
10.97.e: Fly, Spirit of Disease, begone, with the blue jay and kingfisher.  Fly with the wind's impetuousspeed, vanish together with the storm.

10.97.d: अन्या वो अन्यामवत्वन्यान्यस्या उपावत | ताः सर्वाःसंविदाना इदं मे परावता वचः ||
10.97.e: Help every one the other, lend assistance each of you to each,  All of you be accordant, give furtherance to this speech of mine.

10.97.d: याः फलिनीर्या अफला अपुष्पा याश्च पुष्पिणीः | बर्हस्पतिप्रसूतास्ता नो मुञ्चन्त्वंहसः ||
10.97.e: Let fruitful Plants, and fruitless, those that blossom, and the blossomless,  Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, release us from our pain and grief;

10.97.d: मुञ्चन्तु मा शपथ्यादथो वरुण्यादुत | अथो यमस्यपड्बीशात सर्वस्माद देवकिल्बिषात ||
10.97.e: Release me from the curse's plague and woe that comes from Varuṇa;  Free me from Yama's fetter, from sin and offence against the Gods.

10.97.d: अवपतन्तीरवदन दिव ओषधयस परि | यं जीवमश्नवामहै न स रिष्याति पूरुषः ||
10.97.e: What time, descending from the sky, the Plants flew earthward, thus they spake:  No evil shall befall the man whom while he liveth we pervade,

10.97.d: या ओषधीः सोमराज्ञीर्बह्वीः शतविचक्षणाः | तासां तवमस्युत्तमारं कामाय शं हर्दे ||
10.97.e: Of all the many Plants whose King is, Soma, Plants of hundred forms,  Thou art the Plant most excellent, prompt to the wish, sweet to the heart.

10.97.d: या ओषधीः सोमराज्ञीर्विष्ठिताः पर्थिवीमनु | बर्हस्पतिप्रसूता अस्यै सं दत्त वीर्यम ||
10.97.e: O all ye various Herbs whose King is Soma, that o’erspread the earth,  Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, combine your virtue in this Plant.

10.97.d: मा वो रिषत खनिता यस्मै चाहं खनामि वः | दविपच्चतुष्पदस्माकं सर्वमस्त्वनातुरम ||
10.97.e: Unharmed be he who digs you up, unharmed the man for whom I dig:  And let no malady attack biped or quadruped of ours.

10.97.d: याश्चेदमुपश्र्ण्वन्ति याश्च दूरं परागताः | सर्वाः संगत्य वीरुधो.अस्यै सं दत्त वीर्यम ||
10.97.e: All Plants that hear this speech, and those that have departed far away,  Come all assembled and confer your healing power upon this Herb.

10.97.d: ओषधयः सं वदन्ते सोमेन सह राज्ञा | यस्मै कर्णोतिब्राह्मणस्तं राजन पारयामसि ||
10.97.e: With Soma as their Sovran Lord the Plants hold colloquy and say:  O King, we save from death the man whose cure a Brahman undertakes.

10.97.d: तवमुत्तमास्योषधे तव वर्क्षा उपस्तयः | उपस्तिरस्तुसो.अस्माकं यो अस्मानभिदासति ||
10.97.e: Most excellent of all art thou, O Plant thy vassals are the trees.  Let him be subject to our power, the man who seeks to injure us.

10.98.d: बर्हस्पते परति मे देवतामिहि मित्रो वा यद वरुणो वासिपूषा | आदित्यैर्वा यद वसुभिर्मरुत्वान स पर्जन्यंशन्तनवे वर्षाय ||
10.98.e: COME, be thou Mitra, Varuṇa, or Pūṣan, come, O Bṛhaspati, to mine oblation:  With Maruts, Vasus, or Ādityas, make thou Parjanya pour for Santanu his rain-drops.

10.98.d: आ देवो दूतो अजिरश्चिकित्वान तवद देवापे अभि मामगछत | परतीचीनः परति मामा वव्र्त्स्व दधामि ते दयुमतींवाचमासन ||
10.98.e: The God, intelligent, the speedy envoy whom thou hast sent hath come to me, Devapi:  Address thyself to me and turn thee hither within thy lips will I put brilliant language.

10.98.d: अस्मे धेहि दयुमतीं वाचमासन बर्हस्पते अनमीवामिषिराम | यया वर्ष्टिं शन्तनवे वनाव दिवो दरप्सोमधुमाना विवेश ||
10.98.e: Within my mouth, Bṛhaspati, deposit speech lucid, vigorous, and free from weakness,  Thereby to win for Santanu the rain-fall. The meath-rich drop from heaven hath passed within it.

10.98.d: आ नो दरप्सा मधुमन्तो विशन्त्विन्द्र देह्यधिरथंसहस्रम | नि षीद होत्रं रतुथा यजस्व देवान देवापेहविषा सपर्य ||
10.98.e: Let the sweet drops descend on us, O Indra: give us enough to lade a thousand wagons.  Sit to thy Hotar task; pay worship duly, and serve the Gods, Devapi, with oblation.

10.98.d: आर्ष्टिषेणो होत्रं रषिर्निषीदन देवापिर्देवसुमतिंचिकित्वान | स उत्तरस्मादधरं समुद्रमपो दिव्या अस्र्जद्वर्ष्या अभि ||
10.98.e: Knowing the God's good-will, Devapi, Ṛṣi, the son of Rstisena, sate as Hotar.  He hath brought down from heaven's most lofty summit the ocean of the rain, celestial waters.

10.98.d: अस्मिन समुद्रे अध्युत्तरस्मिन्नापो देवेभिर्निव्र्ता अतिष्ठन | ता अद्रवन्नार्ष्टिषेणेन सर्ष्टा देवापिना परेषिताम्र्क्षिणीषु ||
10.98.e: Gathered together in that highest ocean, the waters stood by deities obstructed.  They burried down set free by Arstisena, in gaping clefts, urged onward by Devapi.

10.98.d: यद देवापिः शन्तनवे पुरोहितो होत्राय वर्तः कर्पयन्नदीधेत | देवश्रुतं वर्ष्टिवनिं रराणो बर्हस्पतिर्वाचमस्मा अयछत ||
10.98.e: When as chief priest for Santanu, Devapi, chosen for Hotar's duty, prayed beseeching,  Graciously pleased Bṛhaspati vouchsafed him a voice that reached the Gods and won the waters.

10.98.d: यं तवा देवापिः शुशुचानो अग्न आर्ष्टिषेणो मनुष्यःसमीधे | विश्वेभिर्देवैरनुमद्यमानः पर पर्जन्यमीरया वर्ष्टिमन्तम ||
10.98.e: O Agni whom Devapi Arstisena, the mortal man, hath kindled in his glory,  Joying in him with all the Gods together, urge on the sender of the rain, Parjanya.

10.98.d: तवां पूर्व रषयो गीर्भिरायन तवामध्वरेषु पुरुहूतविश्वे | सहस्राण्यधिरथान्यस्मे आ नो यज्ञंरोहिदश्वोप याहि ||
10.98.e: All ancient Ṛṣis with their songs approached thee, even thee, O Much-invoked, at sacrifices.  We have provided wagon-loads in thousands: come to the solemn rite, Lord of Red Horses.

10.98.d: एतान्यग्ने नवतिर्नव तवे आहुतान्यधिरथा सहस्र | तेभिर्वर्धस्व तन्वः शूर पूर्वीर्दिवो नो वर्ष्टिमिषितोरिरीहि ||
10.98.e: The wagon-loads, the nine-and-ninety thousand, these have been offered up to thee, O Agni.  Hero, with these increase thy many bodies, and, stimulated, send us rain from heaven.

10.98.d: एतान्यग्ने नवतिं सहस्रा सं पर यछ वर्ष्ण इन्द्रायभागम | विद्वान पथ रतुशो देवयानानप्यौलानं दिविदेवेषु धेहि ||
10.98.e: Give thou these ninety thousand loads, O Agni, to Indra, to the Bull, to be his portion.  Knowing the paths which Deities duly travel, set mid the Gods in heaven Aulana also.

10.98.d: अग्ने बाधस्व वि मर्धो वि दुर्गहापामीवामपरक्षांसि सेध | अस्मात समुद्राद बर्हतो दिवो नो.अपाम्भूमानमुप नः सर्जेह ||
10.98.e: O Agni, drive afar our foes, our troubles chase malady away and wicked demons.  From this air-ocean, from the lofty heavens, send down on us a mighty flood of waters.

10.99.d: कं नश्चित्रमिषण्यसि चिकित्वान पर्थुग्मानं वाश्रंवाव्र्धध्यै | कत तस्य दातु शवसो वयुष्टौ तक्षद्वज्रं वर्त्रतुरमपिन्वत ||
10.99.e: WHAT Splendid One, Loud-voiced, Farstriding, dost thou, well knowing, urge us to exalt with praises?  What give we him? When his might dawned, he fashioned the Vṛtra-slaying bolt, and sent us waters.

10.99.d: स हि दयुता विद्युता वेति साम पर्थुं योनिमसुरत्वाससाद | स सनीळेभिः परसहानो अस्य भरातुर्न रतेसप्तथस्य मायाः ||
10.99.e: He goes to end his work with lightning flashes: wide is the seat his Asura glory gives him.  With his Companions, not without his Brother, he quells Saptatha's magic devices.

10.99.d: स वाजं यातापदुष्पदा यन सवर्षाता परि षदत्सनिष्यन | अनर्वा यच्छतदुरस्य वेदो घनञ्छिश्नदेवानभि वर्पसा भूत ||
10.99.e: On most auspicious path he goes to battle he toiled to win heaven's light, full fain to gain it;  He seized the hundred-gated castle's treasure by craft, unchecked, and slew the lustful demons.

10.99.d: स यह्व्यो.अवनीर्गोष्वर्वा जुहोति परधन्यासु सस्रिः | अपादो यत्र युज्यासो.अरथा दरोण्यश्वास ईरते घर्तंवाः ||
10.99.e: Fighting for kine, the prize of war, and I roaming among the berd be brings the young streams hither,  Where, footless, joined, without a car to bear them, with jars for steeds, they pour their flood like butter.

10.99.d: स रुद्रेभिरशस्तवार रभ्वा हित्वी गयमारेवद्यागात | वम्रस्य मन्ये मिथुना विवव्री अन्नमभीत्यारोदयन्मुषायन ||
10.99.e: Bold, unsolicited for wealth, with Rudras he came, the Blameless, having left his dwelling,  Came, seized the food of Vamra and his consort, and left the couple weeping and unsheltered.

10.99.d: स इद दासं तुवीरवं पतिर्दन षळक्षन्त्रिशीर्षाणं दमन्यत | अस्य तरितो नवोजसा वर्धानो विपावराहमयोग्रया हन ||
10.99.e: Lord of the dwelling, he subdued the demon who roared aloud, six-eyed and triple-headed.  Tṛta, made stronger by the might he lent him, struck down the boar with shaft whose point was iron.

10.99.d: स दरुह्वणे मनुष ऊर्ध्वसान आ साविषदर्शसानायशरुम | स नर्तमो नहुषो.अस्मत सुजातः पुरो.अभिनदर्हन्दस्युहत्ये ||
10.99.e: He raised himself on high and shot his arrow against the guileful and oppressive foeman.  Strong, glorious, manliest, for us he shattered the forts of Nabus when he slew the Dasyus.

10.99.d: सो अभ्रियो न यवस उदन्यन कषयाय गातुं विदन नो अस्मे | उप यत सीददिन्दुं शरीरैः शयेनो.अयोपाष्टिर्हन्तिदस्यून ||
10.99.e: He, like a cloud that rains upon the pasture, hath found for us the way to dwell in safety.  When the Hawk comes in body to the Soma, armed with his iron claws he slays the Dasyus.

10.99.d: स वराधतः शवसानेभिरस्य कुत्साय शुष्णं कर्पणेपरादात | अयं कविमनयच्छस्यमानमत्कं वो अस्यसनितोत नर्णाम ||
10.99.e: He with his potent Friends gave up the mighty, gave gusnia up to Kutsa for affliction.  He led the lauded Kavi, he delivered Atka as prey to him and to his heroes.

10.99.d: अयं दशस्यन नर्येभिरस्य दस्मो देवेभिर्वरुणो नमायी | अयं कनीन रतुपा अवेद्यमिमीताररुं यश्चतुष्पात ||
10.99.e: He, with his Gods who love mankind, the Wondrous, giving like Varuṇa who works with magic,  Was known, yet young as guardian of the seasons; and he quelled Araru, four-footed dernon.

10.99.d: अस्य सतोमेभिरौशिज रजिश्वा वरजं दरयद वर्षभेणपिप्रोः | सुत्वा यद यजतो दीदयद गीः पुर इयानो अभिवर्पसा भूत ||
10.99.e: Through lauds of him hath Auśija Ṛjiśvan burst, with the Mighty's aid, the stall of Pipru.  When the saint pressed the juice and shone as singer, he seized the forts and with his craft subdued them.

10.99.d: एवा महो असुर वक्षथाय वम्रकः पड्भिरुप सर्पदिन्द्रम | स इयानः करति सवस्तिमस्मा इषमूर्जंसुक्षितिं विश्वमाभाः ||
10.99.e: So, swiftly Asura, for exaltation, hath the great Vamraka come nigh to Indra.  He will, when supplicated, bring him blessing: he hath brought all, food, strength, a happy dwelling.

10.100.d: इन्द्र दर्ह्य मघवन तवावदिद भुज इह सतुतः सुतपाबोधि नो वर्धे | देवेभिर्नः सविता परावतु शरुतमासर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: Be, like thyself, O Indra, strong for our delight: here lauded, aid us, Maghavan, drinker of the juice.  Savitar with the Gods protect us: hear ye Twain. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: भराय सु भरत भागं रत्वियं पर वायवे शुचिपेक्रन्ददिष्टये | गौरस्य यः पयसः पीतिमानश आसर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: Bring swift, for offering, the snare that suits the time, to the pure-drinker Vāyu, roaring as he goes,  To him who hath approached the draught of shining milk. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: आ नो देवः सविता साविषद वय रजूयते यजमानायसुन्वते | यथा देवान परतिभूषेम पाकवदा सर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: May Savitar the God send us full life, to each who sacrifices, lives aright and pours the juice  That we with simple hearts may wait upon the Gods. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: इन्द्रो अस्मे सुमना अस्तु विश्वहा राजा सोमः सुवितस्याध्येतु नः | यथा-यथा मित्रधितानि सन्दधुरा सर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: May Indra evermore be gracious unto us, and may King Soma meditate our happiness,  Even as men secure the comfort of a friend. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: इन्द्र उक्थेन शवसा परुर्दधे बर्हस्पते परतरीतास्यायुषः | यज्ञो मनुः परमतिर्नः पिता हि कमासर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: Indra hath given the body with its song and strength: Bṛhaspati, thou art the lengthener of life.  The sacrifice is Manu, Providence, our Sire. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: इन्द्रस्य नु सुक्र्तं दैव्यं सहो.अग्निर्ग्र्हे जरितामेधिरः कविः | यज्ञश्च भूद विदथे चारुरन्तम आसर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: Indra possesseth might celestial nobly formed: the singer in the house is Agni, prudent Sage.  He is the sacrifice in synod, fair, most near. We ask for freedom and complete felicity,

10.100.d: न वो गुहा चक्र्म भूरि दुष्क्र्तं नाविष्ट्यं वसवोदेवहेळनम | माकिर्नो देवा अन्र्तस्य वर्पस आ सर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: Not often have we sinned against you secretly, nor, Vasus, have we openly provoked the Gods.  Not one of its, ye Gods, hath worn an alien shape. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: अपामीवां सविता साविषन नयग वरीय इदप सेधन्त्वद्रयः | गरावा यत्र मधुषुदुच्यते बर्हदासर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: May Savitar remove from us our malady, and may the Mountains keep it far away from where  The press-stone as it sheds the meath rings loudly forth. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: ऊर्ध्वो गरावा वसवो.अस्तु सोतरि विश्वा दवेषांसि सनुतर्युयोत | स नो देवः सविता पायुरीड्य आ सर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: Ye Vasus, let the stone, the presser stand erect: avert all enmities and keep them far remote.  Our guard to be adored is Savitar this God. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: ऊर्जं गावो यवसे पीवो अत्तन रतस्य याः सदने कोशेङगध्वे | तनूरेव तन्वो अस्तु भेषजमा सर्वतातिंदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: Eat strength and fatness in the pasture, kine, who are balmed at the reservoir and at the seat of Law.  So let your body be our body's medicine. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: करतुप्रावा जरिता शश्वतामव इन्द्र इद भद्राप्रमतिः सुतावताम | पूर्णमूधर्दिव्यं यस्य सिक्तया सर्वतातिमदितिं वर्णीमहे ||
10.100.e: The singer fills the spirit: all mens, love hath he. Indra takes kindly care of those who pour the juice.  For his libation is the heavenly udder full. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.

10.100.d: चित्रस्ते भानुः करतुप्रा अभिष्टिः सन्ति सप्र्धोजरणिप्रा अध्र्ष्टाः | रजिष्ठया रज्या पश्व आ गोस्तूतूर्षत्य पर्यग्रं दुवस्युः ||
10.100.e: Wondrous thy spirit-filling light, triumpliant; thy hosts save from decay and are resistless.  The pious votary by straightest pathway speeds to possess the best of all the cattle.

10.101.d: उद बुध्यध्वं समनसः सखायः समग्निमिन्ध्वं बहवःसनीळाः | दधिक्रामग्निमुषसं च देवीमिन्द्रावतोऽवसे नि हवये वः ||
10.101.e: WAKE with one mind, my friends, and kindle Agni, ye who are many and who dwell together.  Agni and Dadhikrās and Dawn the Goddess, you, Gods with Indra, I call down to help us.

10.101.d: मन्द्रा कर्णुध्वं धिय आ तनुध्वं नावमरित्रपरणींक्र्णुध्वम | इष्क्र्णुध्वमायुधारं कर्णुध्वं पराञ्चंयज्ञं पर णयता सखायः ||
10.101.e: Make pleasant hymns, spin out your songs and praises: build ye a ship equipped with oars for transport.  Prepare the implements, make all things ready, and let the sacrifice, my friends, go forward.

10.101.d: युनक्त सीरा वि युगा तनुध्वं कर्ते योनौ वपतेह बीजम | गिरा च शरुष्टिः शभरा असन नो नेदीय इत सर्ण्यःपक्वमेयात ||
10.101.e: Lay on the yokes, and fasten well the traces: formed is the furrow, sow the seed within it.  Through song may we find bearing fraught with plenty: near to the ripened grain approach the sickle.

10.101.d: सीरा युञ्जन्ति कवयो युगा वि तन्वते पर्थक | धीरादेवेषु सुम्नया ||
10.101.e: Wise, through desire of bliss from Gods, the skilful bind the traces fast, And lay the yokes on either side.

10.101.d: निराहावान कर्णोतन सं वरत्रा दधातन | सिञ्चामहावतमुद्रिणं वयं सुषेकमनुपक्षितम ||
10.101.e: Arrange the buckets in their place securely fasten on the straps.  We will pour forth the well that hath a copious stream, fair-flowing well that never fails.
I pour the water from the well with pails prepared and goodly straps,  Unfailing, full, with plenteous stream.

10.101.d: परीणीताश्वान हितं जयाथ सवस्तिवाहं रथमित्क्र्णुध्वम | दरोणाहावमवतमश्मचक्रमंसत्रकोशंसिञ्चता नर्पाणम ||
10.101.e: Refresh the horses, win the prize before you: equip a chariot fraught with happy fortune.  Pour forth the well with stone wheel, wooden buckets, the drink of heroes, with the trough for armour.

10.101.d: वरजं कर्णुध्वं स हि वो नर्पाणो वर्म सीव्यध्वं बहुलाप्र्थूनि | पुरः कर्णुध्वमायसीरध्र्ष्टा मा वः सुस्रोच्चमसो दरंहता तम ||
10.101.e: Prepare the cow-stall, for there drink your heroes: stitch ye the coats of armour, wide and many.  Make iron forts, secure from all assailants let not your pitcher leak: stay it securely.

10.101.d: आ वो धियं यज्ञियां वर्त ऊतये देवा देवीं यजतांयज्ञियामिह | सा नो दुहीयद यवसेव गत्वी सहस्रधारापयसा मही गौः ||
10.101.e: Hither, for help, I turn the holy heavenly mind of you the Holy Gods, that longs for sacrifice.  May it pour milk for us, even as a stately cow who, having sought the pasture, yields a thousand streams.

10.101.d: आ तू षिञ्च हरिमीं दरोरुपस्थे वाशीभिस्तक्षताश्मन्मयीभिः | परि षवजध्वं दश कक्ष्याभिरुभे धुरौ परति वह्निं युनक्त ||
10.101.e: Pour golden juice within the wooden vessel: with stone-made axes fashion ye and form it.  Embrace and compass it with tenfold girdle, and to both chariot-poles attach the car-horse.

10.101.d: उभे धुरौ वह्निरापिब्दमानो.अन्तर्योनेव चरति दविजानिः | वनस्पतिं वन आस्थापयध्वं नि षू दधिध्वमखनन्त उत्सम ||
10.101.e: Between both poles the car-horse goes pressed closely, as in his dwelling moves the doubly-wedded.  Lay in the wood the Soviran of the Forest, and sink the well although ye do not dig it.

10.101.d: कप्र्न नरः कप्र्थमुद दधातन चोदयत खुदतवाजसातये | निष्टिग्र्यः पुत्रमा चयावयोतय इन्द्रंसबाध इह सोमपीतये ||
10.101.e: Indra is he, O men, who gives us happiness: sport, urge the giver of delight to win us strength  Bring quickly down, O priests, hither to give us aid, to drink the Soma, Indra Son of Nistigri.

10.102.d: पर ते रथं मिथूक्र्तमिन्द्रो.अवतु धर्ष्णुया | अस्मिन्नाजौ पुरुहूत शरवाय्ये धनभक्षेषु नो.अव ||
10.102.e: FOR thee may Indra boldly speed the car that works on either side.  Favour us, Much-invoked! in this most glorious fight against the raiders of our wealth.

10.102.d: उत सम वातो वहति वासो.अस्या अधिरथं यदजयत सहस्रम | रथीरभून मुद्गलानी गविष्टौ भरे कर्तं वयचेदिन्द्रसेना ||
10.102.e: Loose in the wind the woman's robe was streaming what time she won a car-load worth a thousand.  The charioteer in fight was Mudgalani: she Indra's dart, heaped up the prize of battle.

10.102.d: अन्तर्यछ जिघांसतो वज्रमिन्द्राभिदासतः | दासस्यवा मघवन्नार्यस्य वा सनुतर्यवया वधम ||
10.102.e: O Indra, cast thy bolt among assailants who would slaughter us:  The weapon both of Dāsa and of Ārya foe keep far away, O Maghavan.

10.102.d: उद्नो हरदमपिबज्जर्ह्र्षाणः कूटं सम तरंहदभिमातिमेति | पर मुष्कभारः शरव इछमानो.अजिरम्बाहू अभरत सिषासन ||
10.102.e: The bull in joy had drunk a lake of water. His shattering horn encountered an opponent.  Swiftly, in vigorous strength, eager for glory, he stretched his forefeet, fain to win and triumph.

10.102.d: नयक्रन्दयन्नुपयन्त एनममेहयन वर्षभं मध्य आजेः | तेन सूभर्वं शतवत सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः परधनेजिगाय ||
10.102.e: They came anear the bull; they made him thunder, made him pour rain down ere the fight was ended.  And Mudgala thereby won in the contest well-pastured kine in hundreds and in thousands.

10.102.d: ककर्दवे वर्षभो युक्त आसीदवावचीत सारथिरस्य केशी | दुधेर्युक्तस्य दरवतः सहानस रछन्ति षमा निष्पदोमुद्गलानीम ||
10.102.e: In hope of victory that bull was harnessed: Kesi the driver urged him on with shouting.  As he ran swiftly with the car behind him his lifted heels pressed close on Mudgalani.

10.102.d: उत परधिमुदहन्नस्य विद्वानुपायुनग वंसगमत्रशिक्षन | इन्द्र उदावत पतिमघ्न्यानामरंहतपद्याभिः ककुद्मान ||
10.102.e: Deftly for him he stretched the car-pole forward, guided the bull thereto and firmly yoked him.  Indra vouchsafed the lord of cows his favour: with mighty steps the buffalo ran onward.

10.102.d: शुनमष्त्राव्यचरत कपर्दी वरत्रायां दार्वानह्यमानः | नर्म्णानि कर्ण्वन बहवे जनाय गाःपस्पशानस्तविषीरधत्त ||
10.102.e: Touched by the goad the shaggy beast went nobly, bound to the pole by the yoke's thong of leather.  Performing deeds of might for many people, he, looking on the cows, gained strength and vigour.

10.102.d: इमं तं पश्य वर्षभस्य युञ्जं काष्ठाया मध्येद्रुघणं शयानम | येन जिगाय शतवत सहस्रं गवाम्मुद्गलः पर्तनाज्येषु ||
10.102.e: Here look upon this mace, this bull's companion, now lying midway on the field of battle.  Therewith hath Mudgala in ordered contest won for cattle for himself, a hundred thousand.

10.102.d: आरे अघा को नवित्था ददर्श यं युञ्जन्ति तं वास्थापयन्ति | नास्मै तर्णं नोदकमा भरन्त्युत्तरो धुरोवहति परदेदिशत ||
10.102.e: Far is the evil: who hath here beheld it? Hither they bring the bull whom they are yoking..  To this they give not either food or water. Reaching beyond the pole it gives directions.

10.102.d: परिव्र्क्तेव पतिविद्यमानट पीप्याना कूचक्रेणेव सिञ्चन | एषैष्या चिद रथ्या जयेम सुमङगलं सिनवदस्तु सातम ||
10.102.e: Like one forsaken, she hath found a husband, and teemed as if her breast were full and flowing.  With swiftly-racing chariot may we conquer, and rich and blessed be our gains in battle.

10.102.d: तवं विश्वस्य जगतश्चक्षुरिन्द्रासि चक्षुषः | वर्षायदाजिं वर्षणा सिषाससि चोदयन वध्रिणा युजा ||
10.102.e: Thou, Indra, art the mark whereon the eyes of all life rest, when thou,  A Bull who drivest with thy bull, wilt win the race together with thy weakling friend.

10.103.d: आशुः शिशानो वर्षभो न भीमो घनाघनः कषोभणश्चर्षणीनाम | संक्रन्दनो.अनिमिष एकवीरः शतं सेनाजयत साकमिन्द्रः ||
10.103.e: SWIFT, rapidly striking, like a bull who sharpens his horns, terrific, stirring up the people,  With eyes that close not, bellowing, Sole Hero, Indra. subdued at once a hundred armies.

10.103.d: संक्रन्दनेनानिमिषेण जिष्णुना युत्कारेण दुश्च्यवनेनध्र्ष्णुना | तदिन्द्रेण जयत तत सहध्वं युधो नरैषुहस्तेन वर्ष्णा ||
10.103.e: With him loud-roaring, ever watchful, Victor, bold, hard to overthrow, Rouser of battle,  Indra. the Strong, whose hand bears arrows, conquer, ye warriors, now, now vanquish in the combat.

10.103.d: स इषुहस्तैः स निषङगिभिर्वशी संस्रष्टा स युधैन्द्रो गणेन | संस्र्ष्टजित सोमपा बाहुशर्ध्युग्रधन्वाप्रतिहिताभिरस्ता ||
10.103.e: He rules with those who carry shafts and quivers, Indra who with his band rings hosts together,  Foe-conquering, strong of arm, the Soma-drinker, with mighty bow, shooting with well-laid arrows.

10.103.d: बर्हस्पते परि दीया रथेन रक्षोहामित्रानपबाधमानः | परभञ्जन सेनाः परम्र्णो युधा जयन्नस्माकमेध्यविता रथानाम ||
10.103.e: Bṛhaspati, fly with thy chariot hither, slayer of demons, driving off our foemen.  Be thou protector of our cars, destroyer, victor in battle, breaker-up of armies.

10.103.d: बलविज्ञाय सथविरः परवीरः सहस्वान वाजी सहमानौग्रः | अभिवीरो अभिसत्वा सहोजा जैत्रमिन्द्र रथमातिष्ठ गोवित ||
10.103.e: Conspicuous by thy strength, firm, foremost fighter, mighty and fierce, victorious, all-subduing,  The Son of Conquest, passing men and heroes, kine-winner, mount thy conquering car, O Indra.

10.103.d: गोत्रभिदं गोविदं वज्रबाहुं जयन्तमज्म परम्र्णन्तमोजसा | इमं सजाता अनु वीरयध्वमिन्द्रं सखायो अनुसं रभध्वम ||
10.103.e: Cleaver of stalls, kine-winner, armed with thunder, who quells an army and with might destroys it.-  Follow him, brothers! quit yourselves like heroes, and like this Indra show your zeal and courage.

10.103.d: अभि गोत्राणि सहसा गाहमानो.अदयो वीरः शतमन्युरिन्द्रः | दुश्च्यवनः पर्तनाषाळ अयुध्यो.अस्माकं सेनावतु पर युत्सु ||
10.103.e: Piercing the cow-stalls with surpassing vigour, Indra, the pitiless Hero, wild with anger,  Victor in fight, unshaken and resistless,may he protect our armies in our battles.

10.103.d: इन्द्र आसां नेता बर्हस्पतिर्दक्षिणा यज्ञः पुर एतुसोमः | देवसेनानामभिभञ्जतीनां जयन्तीनां मरुतोयन्त्वग्रम ||
10.103.e: Indra guide these: Bṛhaspati precede them, the guerdon, and the sacrifice, and Soma;  And let the banded Maruts march in forefront of heavenly hosts that conquer and demolish.

10.103.d: इन्द्रस्य वर्ष्णो वरुणस्य राज्ञ आदित्यानां मरुतांशर्ध उग्रम | महामनसां भुवनच्यवानां घोषोदेवानां जयतामुदस्थात ||
10.103.e: Ours be the potent host of mighty Indra, King Varuṇa, and Maruts, and Ādityas.  Uplifted is the shout of Gods who conquer high-minded Gods who cause the worlds to tremble.

10.103.d: उद धर्षय मघवन्नायुधान्युत सत्वनां मामकानाम्मनांसि | उद वर्त्रहन वाजिनां वाजिनान्युद रथानांजयतां यन्तु घोषाः ||
10.103.e: Bristle thou up, O Maghavan, our weapons: excite the spirits of my warring heroes.  Urge on the strong steeds' might, O Vṛtra-slayer, and let the din of conquering cars go upward.

10.103.d: अस्माकमिन्द्रः सम्र्तेषु धवजेष्वस्माकं या इषवस्ताजयन्तु | अस्माकं वीरा उत्तरे भवन्त्वस्मानु देवा अवताहवेषु ||
10.103.e: May Indra aid us when our flags are gathered: victorious be the arrows of our army.  May our brave men of war prevail in battle. Ye Gods, protect us in the shout of onset.

10.103.d: अमीषां चित्तं परतिलोभयन्ती गर्हाणाङगान्यप्वे परेहि | अभि परेहि निर्दह हर्त्सु शोकैरन्धेनामित्रास्तमसासचन्ताम ||
10.103.e: Bewildering the senses of our foemen, seize thou their bodies and depart, O Apva.  Attack them, set their hearts on fire and burn them: so let our foes abide in utter darkness.

10.103.d: परेता जयता नर इन्द्रो वः शर्म यछतु | उग्रा वः सन्तुबाहवो.अनाध्र्ष्या यथासथ ||
10.103.e: Advance, O heroes, win the day. May Indra be your sure defence.  Exceeding mighty be your arms, that none may wound or injure you.

10.104.d: असावि सोमः पुरुहूत तुभ्यं हरिभ्यां यज्ञमुप याहितूयम | तुभ्यं गिरो विप्रवीरा इयाना दधन्विर इन्द्रपिबा सुतस्य ||
10.104.e: Soma hath flowed for thee, Invoked of mat Speed to our sacrifice with both thy Coursers.  To thee have streameld the songs or mighty singers, imploring, Indra, drink of our libation.

10.104.d: अप्सु धूतस्य हरिवः पिबेह नर्भिः सुतस्य जठरम्प्र्णस्व | मिमिक्षुर्यमद्रय इन्द्र तुभ्यं तेभिर्वर्धस्वमदमुक्थवाहः ||
10.104.e: Drink of the juice which men have washed in waters, and fill thee full, O Lord of Tawny Horses.  O Indra, hearer of the laud, with Soma which stones have mixed for thee enhance thy rapture.

10.104.d: परोग्रां पीतिं वर्ष्ण इयर्मि सत्यां परयै सुतस्यहर्यश्व तुभ्यम | इन्द्र धेनाभिरिह मादयस्व धीभिर्विश्वाभिः शच्या गर्णानः ||
10.104.e: To make thee start, a strong true draught I offer to thee, the Bull, O thou whom Bay Steeds carry.  Here take delight, O Indra, in our voices while thou art hymned with power and all our spirit.

10.104.d: ऊती शचीवस्तव वीर्येण वयो दधाना उशिज रतज्ञाः | परजावदिन्द्र मनुषो दुरोणे तस्थुर्ग्र्णन्तःसधमाद्यासः ||
10.104.e: O Mighty Indra, through thine aid, thy prowess, obtaining life, zealous, and skilled in Order,  Men in the house who share the sacred banquet stand singing praise that brings them store of children.

10.104.d: परणीतिभिष टे हर्यश्व सुष्टोः सुषुम्नस्य पुरुरुचोजनासः | मंहिष्ठामूतिं वितिरे दधाना सतोतारैन्द्र तव सून्र्ताभिः ||
10.104.e: Through thy directions, Lord of Tawny Coursers, thine who art firm, splendid, and blest, the people  Obtain most liberal aid for their salvation, and praise thee, Indra, through thine excellencies.

10.104.d: उप बरह्माणि हरिवो हरिभ्यां सोमस्य याहि पीतये सुतस्य | इन्द्र तवा यज्ञः कषममाणमानड दाश्वानस्यध्वरस्य परकेतः ||
10.104.e: Lord of the Bays, come with thy two Bay Horses, come to our prayers, to drink the juice of Soma.  To thee comes sacrifice which thou acceptest: thou, skilled in holy rites, art he who giveth.

10.104.d: सहस्रवाजमभिमातिषाहं सुतेरणं मघवानं सुव्र्क्तिम | उप भूषन्ति गिरो अप्रतीतमिन्द्रं नमस्या जरितुःपनन्त ||
10.104.e: Him of a thousand powers, subduing foemen, Maghavan praised with hymns and pleased with Soma,—  Even him our songs approach, resistless Indra: the adorations of the singer laud him.

10.104.d: सप्तापो देवीः सुरणा अम्र्क्ता याभिः सिन्धुमतर इन्द्रपूर्भित | नवतिं सरोत्या नव च सरवन्तीर्देवेभ्यो गातुम्मनुषे च विन्दः ||
10.104.e: The way to bliss for Gods and man thou foundest, Indra, seven lovely floods, divine, untroubled,  Wherewith thou, rending forts, didst move the ocean, and nine-and-ninety flowing streams of water.

10.104.d: अपो महीरभिशस्तेरमुञ्चो.अजागरास्वधि देव एकः | इन्द्र यास्त्वं वर्त्रतूर्ये चकर्थ ताभिर्विश्वायुस्तन्वं पुपुष्याः ||
10.104.e: Thou from the curse didst free the mighty Waters, and as their only God didst watch and guard them.  O Indra, cherish evermore thy body with those which thou hast won in quelling Vṛtra.

10.104.d: वीरेण्यः करतुरिन्द्रः सुशस्तिरुतापि धेना पुरुहूतमीट्टे | आर्दयद वर्त्रमक्र्णोदु लोकं ससाहे शक्रःप्र्तना अभिष्टिः ||
10.104.e: Heroic power and noble praise is Indra yea, the song worships him invoked of many.  Vṛtra he quelled, and gave men room and freedom: gakra, victorious, hath conquered armies.
Call we on Maghayan, auspicious Indra. best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

10.105.d: कदा वसो सतोत्रं हर्यत आव शमशा रुधद वाः | दीर्घं सुतं वाताप्याय ||
10.105.e: WHEN, Vasu, wilt thou love the laud? Now let the channel bring the stream.  The juice is ready to ferment.

10.105.d: हरी यस्य सुयुजा विव्रता वेरर्वन्तानु शेपा | उभारजी न केशिना पतिर्दन ||
10.105.e: He whose two Bay Steeds harnessed well, swerving, pursue the Bird's tail-plumes,  With Rowing manes, like heaven and earth, he is the Lord with power to give.

10.105.d: अप योरिन्द्रः पापज आ मर्तो न शश्रमाणो बिभीवान | शुभे यद युयुजे तविषीवान ||
10.105.e: Bereft of skill is Indra, if, like some outwearied man he fears  The sinner, when the Mighty hath prepared himself for victory.

10.105.d: सचायोरिन्द्रश्चर्क्र्ष आनुपानसः सपर्यन | नदयोर्विव्रतयोः शूर इन्द्रः ||
10.105.e: Indra with these drives round, until he meets with one to worship him:  Indra is Master of the pair who snort and swerve upon their way.

10.105.d: अधि यस्तस्थौ केशवन्ता वयचस्वन्ता न पुष्ट्यै | वनोति शिप्राभ्यां शिप्रिणीवान ||
10.105.e: Borne onward by the long-maned Steeds who stretch themselves as ’twere for food,  The God who wears the helm defends them with his jaws.

10.105.d: परास्तौद रष्वौजा रष्वेभिस्ततक्ष शूरः शवसा | रभुर्न करतुभिर्मातरिश्वा ||
10.105.e: The Mighty sang with Lofty Ones: the Hero fashioned with his strength,  Like skilful Mātariśvan with his power and might,

10.105.d: वज्रं यश्चक्रे सुहनाय दस्यवे हिरीमशो हिरीमान | अरुतहनुरद्भुतं न रजः ||
10.105.e: The bolt, which pierced at once the vitals of the Dasyu easy to be slain,  With jaw uninjured like the wondrous firmament.

10.105.d: अव नो वर्जिना शिशीह्य रचा वनेमान्र्चः | नाब्रह्मा यज्ञर्धग जोषति तवे ||
10.105.e: Grind off our sins: with song will we conquer the men who sing no hymns:  Not easily art thou pleased with prayerless sacrifice.

10.105.d: ऊर्ध्वा यत ते तरेतिनी भूद यज्ञस्य धूर्षु सद्मन | सजूर्नावं सवयशसं सचायोः ||
10.105.e: When threefold flame burns high for thee, to rest on poles of sacrifice,  Thou with the living joyest in the self-bright Ship.

10.105.d: शरिये ते पर्श्निरुपसेचनी भूच्छ्रिये दर्विररेपाः | यया सवे पात्रे सिञ्चस उत ||
10.105.e: Thy glory was the speckled cup, thy glory was the flawless scoop.  Wherewith thou pourest into thy receptacle.

10.105.d: शतं वा यदसुर्य परति तवा सुमित्र इत्थास्तौद दुर्मित्रैत्थास्तौ | आवो यद दस्युहत्ये कुत्सपुत्रं परावो यद्दस्युहत्ये कुत्सवत्सम ||
10.105.e: As hundreds, O Immortal God, have sung to thee, so hath Sumitra, yea, Durmitra praised thee here,  What time thou holpest Kutsa's son, when Dasyus fell, yea, holpest Kutsa's darling when the Dasyus died.

10.106.d: उभा उ नूनं तदिदर्थयेथे वि तन्वाथे धियोवश्त्रापसेव | सध्रीचीना यातवे परेमजीगः सुदिनेवप्र्क्ष आ तंसयेथे ||
10.106.e: THIS very thing ye Twain hold as your object: ye weave your songs as skilful men weave garments.  That ye may come united have I waked you: ye spread out food like days of lovely weather.

10.106.d: उष्टारेव फर्वरेषु शरयेथे परायोगेव शवात्र्या शासुरेथः | दूतेव हि षठो यशसा जनेषु माप सथातम्महिषेवापानात ||
10.106.e: Like two plough-bulls ye move along in traces, and seek like eager guests your bidder's banquet.  Ye are like glorious envoys mid the people: like bulls, approach the place where ye are watered.

10.106.d: साकंयुजा शकुनस्येव पक्षा पश्वेव चित्रा यजुरागमिष्टम | अग्निरिव देवयोर्दीदिवांसा परिज्मानेवयजथः पुरुत्रा ||
10.106.e: Like the two pinions of a bird, connected, like two choice animals, ye have sought our worship.  Bright as the fire the votary hath kindled, ye sacrifice in many a spot as roamers.

10.106.d: आपी वो अस्मे पितरेव पुत्रोग्रेव रुचा नर्पतीव तुर्यै | इर्येव पुष्ट्यै किरणेव भुज्यै शरुष्टीवानेव हवमागमिष्टम ||
10.106.e: Ye are our kinsmen, like two sons, two fathers, strong in your splendour and like kings for conquest;  Like rays for our enjoyment, Lords to feed us, ye, like quick bearers, have obeyed our calling.

10.106.d: वंसगेव पूषर्या शिम्बाता मित्रेव रता शतराशातपन्ता | वाजेवोच्चा वयसा घर्म्येष्ठा मेषेवेषासपर्या पुरीषा ||
