10.106.e: You are like two pleasantly moving well-fed (hills) like Mitra and Varuṇa, the two bestowers of felicity, veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy, like two horses plump with fodder, abiding in the firmament, like two rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations).

10.106.d: सर्ण्येव जर्भरी तुर्फरीतू नैतोशेव तुर्फरीपर्फरीका | उदन्यजेव जेमना मदेरू ता मे जराय्वजरम्मरायु ||
10.106.e: You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe, like the two sons of Nitosa destroying (foes), and cherishing (friends); you are bright as two water-born (jewels), do you, who are victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay.

10.106.d: पज्रेव चर्चरं जारं मरायु कषद्मेवार्थेषु तर्तरीथौग्रा | रभू नापत खरमज्रा खरज्रुर्वायुर्न पर्फरत्क्षयद रयीणाम ||
10.106.e: Fierce (Aśvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving, perishable mortal (frame) to cross over to the objects (of its destination) as over water; extremely strong, like the Ṛbhus, your chariot, attained its destination swift as the wind, it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches.

10.106.d: घर्मेव मधु जठरे सनेरू भगेविता तुर्फरीफारिवारम | पतरेव चचरा चन्द्रनिर्णिं मनर्ङगामनन्या न जग्मी ||
10.106.e: With your bellies full of the Soma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies. (you are) armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds) with forms like the moon, attaining success through the mind, like two laudable beings, (you are) approaching (the sacrifice).

10.106.d: बर्हन्तेव गम्भरेषु परतिष्ठां पादेव गाधं तरतेविदाथः | कर्णेव शासुरनु हि समराथो.अंशेव नोभजतं चित्रमप्नः ||
10.106.e: Like giants, ye will find firm ground to stand on in depths, like feet for one who fords a shallow.  Like cars ye will attend to him who orders: ye Two enjoy our wondrous work as sharers.

10.106.d: आरङगरेव मध्वेरयेथे सारघेव गवि नीचीनबारे | कीनारेव सवेदमासिष्विदाना कषामेवोर्जा सूयवसात्सचेथे ||
10.106.e: Like toiling bees ye bring to us your honey, as bees into the hide that opens downward.

10.106.d: रध्याम सतोमं सनुयाम वाजमा नो मन्त्रं सरथेहोपयातम | यशो न पक्वं मधु गोष्वन्तरा भूतांशोश्विनोः काममप्राः ||
10.106.e: May we increase the laud and gain us vigour: come to our song, ye whom one chariot carries.  Filled be our kine with ripened meath like glory: Bhutamsa hath fulfilled the Aśvins' longing.

10.107.d: आविरभून महि माघोनमेषां विश्वं जीवं तमसो निरमोचि | महि जयोतिः पित्र्भिर्दत्तमागादुरुः पन्थादक्षिणाया अदर्शि ||
10.107.e: THESE men's great bounty hath been manifested, and the whole world of life set free from darkness.  Great light hath come, vouchsafed us by the Fathers: apparent is the spacious path of Guerdon.

10.107.d: उच्चा दिवि दक्षिणावन्तो अस्थुर्ये अश्वदाः सह तेसूर्येण | हिरण्यदा अम्र्तत्वं भजन्ते वासोदाः सोम परतिरन्त आयुः ||
10.107.e: High up in heaven abide the Guerdon-givers: they who give steeds dwell with the Sun for ever.  They who give gold are blest with life eternal. they who give robes prolong their lives, O Soma.

10.107.d: दैवी पूर्तिर्दक्षिणा देवयज्या न कवारिभ्यो नहि तेप्र्णन्ति | अथा नरः परयतदक्षिणासो.अवद्यभियाबहवः पर्णन्ति ||
10.107.e: Not from the niggards-for they give not fireely-comes Meed at sacrifice, Gods’ satisfaction:  Yea, many men with hands stretched out with Guerdon present their gifts because they dread dishonour.

10.107.d: शतधारं वायुमर्कं सवर्विदं नर्चक्षसस्ते अभिचक्षते हविः | ये पर्णन्ति पर च यछन्ति संगमे तेदक्षिणां दुहते सप्तमातरम ||
10.107.e: These who observe mankind regard oblation as streamy Vāyu and light-finding Arka.  They satisfy and give their gifts in synod, and pour in streams the seven-mothered Guerdon.

10.107.d: दक्षिणावान परथमो हूत एति दक्षिणावान गरामणीरग्रमेति | तमेव मन्ये नर्पतिं जनानां यः परथमोदक्षिणामाविवाय ||
10.107.e: He who brings Guerdon comes as first invited: chief of the hamlet comes the Guerdon-bearer.  Him I account the ruler of the people who was the first to introduce the Guerdon.

10.107.d: तमेव रषिं तमु बरह्माणमाहुर्यज्ञन्यं सामगामुक्थशासम | स शुक्रस्य तन्वो वेद तिस्रो यः परथमोदक्षिणया रराध ||
10.107.e: They call him Ṛṣi, Brahman, Sāma-chanter, reciter of the laud, leader of worship.  The brightly-shining God's three forms he knoweth who first bestowed the sacrificial Guerdon.

10.107.d: दक्षिणाश्वं दक्षिणा गां ददाति दक्षिणा चन्द्रमुत यद धिरण्यम | दक्षिणान्नं वनुते यो न आत्मादक्षिणां वर्म कर्णुते विजानन ||
10.107.e: Guerdon bestows the horse, bestows the bullock, Guerdon bestows, moreover, gold that Rsisters.  Guerdon gives food which is our life and spirit. He who is wise takes Guerdon for his armour.

10.107.d: न भोजा मम्रुर्न नयर्थमीयुर्न रिष्यन्ति न वयथन्ते हभोजाः | इदं यद विश्वं भुवनं सवश्चैतत सर्वन्दक्षिणैभ्यो ददाति ||
10.107.e: The liberal die not, never are they ruined: the liberal suffer neither harm nor trouble.  The light of heaven, the universe about us,—all this doth sacrificial Guerdon give them.

10.107.d: भोजा जिग्युः सुरभिं योनिमग्रे भोजा जिग्युर्वध्वं यासुवासाः | भोजा जिग्युरन्तःपेयं सुराया भोजा जिग्युर्ये अहूताः परयन्ति ||
10.107.e: First have the liberal gained a fragrant dwelling, and got themselves a bride in fair apparel.  The liberal have obtained their draught of liquor, and conquered those who, unprovoked, assailed them.

10.107.d: भोजायाश्वं सं मर्जन्त्याशुं भोजायास्ते कन्याशुम्भमाना | भोजस्येदं पुष्करिणीव वेश्म परिष्क्र्तन्देवमानेव चित्रम ||
10.107.e: They deck the fleet steed for the bounteous giver: the maid adorns herself and waits to meet him.  His home is like a lake with lotus blossoms, like the Gods’ palaces adorned and splendid.

10.107.d: भोजमश्वाः सुष्ठुवाहो वहन्ति सुव्र्द रथो वर्ततेदक्षिणायाः | भोजं देवासो.अवता भरेषु भोजःशत्रून समनीकेषु जेता ||
10.107.e: Steeds good at draught convey the liberal giver, and lightly rolling moves the car of Guerdon.  Assist, ye Gods, the liberal man in battles: the liberal giver conquers foes in combat.

10.108.d: किमिछन्ती सरमा परेदमानड दूरे हयध्वा जगुरिःपराचैः | कास्मेहितिः का परितक्म्यासीत कथं रसायातरः पयांसि ||
10.108.e: WHAT wish of Saramā hath brought her hither? The path leads far away to distant places.  What charge hast thou for us? Where turns thy journey? How hast thou made thy way o’er Rasā's waters.

10.108.d: इन्द्रस्य दूतीरिषिता चरामि मह इछन्ती पणयो निधीन्वः | अतिष्कदो भियसा तन न आवत तथा रसाया अतरम्पयांसि ||
10.108.e: I come appointed messenger of Indra, seeking your ample stores of wealth, O Paṇis.  This hath preserved me from the fear of crossing: thus have I made my way o’er Rasā's waters.

10.108.d: कीद्रंं इन्द्रः सरमे का दर्शीका यस्येदं दूतीरसरः पराकात | आ च गछान मित्रमेना दधामाथागवां गोपतिर्नो भवाति ||
10.108.e: What is that Indra like, what is his aspect whose envoy, Saramā, from afar thou comest?  Let him approach, and we will show him friendship: he shall be made the herdsman of our cattle.

10.108.d: नाहं तं वेद दभ्यं दभत स यस्येदं दूतीरसरं पराकात | न तं गूहन्ति सरवतो गभीरा हतािन्द्रेण पणयः शयध्वे ||
10.108.e: I know him safe from harm: but he can punish who sent me hither from afar as envoy.  Him rivers flowing with deep waters bide not. Low will ye be, O Paṇis, slain by Indra.

10.108.d: इमा गावः सरमे या ऐछः परि दिवो अन्तान सुभगेपतन्ती | कस्त एना अव सर्जादयुध्व्युतास्माकमायुधासन्ति तिग्मा ||
10.108.e: These are the kine which, Saramā, thou seekest, flying, O Blest One, to the ends of heaven.  Who will loose these for thee without a battle? Yea, and sharp-pointed are our warlike weapons.

10.108.d: असेन्या वः पणयो वचांस्यनिषव्यास्तन्वः सन्तु पापीः | अध्र्ष्टो व एतवा अस्तु पन्था बर्हस्पतिर्व उभया नम्र्ळात ||
10.108.e: Even if your wicked bodies, O ye Paṇis, were arrow-proof, your words are weak for wounding;  And were the path to you as yet unmastered, Bṛhaspati in neither case will spare you.

10.108.d: अयं निधिः सरमे अद्रिबुध्नो गोभिरश्वेभिर्वसुभिर्न्य्र्ष्टः | रक्षन्ति तं पणयो ये सुगोपा रेकु पदमलकमा जगन्थ ||
10.108.e: Paved with the rock is this our treasure-chamber; filled full of precious things, of kine, and horses.  These Paṇis who are watchful keepers guard it. In vain hast thou approached this lonely station.

10.108.d: एह गमन्न्र्षयः सोमशिता अयास्यो अङगिरसो नवग्वाः | त एतमूर्वं वि भजन्त गोनामथैतद वचः पणयोवमन्नित ||
10.108.e: Ṛṣis will come inspirited with Soma, Aṅgirases unwearied, and Navagvas.  This stall of cattle will they part among them: then will the Paṇis wish these words unspoken.

10.108.d: एवा च तवं सरम आजगन्थ परबाधिता सहसा दैव्येन | सवसारं तवा कर्णवै मा पुनर्गा अप ते गवां सुभगेभजाम ||
10.108.e: Even thus, O Saramā, hast thou come hither, forced by celestial might to make the journey.  Turn thee not back, for thou shalt be our sister: O Blest One, we will give thee of the cattle.

10.108.d: नाहं वेद भरात्र्त्वं नो सवस्र्त्वमिन्द्रो विदुरङगिरसश्च घोराः | गोकामा मे अछदयन यदायमपात इत पणयोवरीयः ||
10.108.e: Brotherhood, sisterhood, I know not either: the dread Aṅgirases and Indra know them.  They seemed to long for kine when I departed. Hence, into distance, be ye gone, O Paṇis.

10.108.d: दूरमित पणयो वरीय उद गावो यन्तु मिनतीरतेन | बर्हस्पतिर्या अविन्दन निगूळाः सोमो गरावाण रषयश्च विप्राः ||
10.108.e: Hence, far away, ye Paṇis! Let the cattle lowing come forth as holy Law commandeth,  Kine which Bṛhaspati, and Soma, Ṛṣis, sages, and pressing-stones have found when hidden.

10.109.d: ते.अवदन परथमा बरह्मकिल्बिषे.अकूपारः सलिलोमातरिश्वा | वीळुहरास्तप उग्रो मयोभूरापो देवीःप्रथमजा रतेन ||
10.109.e: THESE first, the boundless Sea, and Mātariśvan, fierce-glowing Fire, the Strong, the Bliss-bestower.  And heavenly Floods, first-born by holy Order, exclaimed against the outrage on a Brahman.

10.109.d: सोमो राजा परथमो बरह्मजायां पुनः परायछदह्र्णीयमानः | अन्वर्तिता वरुणो मित्र आसीदग्निर्होताहस्तग्र्ह्या निनाय ||
10.109.e: King Soma first of all, without reluctance, made restitution of the Brahman's consort.  Mitra and Varuṇa were the inviters: Agni as Hota; took her hand and led her.

10.109.d: हस्तेनैव गराह्य आधिरस्या बरह्मजायेयमिति चेदवोचन | न दूताय परह्ये तस्थ एषा तथा राष्ट्रं गुपितंक्षत्रियस्य ||
10.109.e: The man, her pledge, must by her hand be taken when they have cried, She is a Brahman's consort.  She stayed not for a herald to conduct her: thus is the kingdom of a ruler guarded.

10.109.d: देवा एतस्यामवदन्त पूर्वे सप्तर्षयस्तपसे ये निषेदुः | भीमा जाया बराह्मणस्योपनीता दुर्धां दधातिपरमे वयोमन ||
10.109.e: Thus spake of her those Gods of old, Seven Ṛṣis who sate them down to their austere devotion:  Dire is a Brahman's wife led home by others: in the supremest heaven she plants confusion.

10.109.d: बरह्मचारी चरति वेविषद विषः स देवानां भवत्येकमङगम | तेन जायामन्वविन्दद बर्हस्पतिः सोमेन नीतांजुह्वं न देवाः ||
10.109.e: The Brahmacari goes engaged in duty: he is a member of the Gods’ own body.  Through him Bṛhaspati obtained his consort, as the Gods gained the ladle brought by Soma.

10.109.d: पुनर्वै देवा अददुः पुनर्मनुष्या उत | राजानःसत्यं कर्ण्वाना बरह्मजायां पुनर्ददुः ||
10.109.e: So then the Gods restored her, so men gave the woman back again.  The Kings who kept their promises restored the Brahman's wedded wife,

10.109.d: पुनर्दाय बरह्मजायां कर्त्वी देवैर्निकिल्बिषम | ऊर्जम्प्र्थिव्या भक्त्वायोरुगायमुपासते ||
10.109.e: Having restored the Brahman's wife, and freed them, with Gods’ aid, from sin,  They shared the fulness of the earth, and won themselves extended sway.

10.110.d: समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान यजसि जातवेदः | आ च वह मित्रमहश्चिकित्वान तवं दूतः कविरसिप्रचेताः ||
10.110.e: THOU in the house of man this day enkindled worshippest Gods as God, O Jātavedas.  Observant, bright as Mitra, bring them hither: thou art a sapient and foreknowing envoy.

10.110.d: तनूनपात पथ रतस्य यानान मध्वा समञ्जन सवदयासुजिह्व | मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञं रन्धन देवत्रा चक्र्णुह्यध्वरं नः ||
10.110.e: Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued, with sweet meath balming the paths and waysof Order, make them pleasant.  Convey our sacrifice to heaven, exalting with holy thoughts ourhymns of praise and worship.

10.110.d: आजुह्वान ईड्यो वन्द्यश्चा याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः | तवं देवानामसि यह्व होता स एनान यक्षीषितो यजीयान ||
10.110.e: Invoked, deserving prayer and adoration, O Agni, come accordant with the Vasus.  Thou art, O Youthful Lord, the Gods’ Invoker, so, best of Sacrificers, bring them quickly.

10.110.d: पराचीनं बर्हिः परदिशा पर्थिव्या वस्तोरस्या वर्ज्यतेग्रे अह्नाम | वयु परथते वितरं वरीयो देवेभ्यो अदितयेस्योनम ||
10.110.e: By rule the Sacred Grass is scattered eastward, a robe to clothe this earth when dawns are breaking.  Widely it spreads around and far-extended, fair for the Gods and bringing peace and freedom.

10.110.d: वयचस्वतीरुर्विया वि शरयन्तां पतिभ्यो न जनयःशुम्भमानाः | देवीर्द्वारो बर्हतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्योभवत सुप्रायणाः ||
10.110.e: Let the expansive Doors be widely opened, like wives who deck their beauty for their husbands.  Lofty, celestial, all-impelling Portals, admit the Gods and give them easy entrance.

10.110.d: आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नियोनौ | दिव्ये योषणे बर्हती सुरुक्मे अधि शरियंशुक्रपिशं दधाने ||
10.110.e: Pouring sweet dews let holy Night and Morning, each close to each, he seated at their station,  Lofty, celestial Dames with gold to deck them. assuming all their fair and radiant beauty.

10.110.d: दैव्या होतारा परथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषोयजध्यै | परचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू पराचीनं जयोतिःप्रदिशा दिशन्ता ||
10.110.e: Come the two first celestial sweet-voiced Hotars, arranging sacrifice for man to worship  As singers who inspire us in assemblies, showing the eastward light with their direction.

10.110.d: आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिहचेतयन्ती | तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं सयोनं सरस्वतीस्वपसः सदन्तु ||
10.110.e: Let Bhāratī come quickly to our worship, and Iḷā showing like a human being.  So let Sarasvatī and both her fellows, deft Goddesses, on this fair grass be seated.

10.110.d: य इमे दयावाप्र्थिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद भुवनानिविश्वा | तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान देवं तवष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान ||
10.110.e: Hotar more skilled in sacrifice, bring hither with speed to-day God Tvaṣṭar, thou who knowest.  Even him who formed these two, the Earth and Heaven the Parents, with their forms, and every creature.

10.110.d: उपावस्र्ज तमन्या समञ्जन देवानां पाथ रतुथाहवींषि | वनस्पतिः शमिता देवो अग्निः सवदन्तु हव्यम्मधुना घर्तेन ||
10.110.e: Send to our offerings which thyself thou balmest the Companies of Gods in ordered season.  Agni, Vanaspati the Immolator sweeten our offered gift with meath and butter.

10.110.d: सद्यो जातो वयमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः | अस्य होतुः परदिश्य रतस्य वाचि सवाहाक्र्तंहविरदन्तु देवाः ||
10.110.e: Agni, as soon as he was born, made ready the sacrifice, and was the Gods’ preceder.  May the Gods cat our offering consecrated according to this true Priest's voice and guidance.

10.111.d: मनीषिणः पर भरध्वं मनीषां यथा-यथा मतयःसन्ति नर्णाम | इन्द्रं सत्यैरेरयामा कर्तेभिः स हिवीरो गिर्वणस्युर्विदानः ||
10.111.e: BRING forth your sacred song ye prudent singers, even as are the thoughts of human beings.  Let us draw Indra with true deeds anear us: he loves our songs, the Hero, and is potent.

10.111.d: रतस्य हि सदसो धीतिरद्यौत सं गार्ष्टेयो वर्षभोगोभिरानट | उदतिष्ठत तविषेणा रवेण महान्ति चित्सं विव्याचा रजांसि ||
10.111.e: The hymn shone brightly from the seat of worship: to the kine came the Bull, the Heifer's Offipring  With mighty bellowing hath he arisen, and hath pervaded even the spacious regions.

10.111.d: इन्द्रः किल शरुत्या अस्य वेद स हि जिष्णुः पथिक्र्त्सूर्याय | आन मेनां कर्ण्वन्नच्युतो भुवद गोः पतिर्दिवः सनजा अप्रतीतः ||
10.111.e: Indra knows, verily, how to hear our singing, for he, victorious, made a path for Sūrya.  He made the Cow, and be became the Sovran of Heaven, primeval, matchless, and unshaken.

10.111.d: इन्द्रो मह्ना महतो अर्णवस्य वरतामिनादङगिरोभिर्ग्र्णानः | पुरूणि चिन नि तताना रजांसि दाधार योधरुणं सत्यताता ||
10.111.e: Praised by Aṅgirases, Indra demolished with might the works of the great watery monster  Full many regions, too, hath he pervaded, and by his truth supported earth's foundation.

10.111.d: इन्द्रो दिवः परतिमानं पर्थिव्या विश्वा वेद सवना हन्तिशुष्णम | महीं चिद दयामातनोत सूर्येण चास्कम्भ चित्कम्भनेन सकभीयान ||
10.111.e: The counterpart of heaven and earth is Indra: he knoweth all libations, slayeth Śuṣṇa.  The vast sky with the Sun hath he extended, and, best otpillars, stayed it with a pillar.

10.111.d: वज्रेण हि वर्त्रहा वर्त्रमस्तरदेवस्य शूशुवानस्यमायाः | वि धर्ष्णो अत्र धर्षता जघन्थाथाभवोमघवन बाह्वोजाः ||
10.111.e: The Vṛtra-slaver with his bolt felled Vṛtra: the magic of the godless, waxen mighty,  Here hast thou, Bold Assailant, boldly conquered. Yea, then thine arms, O Maghavan, were potent.

10.111.d: सचन्त यदुषसः सूर्येण चित्रामस्य केतवो रामविन्दन | आ यन नक्षत्रं दद्र्शे दिवो न पुनर्यतो नकिरद्धा नु वेद ||
10.111.e: When the Dawns come attendant upon Sūrya their rays discover wealth of divers colours.  The Star of heaven is seen as ’twere approaching: none knoweth aught of it as it departeth.

10.111.d: दूरं किल परथमा जग्मुरासामिन्द्रस्य याः परसवेसस्रुरापः | कव सविदग्रं कव बुध्न आसामापोमध्यं कव वो नूनमन्तः ||
10.111.e: Far have they gone, the first of all these waters, the waters that flowed forth when Indra sent them.  Where is their spring, and where is their foundation? Where now, ye Waters, is your inmost centre?

10.111.d: सर्जः सिन्धून्रहिना जग्रसानानादिदेताः पर विविज्रेजवेन | मुमुक्षमाणा उत या मुमुच्रे.अधेदेता नरमन्ते नितिक्ताः ||
10.111.e: Thou didst free rivers swallowed by the Dragon; and rapidly they set themselves in motion,  Those that were loosed and those that longed for freedom. Excited now to speed they run unresting.

10.111.d: सध्रीचीः सिन्धुमुशतीरिवायन सनाज्जार आरितःपूर्भिदासाम | अस्तमा ते पार्थिवा वसून्यस्मे जग्मुःसून्र्ता इन्द्र पूर्वीः ||
10.111.e: Yearning together they have sped to Sindhu: the Fort-destroyer, praised, of old, hath loved them.  Indra, may thy terrestrial treasures reach us, and our full songs of joy approach thy dwelling.

10.112.d: इन्द्र पिब परतिकामं सुतस्य परातःसावस्तव हिपूर्वपीतिः | हर्षस्व हन्तवे शूर शत्रूनुक्थेभिष टेवीर्या पर बरवाम ||
10.112.e: DRINK of the juice, O Indra, at thy plea. sure, for thy first draught is early morn's libation.  Rejoice, that thou mayst slay our foes, O Hero, and we with lauds will tell thy mighty exploits.

10.112.d: यस्ते रथो मनसो जवीयानेन्द्र तेन सोमपेयाय याहि | तूयमा ते हरयः पर दरवन्तु येभिर्यासि वर्षभिर्मन्दमानः ||
10.112.e: Thou hast a car more swift than thought, O Indra; thercon come hither, come to drink the Soma.  Let thy Bay Steeds, thy Stallions, hasten hither, with whom thou cornest nigh and art delighted.

10.112.d: हरित्वता वर्चसा सूर्यस्य शरेष्ठै रूपैस्तन्वंस्पर्शयस्व | अस्माभिरिन्द्र सखिभिर्हुवानः सध्रीचीनोमादयस्वा निषद्य ||
10.112.e: Deck out thy body with the fairest colours, with golden splendour of the Sun adorn it.  O Indra, turn thee hitherward invited by us thy friends; be seated and be joyful.

10.112.d: यस्य तयत ते महिमानं मदेष्विमे मही रोदसीनाविविक्ताम | तदोक आ हरिभिरिन्द्र युक्तैः परियेभिर्याहि परियमन्नमछ ||
10.112.e: O thou whose grandeur in thy festive transports not even these two great worlds have comprehended.  Come, Indra, with thy dear Bay Horses harnessed, come to our dwelling and the food thou lovest.

10.112.d: यस्य शश्वत पपिवानिन्द्र शत्रूननानुक्र्त्या रण्याचकर्थ | स ते पुरन्धिं तविषीमियर्ति स ते मदायसुत इन्द्र सोमः ||
10.112.e: Pressed for thy joyous banquet is the Soma, Soma whereof thou, Indra, ever drinking,  Hast waged unequalled battles with thy foemen, which prompts the mighty flow of thine abundance.

10.112.d: इदं ते पात्रं सनवित्तमिन्द्र पिबा सोममेना शतक्रतो | पूर्ण आहावो मदिरस्य मध्वो यं विश्व इदभिहर्यन्तिदेवाः ||
10.112.e: Found from of old is this thy cup, O Indra: Śatakratu, drink therefrom the Soma.  Filled is the beaker with the meath that gladdens, the beaker which all Deities delight in.

10.112.d: वि हि तवामिन्द्र पुरुधा जनासो हितप्रयसो वर्षभह्वयन्ते | अस्माकं ते मधुमत्तमानीमा भुवन सवना तेषुहर्य ||
10.112.e: From many a side with proffered entertainment the folk are calling thee, O Mighty Indra.  These our libations shall for thee be richest in sweet meath: dvink thereof and find them pleasant.

10.112.d: पर त इन्द्र पूर्व्याणि पर नूनं वीर्या वोचं परथमाक्र्तानि | सतीनमन्युरश्रथायो अद्रिं सुवेदनामक्र्णोर्ब्रह्मणे गाम ||
10.112.e: I will declare thy deeds of old, O Indra, the mighty acts which thou hast first accomplished.  In genuine wrath thou loosenedst the mountain so that the Brahman easily found the cattle.

10.112.d: नि षु सीद गणपते गणेषु तवामाहुर्विप्रतमंकवीनाम | न रते तवत करियते किं चनारे महामर्कंमघवञ्चित्रमर्च ||
10.112.e: Lord of the hosts, amid our bands be seated: they call thee greatest Sage among the sages.  Nothing is done, even far away, without thee: great, wondrous, Maghavan, is the hymn I sing thee.

10.112.d: अभिख्या नो मघवन नाधमानान सखे बोधि वसुपतेसखीनाम | रणं कर्धि रणक्र्त सत्यशुष्माभक्ते चिदाभजा राये अस्मान ||
10.112.e: Aim of our eyes be thou, for we implore thee, O Maghavan, Friend of friends and Lord of treasures.  Fight, Warrior strong in truth, fight thou the battle: give us our share of undivided riches.

10.113.d: तमस्य दयावाप्र्थिवी सचेतसा विश्वेभिर्देवैरनुशुष्ममावताम | यदैत कर्ण्वानो महिमानमिन्द्रियम्पीत्वी सोमस्य करतुमानवर्धत ||
10.113.e: THE Heavens and the Earth accordant with all Gods encouraged graciously that vigorous might of his.  When he came showing forth his majesty and power, he drank of Soma juice and waxed exceeding strong.

10.113.d: तमस्य विष्णुर्महिमानमोजसांशुं दधन्वान मधुनोवि रप्शते | देवेभिरिन्द्रो मघवा सयावभिर्व्र्त्रंजघन्वानभवद वरेण्यः ||
10.113.e: This majesty of his Viṣṇu extols and lauds, making the stalCthat gives the meath flow forth with inight.  When Indra Maghavan with those who followed him had smitten Vṛtra he deserved the choice of Gods.

10.113.d: वर्त्रेण यदहिना बिभ्रदायुधा समस्थिथा युधयेशंसमाविदे | विश्वे ते अत्र मरुतः सह तमनावर्धन्नुग्र महिमानमिन्द्रियम ||
10.113.e: When, bearing warlike weapons, fain to win thee praise, thou mettest Vṛtra, yea, the Dragon, for the fight,  Then all the Maruts who were gathered with dice there extolled, O Mighty One, thy powerful majesty.

10.113.d: जज्ञान एव वयबाधत सप्र्धः परापश्यद वीरो अभिपौंस्यं रणम | अव्र्श्चदद्रिमव सस्यदः सर्जदस्तभ्नान नाकं सवपस्यया पर्थुम ||
10.113.e: Soon as he sprang to life he forced asun. der hosts: forward the Hero looked to manly deed and war.  He cleft the rock, he let concurrent streams flow forth, and with his skilful art stablished the heavens' wide vault.

10.113.d: आदिन्द्रः सत्रा तविषीरपत्यत वरीयो दयावाप्र्थिवीबाधत | अवाभरद धर्षितो वज्रमायसं शेवं मित्रायवरुणाय दाशुषे ||
10.113.e: Indra hath evermore possessed surpassing power: he forced, far from each other, heaven and earth apart.  He hurled impetuous down his iron thunderbolt, a joy to Varuṇa's and Mitra's worshipper.

10.113.d: इन्द्रस्यात्र तविषीभ्यो विरप्शिन रघायतो अरंहयन्तमन्यवे | वर्त्रं यदुग्रो वयव्र्श्चदोजसापो बिभ्रतन्तमसा परीव्र्तम ||
10.113.e: Then to the mighty powers of Indra, to his wrath, his the fierce Stormer, loud of voice, they came with speed;  What time the Potent One rent Vṛtra with his strength, who held the waters back, whom darkness compassed round.

10.113.d: या वीर्याणि परथमानि कर्त्वा महित्वेभिर्यतमानौसमीयतुः | धवान्तं तमो.अव दध्वसे हत इन्द्रो मह्नापूर्वहूतावपत्यत ||
10.113.e: Even in the first of those heroic acts which they who strove together came with might to execute,  Deep darkness fell upon the slain, and Indra won by victory the right of being first invoked.

10.113.d: विश्वे देवासो अध वर्ष्ण्यानि ते.अवर्धयन सोमवत्यावचस्यया | रद्धं वर्त्रमहिमिन्द्रस्य हन्मनाग्निर्नजम्भैस्त्र्ष्वन्नमावयत ||
10.113.e: Then all the Gods extolled, with eloquence inspired by draughts of Soma juice, thy deeds of manly might.  As Agni eats the dry food with his tcetlv, he ate Vṛtra, the Dragon, maimed by Indra's deadly dart.

10.113.d: भूरि दक्षेभिर्वचनेभिरकवभिः सख्येभिः सख्यानिप्र वोचत | इन्द्रो धुनिं च चुमुरिं च दम्भयञ्छ्रद्धामनस्या शर्णुते दभीतये ||
10.113.e: Proclaim his many friendships, met with friendship, made with singers, with the skilful and the eloquent.  Indra, when he subdues Dhuni and Cumuri, lists to Dabhīti for his faithful spirit's sake.

10.113.d: तवं पुरूण्या भरा सवश्व्या येभिर्मंसै निवचनानिशंसन | सुगेभिर्विश्वा दुरिता तरेम विदो षु ण उर्वियागाधमद्य ||
10.113.e: Give riches manifold with noble horses, to be remembered while my songs address thee.  May we by easy paths pass all our troubles: find us this day a ford wide and extensive.

10.114.d: घर्मा समन्ता तरिव्र्तं वयापतुस्तयोर्जुष्टिम्मातरिश्वा जगाम | दिवस पयो दिधिषाणा अवेषन विदुर्देवाः सहसामानमर्कम ||
10.114.e: Two perfect springs of heat pervade the Threefold, and come for their delight is Mātariśvan.  Craving the milk of heaven the Gods are present: well do they know the praisesong and the Sāman.

10.114.d: तिस्रो देष्ट्राय निरतीरुपासते दीर्घश्रुतो वि हिजानन्ति वह्नयः | तासां नि चिक्युः कवयो निदानम्परेषु या गुह्येषु वरतेषु ||
10.114.e: The priests beard far away, as they are ordered, serve the three Nirrtis, for well they know them.  Sages have traced the cause that first produced them, dwelling in distant and mysterious chambers.

10.114.d: चतुष्कपर्दा युवतिः सुपेशा घर्तप्रतीका वयुनानि वस्ते | तस्यां सुपर्णा वर्षणा नि षेदतुर्यत्र देवा दधिरेभागधेयम ||
10.114.e: The Youthful One, well-shaped, with four locks braided, brightened with oil, puts on the ordinances.  Two Birds of mighty power are seated near her, there where the Deities receive their portion.

10.114.d: एकः सुपर्णः स समुद्रमा विवेष स इदं विश्वम्भुवनं वि चष्टे | तं पाकेन मनसापश्यमन्तितस्तम्माता रेळि स उ रेळि मातरम ||
10.114.e: One of these Birds hath passed into the sea of air: thence he looks round and views this universal world.  With simple heart I have beheld him from anear: his Mother kisses him and he returns her kiss.

10.114.d: सुपर्णं विप्राः कवयो वचोभिरेकं सन्तं बहुधाकल्पयन्ति | छन्दांसि च दधतो अध्वरेषु गरहान सोमस्यमिमते दवादश ||
10.114.e: Him with fair wings though only One in nature, wise singers shape, with songs, in many figures.  While they at sacrifices fix the metres, they measure out twelve chalices of Soma.

10.114.d: षट्त्रिंशांश्च चतुरः कल्पयन्तश्छन्दांसि चदधत आद्वादशम | यज्ञं विमाय कवयो मनीषर्क्सामाभ्यां पर रथं वर्तयन्ति ||
10.114.e: While they arrange the four and six-and-thirty, and duly order, up to twelve, the measures,  Having disposed the sacrifice thoughtful sages send the Car forward with the Rc and Sāman.

10.114.d: चतुर्दशान्ये महिमानो अस्य तं धीरा वाचा पर णयन्तिसप्त | आप्नानं तीर्थं क इह पर वोचद येन पथाप्रपिबन्ते सुतस्य ||
10.114.e: The Chariot's majesties are fourteen others: seven sages lead it onward with their Voices.  Who will declare to us the ford Apnana, the path whereby they drink first draughts of Soma?

10.114.d: सहस्रधा पञ्चदशान्युक्था यावद दयावाप्र्थिवीतावदित तत | सहस्रधा महिमानः सहस्रं यावद्ब्रह्म विष्ठितं तावती वाक ||
10.114.e: The fifteen lauds are in a thousand places that is as vast as heaven and earth in measure.  A thousand spots contain the mighty thousand. Vāk spreadeth forth as far as Prayer extendeth.

10.114.d: कश्छन्दसां योगमा वेद धीरः को धिष्ण्यां परतिवाचं पपाद | कं रत्विजामष्टमं शूरमाहुर्हरीिन्द्रस्य नि चिकाय कः सवित ||
10.114.e: What sage hath learned the metres' application? Who hath gained Vāk, the spirit's aim and object?  Which ministering priest is called eighth Hero? Who then hath tracked the two Bay Steeds of Indra?

10.114.d: भूम्या अन्तं पर्येके चरन्ति रथस्य धूर्षु युक्तासोस्थुः | शरमस्य दायं वि भजन्त्येभ्यो यदा यमो भवतिहर्म्ये हितः ||
10.114.e: Yoked to his chariot-pole there stood the Coursers: they only travel round earth's farthest limits.  These, when their driver in his home is settled, receive the allotted meed of their exertion.

10.115.d: चित्र इच्छिशोस्तरुणस्य वक्षथो न यो मातरावप्येतिधातवे | अनूधा यदि जीजनदधा च नु ववक्ष सद्योमहि दूत्यं चरन ||
10.115.e: VERILY wondrous is the tender Youngling's growth who never draweth nigh to drink his Mothers' milk.  As soon as she who hath no udder bore him, he, faring on his great errand, suddenly grew strong.

10.115.d: अग्निर्ह नाम धायि दन्नपस्तमः सं यो वना युवतेभस्मना दता | अभिप्रमुरा जुह्वा सवध्वर इनो नप्रोथमानो यवसे वर्षा ||
10.115.e: Then Agni was his name, most active to bestow, gathering up the trees with his consuming tooth;  Skilled in fair sacrifice, armed with destroying tongue, impetuous as a bull that snorteth in the mead.

10.115.d: तं वो विं न दरुषदं देवमन्धस इन्दुं परोथन्तम्प्रवपन्तमर्णवम | आसा वह्निं न शोचिषा विरप्शिनम्महिव्रतं न सरजन्तमध्वनः ||
10.115.e: Praise him, yourGod who, bird-like, rests upon a tree, scattering drops of juice and pouring forth his flood,  Speaking aloud with flame as with his lips a priest, and broadening his paths like one of high command.

10.115.d: वि यस्य ते जरयसानस्याजर धक्षोर्न वाताः परि सन्त्यच्युताः | आ रण्वासो युयुधयो न सत्वनं तरितंनशन्त पर शिषन्त इष्टये ||
10.115.e: Thou Everlasting, whom, far-striding fain to burn, the winds, uninterrupted, never overcome,  They have approached, as warriors eager for the fight, heroic Trita, guiding him to gain his wish.

10.115.d: स इदग्निः कन्व्वतमः कण्वसखार्यः परस्यान्तरस्यतरुषः | अग्निः पातु गर्णतो अग्निः सूरीनग्निर्ददातुतेषामवो नः ||
10.115.e: This Agni is the best of Kaṇvas, Kaṇvas' Friend, Conqueror of the foe whether afar or near.  May Agni guard the singers, guard the princes well: may Agni grant to us our princes' gracious help.

10.115.d: वाजिन्तमाय सह्यसे सुपित्र्य तर्षु चयवानो अनु जातवेदसे | अनुद्रे चिद यो धर्षता वरं सते महिन्तमाय धन्वनेदविष्यते ||
10.115.e: Do thou, Supitrya, swiftly following, make thyself the lord of Jātavedas, mightiest of all,  Who surely gives a boon even in thirsty land most powerful, prepared to aid us in the wilds.

10.115.d: एवाग्निर्मर्तैः सह सूरिभिर्वसु षटवे सहसः सूनरोन्र्भिः | मित्रासो न ये सुधिता रतायवो दयावो न दयुम्नैरभि सन्ति मानुषान ||
10.115.e: Thus noble Agni with princes and mortal men is lauded, excellent for conquering strength with chiefs,  Men who are well-disposed as friends and true to Law, even as the heavens in majesty surpass mankind.

10.115.d: ऊर्जो नपात सहसावन्निति तवोपस्तुतस्य वन्दते वर्षा वाक | तवां सतोषाम तवया सुवीरा दराघीय आयुः परतरन्दधानाः ||
10.115.e: O Son of Strength, Victorious, with this title Upastuta's most potent voice reveres thee.  Blest with brave sons by thee we will extol thee, and lengthen out the days of our existence.

10.115.d: इति तवाग्ने वर्ष्टिहव्यस्य पुत्रा उपस्तुतास रषयो.अवोचन | तांश्च पाहि गर्णतश्च सूरीन वषड वषळ इत्यूर्ध्वासो अनक्षन नमो नम इत्यूर्ध्वासो अनक्षन ||
10.115.e: Thus, Agni, have the sons of Vrstihavya, the Ṛṣis, the Upastutas invoked thee.  Protect them, guard the singers and the princes. With Vaṣaṭ! have they come, with hands uplifted, with their uplifted hands and cries of Glory!

10.116.d: पिबा सोमं महत इन्द्रियाय पिबा वर्त्राय हन्तवेशविष्ठ | पिब राये शवसे हूयमानः पिब मध्वस्त्र्पदिन्द्रा वर्षस्व ||
10.116.e: DRINK Soma juice for mighty power and vigour, drink, Strongest One, that thou mayst smite down Vṛtra.  Drink thou, invoked, for strength, and riches: drink thou thy fill of meath and pour it down, O Indra.

10.116.d: अस्य पिब कषुमतः परस्थितस्येन्द्र सोमस्य वरमासुतश्य | सवस्तिदा मनसा मादयस्वार्वाचीनो रेवतेसौभगाय ||
10.116.e: Drink of the foodful juice stirred into motion, drink what thou choosest of the flowing Soma.  Giver of weal, be joyful in thy spirit, and turn thee hitherward to bless and prosper.

10.116.d: ममत्तु तवा दिव्यः सोम इन्द्र ममत्तु यः सूयतेपार्थिवेषु | ममत्तु येन वरिवश्चकर्थ ममत्तु येननिरिणासि शत्रून ||
10.116.e: Let heavenly Soma gladden thee, O Indra, let that effused among mankind delight thee.  Rejoice in that whereby thou gavest freedom, and that whereby thou conquerest thy foemen.

10.116.d: आ दविबर्हा अमिनो यात्विन्द्रो वर्षा हरिभ्यां परिषिक्तमन्धः | गव्या सुतस्य परभ्र्तस्य मध्वः सत्रा खेदामरुशहा वर्षस्व ||
10.116.e: Let Indra come, impetuous, doubly mighty, to the poured juice, the Bull, with two Bay Coursers.  With juices pressed in milk, with meath presented, glut evermore thy bolt, O Foe-destroyer.

10.116.d: नि तिग्मानि भराशयन भराश्यान्यव सथिरा तनुहियातुजूनाम | उग्राय ते सहो बलं ददामि परतीत्याशत्रून विगदेषु वर्श्च ||
10.116.e: Dash down, outffaming their sharp flaming weapons, the strong-holds of the men urged on by demons.  I give thee, Mighty One, great strength and conquest: go, meet thy foes and rend them in the battle.

10.116.d: वयर्य इन्द्र तनुहि शरवांस्योज सथिरेव धन्वनोऽभिमातीः | अस्मद्र्यग वाव्र्धानः सहोभिरनिभ्र्ष्टस्तन्वं वाव्र्धस्व ||
10.116.e: Extend afar the votary's fame and glory, as the firm archer's strength drives off the foeman.  Ranged on our side, grown strong in might that conquers, never defeated, still increase thy body.

10.116.d: इदं हविर्मघवन तुभ्यं रातं परति सम्राळ अह्र्णानोग्र्भाय | तुभ्यं सुतो मघवन तुभ्यं पक्वो.अद्धीन्द्र पिबच परस्थितस्य ||
10.116.e: To thee have we presented this oblation: accept it, Sovran Ruler, free from anger.  Juice, Maghavan, for thee is pressed and ripened: eat, Indra, drink of that which stirs to meet thee.

10.116.d: अद्धीदिन्द्र परस्थितेमा हवींषि चनो दधिष्व पचतोतसोमम | परयस्वन्तः परति हर्यामसि तवा सत्याः सन्तुयजमानस्य कामाः ||
10.116.e: Eat, Indra, these oblations which approach thee: be pleased with food made ready and with Soma.  With entertainment we receive thee friendly: effectual be the sacrificer's wishes.

10.116.d: परेन्द्राग्निभ्यां सुवचस्यामियर्मि सिन्धाविव परेरयंनावमर्कैः | अया इव परि चरन्ति देवा ये अस्मभ्यन्धनदा उद्भिदश्च ||
10.116.e: I send sweet speech to Indra and to Agni: with hymns I speed it like a boat through waters.  Even thus, the Gods seem moving round about me, the fountains and bestowers of our riches.

10.117.d: न वा उ देवाः कषुधमिद वधं ददुरुताशितमुपगछन्ति मर्त्यवः | उतो रयिः पर्णतो नोप दस्यत्युताप्र्णन्मर्डितारं न विन्दते ||
10.117.e: THE Gods have not ordained hunger to be our death: even to the well-fed man comes death in varied shape.  The riches of the liberal never waste away, while he who will not give finds none to comfort him.

10.117.d: य आध्राय चकमानाय पित्वो.अन्नवान सन्रफितायोपजग्मुषे | सथिरं मनः कर्णुते सेवते पुरोतोचित स मर्डितारं न विन्दते ||
10.117.e: The man with food in store who, when the needy comes in miserable case begging for bread to eat,  Hardens his heart against him-even when of old he did him service-finds not one to comfort him.

10.117.d: स इद भोजो यो गर्हवे ददात्यन्नकामाय चरते कर्शाय | अरमस्मै भवति यामहूता उतापरीषु कर्णुते सखायम ||
10.117.e: Bounteous is he who gives unto the beggar who comes to him in want of food and feeble.  Success attends him in the shout of battle. He makes a friend of him in future troubles.

10.117.d: न स सखा यो न ददाति सख्ये सचाभुवे सचमानायपित्वः | अपास्मात परेयान न तदोको अस्ति पर्णन्तमन्यमरणं चिदिचःेत ||
10.117.e: No friend is he who to his friend and comrade who comes imploring food, will offer nothing.  Let him depart-no home is that to rest in-, and rather seek a stranger to support him.

10.117.d: पर्णीयादिन नाधमानाय तव्यान दराघीयांसमनुपश्येत पन्थाम | ओ हि वर्तन्ते रथ्येव चक्रान्यम-अन्यमुप तिष्ठन्त रायः ||
10.117.e: Let the rich satisfy the poor implorer, and bend his eye upon a longer pathway.  Riches come now to one, now to another, and like the wheels of cars are ever rolling.

10.117.d: मोघमन्नं विन्दते अप्रचेताः सत्यं बरवीमि वध इत सतस्य | नार्यमणं पुष्यति नो सखायं केवलाघो भवतिकेवलादी ||
10.117.e: The foolish man wins food with fruitless labour: that food -I speak the truth- shall be his ruin.  He feeds no trusty friend, no man to love him. All guilt is he who eats with no partaker.

10.117.d: कर्षन्नित फाल आशितं कर्णोति यन्नध्वानमप वर्ङकतेचरित्रैः | वदन बरह्मावदतो वनीयान पर्णन्नापिरप्र्णन्तमभि षयात ||
10.117.e: The ploughshare ploughing makes the food that feeds us, and with its feet cuts through the path it follows.  Better the speaking than the silent Brahman: the liberal friend outyalues him who gives not.

10.117.d: एकपाद भूयो दविपदो वि चक्रमे दविपात तरिपादमभ्येतिपश्चात | चतुष्पादेति दविपदामभिस्वरे सम्पश्यन्पङकतीरुपतिष्ठमानः ||
10.117.e: He with one foot hath far outrun the biped, and the two-footed catches the three-footed.  Four-footed creatures come when bipeds call them, and stand and look where five are met together.

10.117.d: समौ चिद धस्तौ न समं विविष्टः सम्मातरा चिन नसमं दुहाते | यमयोश्चिन न समा वीर्याणि जञाती चित्सन्तौ न समं पर्णीतः ||
10.117.e: The hands are both alike: their labour differs. The yield of sister milch-kine is unequal.  Twins even diffier in their strength and vigour: two, even kinsmen, differ in their bounty.

10.118.d: अग्ने हंसि नयत्रिणं दीद्यन मर्त्येष्वा | सवे कषयेशुचिव्रत ||
10.118.e: AGNI, refulgent among men thou slayest the devouring fiend,  Bright Ruler in thine own abode.

10.118.d: उत तिष्ठसि सवाहुतो घर्तानि परति मोदसे | यत तवा सरुचःसमस्थिरन ||
10.118.e: Thou springest up when worshipped well the drops of butter are thy joy  When ladies are brought near to thee.

10.118.d: स आहुतो वि रोचते.अग्निरीळेन्यो गिरा | सरुचा परतीकमज्यते ||
10.118.e: Honoured with gifts he shines afar, Agni adorable with song:  The dripping ladle balms his face.
Agni with honey in his mouth, honoured with gifts, is balmed with oil,  Refulgent in his wealth of light.

10.118.d: जरमाणः समिध्यसे देवेभ्यो हव्यवाहन | तं तवा हवन्तमर्त्याः ||
10.118.e: Praised by our hymns thou kindlest thee, Oblation-bearer, for the Gods  As such do mortals call on thee.

10.118.d: तं मर्ता अमर्त्यं घर्तेनाग्निं सपर्यत | अदाभ्यंग्र्हपतिम ||
10.118.e: To that Immortal Agni pay worship with oil, ye mortal men,—  Lord of the house, whom none deceives.

10.118.d: अदाभ्येन शोचिषाग्ने रक्षस्त्वं दह | गोपा रतस्यदीदिहि ||
10.118.e: O Agni, burn the Rākṣasas with thine unconquerable flame  Shine guardian of Eternal Law.

10.118.d: स तवमग्ने परतीकेन परत्योष यातुधान्यः | उरुक्षयेषुदीद्यत ||
10.118.e: So, Agni, with thy glowing face burn fierce against the female fiends,  Shining among Uruksayas.

10.118.d: तं तवा गीर्भिरुरुक्षया हव्यवाहं समीधिरे | यजिष्ठं मानुषे जने ||
10.118.e: Uruksayas have kindled thee, Oblation-bearer, thee, with hymns.  Best Worshipper among mankind.

10.119.d: इति वा इति मे मनो गामश्वं सनुयामिति | कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ||
10.119.e: THIS, even this was my resolve, to win a cow, to win a steed:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: पर वाता इव दोधत उन मा पीता अयंसत | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: Like violent gusts of wind the draughts that I have drunk have lifted me  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: उन मा पीता अयंसत रथमश्वा इवाशवः | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: The draughts I drank have borne me up, as fleet-foot horses draw a car:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: उप मा मतिरस्थित वाश्रा पुत्रमिव परियम | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: The hymn hath reached me, like a cow who lows to meet her darling calf:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: अहं तष्टेव वन्धुरं पर्यचामि हर्दा मतिम | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: As a wright bends a chariot-seat so round my heart I bend the hymn:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: नहि मे अक्षिपच्चनाछान्त्सुः पञ्च कर्ष्टयः | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: Not as a mote within the eye count the Five Tribes of men with me:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: नहि मे रोदसी उभे अन्यं पक्षं चन परति | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: The heavens and earth themselves have not grown equal to one half of me  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: अभि दयां महिना भुवमभीमां पर्थिवीं महीम | कुवित... ||
10.119.e: I in my grandeur have surpassed the heavens and all this spacious earth  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: हन्ताहं पर्थिवीमिमां नि दधानीह वेह वा | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: Aha! this spacious earth will I deposit either here or there  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: ओषमित पर्थिवीमहं जङघनानीह वेह वा | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: In one short moment will I smite the earth in fury here or there:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.119.d: दिवि मे अन्यः पक्षो.अधो अन्यमचीक्र्षम | कुवित ... ||
10.119.e: One of my flanks is in the sky; I let the other trail below:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
1, greatest of the Mighty Ones, am lifted to the firmament:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
I seek the worshipper's abode; oblation-bearer to the Gods:  Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

10.120.d: तदिदास भुवनेषु जयेष्ठं यतो जज्ञ उग्रस्त्वेषन्र्म्णः | सद्यो जज्ञानो नि रिणाति शत्रूननु यंविश्वे मदन्त्यूमाः ||
10.120.e: IN all the worlds That was the Best and Highest whence sprang the Mighty Gods, of splendid valour.  As soon as born he overcomes his foemen, be in whom all who lend him aid are joyful.

10.120.d: वाव्र्धानः शवसा भूर्योजाः शत्रुर्दासाय भियसन्दधाति | अव्यनच्च वयनच्च सस्नि सं ते नवन्त परभ्र्तामदेषु ||
10.120.e: Grown mighty in his strength, with ample vigour, he as a foe strikes fear into the Dāsa,  Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation.

10.120.d: तवे करतुमपि वर्ञ्जन्ति विश्वे दविर्यदेते तरिर्भवन्त्यूमाः | सवादोः सवादीयः सवादुना सर्जा समदः सुमधु मधुनाभि योधीः ||
10.120.e: All concentrate on thee their mental vigour, what time these, twice or thrice, are thine assistants.  Blend what is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness: win. quickly with our meath that meath in battle.

10.120.d: इति चिद धि तवा धना जयन्तं मदे-मदे अनुमदन्ति विप्राः | ओजीयो धर्ष्णो सथिरमा तनुष्व मा तवा दभन्यातुधाना दुरेवाः ||
10.120.e: Therefore in thee too, thou who winnest riches, at every banquet are the sages joyful.  With mightier power, Bold God, extend thy firmness: let not malignant Yātudhānas harm thee.

10.120.d: तवया वयं शाशद्महे रणेषु परपश्यन्तो युधेन्यानिभूरि | चोदयामि त आयुधा वचोभिः सं ते शिशामिब्रह्मणा वयांसि ||
10.120.e: Proudly we put our trust in thee in battles, when we behold great wealth the prize of combat.  I with my words impel thy weapons onward, and sharpen with my prayer thy vital vigour.

10.120.d: सतुषेय्यं पुरुवर्पसं रभ्वमिनतममाप्त्यमाप्त्यानाम | आ दर्षते शवसा सप्त दानून पर साक्षते परतिमानानिभूरि ||
10.120.e: Worthy of praises, many-shaped, most skilful, most energetic, Āptya of the Aptyas:  He with his might destroys the seven Danus, subduing many who were deemed his equals.

10.120.d: नि तद दधिषे.अवरं परं च यस्मिन्नाविथावसा दुरोणे | आ मातरा सथापयसे जिगत्नू अत इनोषि कर्वरा पुरूणि ||
10.120.e: Thou in that house which thy protection guardeth bestowest wealth, the higher and the lower.  Thou stablishest the two much-wandering Mothers, and bringest many deeds to their completion.

10.120.d: इमा बरह्म बर्हद्दिवो विवक्तीन्द्राय शूषमग्रियःस्वर्षाः | महो गोत्रस्य कषयति सवराजो दुरश्च विश्वाव्र्णोदप सवाः ||
10.120.e: Brhaddiva, the foremost of light-winners, repeats these holy prayers, this strength of Indra.  He rules the great self-luminous fold of cattle, and all the doors of light hath he thrown open.

10.120.d: एवा महान बर्हद्दिवो अथर्वावोचत सवां तन्वमिन्द्रमेव | सवसारो मातरिभ्वरीररिप्रा हिन्वन्ति च शवसावर्धयन्ति च ||
10.120.e: Thus hath Brhaddiva, the great Atharvan, spoken to Indra as himself in person.  The spotless Sisters, they who are his Mothers, with power exalt him and impel him onward.

10.121.d: हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेकासीत | स दाधार पर्थिवीं दयामुतेमां कस्मै देवायहविषा विधेम ||
10.121.e: IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, born Only Lord of all created beings.  He fixed and holdeth up this earth and heaven. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: य आत्मदा बलदा यस्य विश्व उपासते परशिषं यस्यदेवाः | यस्य छायाम्र्तं यस्य मर्त्युः कस्मै देवायहविषा विधेम ||
10.121.e: Giver of vital breath, of power and vigour, he whose commandments all the Gods acknowledge -.  The Lord of death, whose shade is life immortal. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: यः पराणतो निमिषतो महित्वैक इद राजा जगतो बभूव | य ईशे अस्य दविपदश्चतुष्पदः कस्मै देवाय हविषाविधेम ||
10.121.e: Who by his grandeur hath become Sole Ruler of all the moving world that breathes and slumbers;  He who is Loord of men and Lord of cattle. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: यस्येमे हिमवन्तो महित्वा यस्य समुद्रं रसया सहाहुः | यस्येमाः परदिशो यस्य बाहू कस्मै देवाय हविषाविधेम ||
10.121.e: His, through his might, are these snow-covered mountains, and men call sea and Rasā his possession:  His arms are these, his are these heavenly regions. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: येन दयौरुग्रा पर्थिवी च दर्ळ्हा येन सव सतभितं येननाकः | यो अन्तरिक्षे रजसो विमानः कस्मै देवायहविषा विधेम ||
10.121.e: By him the heavens are strong and earth is stedfast, by him light's realm and sky-vault are supported:  By him the regions in mid-air were measured. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: यं करन्दसी अवसा तस्तभाने अभ्यैक्षेतां मनसारेजमाने | यत्राधि सूर उदितो विभाति कस्मै देवायहविषा विधेम ||
10.121.e: To him, supported by his help, two armies embattled look while trembling in their spirit,  When over them the risen Sun is shining. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: आपो ह यद बर्हतीर्विश्वमायन गर्भं दधानाजनयन्तीरग्निम | ततो देवानां समवर्ततासुरेकःकस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ||
10.121.e: What time the mighty waters came, containing the universal germ, producing Agni,  Thence sprang the Gods’ one spirit into being. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: यश्चिदापो महिना पर्यपश्यद दक्षं दधानाजनयन्तीर्यज्ञम | यो देवेष्वधि देव एक आसीत कस्मैदेवाय हविषा विधेम ||
10.121.e: He in his might surveyed the floods containing productive force and generating Worship.  He is the God of gods, and none beside him. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: मा नो हिंसीज्जनिता यः पर्थिव्या यो वा दिवंसत्यधर्मा जजान | यश्चापश्चन्द्रा बर्हतीर्जजानकस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ||
10.121.e: Neer may he harm us who is earth's Begetter, nor he whose laws are sure, the heavens' Creator,  He who brought forth the great and lucid waters. What God shall we adore with our oblation?

10.121.d: परजापते न तवदेतान्यन्यो विश्वा जातानि परि ताबभूव | यत्कामास्ते जुहुमस्तन नो अस्तु वयं सयाम पतयोरयीणाम ||
10.121.e: Prajāpati! thou only comprehendest all these created things, and none beside thee.  Grant us our hearts' desire when we invoke thee: may we have store of riches in possession.

10.122.d: वसुं न चित्रमहसं गर्णीषे वामं शेवमतिथिमद्विषेण्यम | स रासते शुरुधो विश्वधायसो.अग्निर्होताग्र्हपतिः सुवीर्यम ||
10.122.e: I PRAISE the God of wondrous might like Indra, the lovely pleasant Guest whom all must welcome.  May Agni, Priest and Master of the household, give hero strength and all-sustaining riches.

10.122.d: जुषाणो अग्ने परति हर्य मे वचो विश्वानि विद्वान वयुनानिसुक्रतो | घर्तनिर्णिग बरह्मणे गातुमेरय तव देवाजनयन्ननु वरतम ||
10.122.e: O Agni, graciously accept this song of mine, thou passing-wise who knowest every ordinance.  Enwrapped in holy oil further the course of prayer: the Gods bestow according to thy holy law.

10.122.d: सप्त धामानि परियन्नमर्त्यो दाशद दाशुषे सुक्र्तेमामहस्व | सुवीरेण रयिणाग्ने सवाभुवा यस्त आनट्समिधा तं जुषस्व ||
10.122.e: Immortal, wandering round the seven stations, give, a liberal Giver, to the pious worshipper,  Wealth, Agni, with brave sons and ready for his use: welcome the man who comes with fuel unto thee.

10.122.d: यज्ञस्य केतुं परथमं पुरोहितं हविष्मन्त ईळते सप्तवाजिनम | शर्ण्वन्तमग्निं घर्तप्र्ष्ठमुक्षणम्प्र्णन्तं देवं पर्णते सुवीर्यम ||
10.122.e: The seven who bring oblations worship thee, the Strong, the first, the Great Chief Priest, Ensign of sacrifice,  The oil-anointed Bull, Agni who hears, who sends as God full hero strength to him who freely gives.

10.122.d: टवं दूतः परथमो वरेण्यः स हूयमानो अम्र्तायमत्स्व | तवां मर्जयन मरुतो दाशुषो गर्हे तवां सतोमेभिर्भ्र्गवो वि रुरुचुः ||
10.122.e: First messenger art thou, meet for election: drink thou thy fill invited to the Anirta,  The Maruts in the votary's house adorned thee; with lauds the Bhṛgus gave thee light and glory.

10.122.d: इषं दुहन सुदुघां विश्वधायसं यज्ञप्रियेयजमानाय सुक्रतो | अग्ने घर्तस्नुस्त्रिरतानि दीद्यद्वर्तिर्यज्ञं परियन सुक्रतूयसे ||
10.122.e: Milking the teeming Cow for all-sustaining food. O Wise One, for the worship-loving worshipper,  Thou, Agni, dropping oil, thrice lighting works of Law, showest thy wisdom circling home and sacrifice.

10.122.d: तवामिदस्या उषसो वयुष्टिषु दूतं कर्ण्वाना अयजन्तमानुषाः | तवां देवा महयाय्याय वाव्र्धुराज्यमग्नेनिम्र्जन्तो अध्वरे ||
10.122.e: They who at flushing of this dawn appointed thee their messenger, these men have paid thee reverence.  Gods strengthened thee for work that must be glorified, Agni, while they made butter pure for sacrifice.

10.122.d: नि तवा वसिष्ठा अह्वन्त वाजिनं गर्णन्तो अग्ने विदथेषुवेधसः | रायस पोषं यजमानेषु धारय यूयं पातस्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ||
10.122.e: Arrangers in our synods, Agni, while they sang Vasisistha s sons have called thee down, the Potent One.  Maintain the growth of wealth with men who sacrifice. Ye Gods, preserve us with your blessings evermore.

10.123.d: अयं वेनश्चोदयत पर्श्निगर्भा जयोतिर्जरायू रजसोविमाने | इममपां संगमे सूर्यस्य शिशुं न विप्रामतिभी रिहन्ति ||
10.123.e: SEE, Vena, born in light, hath driven hither, on chariot of the air, the Calves of Pṛśni.  Singers with hymns caress him as an infant there where the waters and the sunlight mingle.

10.123.d: समुद्रादूर्मिमुदियर्ति वेनो नभोजाः पर्ष्ठंहर्यतस्य दर्शि | रतस्य सानावधि विष्टपि भराट्समानं योनिमभ्यनूषत वराः ||
10.123.e: Vena draws up his wave from out the ocean. mist-born, the fair one's back is made apparent,  Brightly he shone aloft on Order's summit: the hosts sang glory to their common birthplace.

10.123.d: समानं पूर्वीरभि वावशानास्तिष्ठन वत्सस्यमातरः सनीळाः | रतस्य सानावधि चक्रमाणारिहन्ति मध्वो अम्र्तस्य वाणीः ||
10.123.e: Full many, lowing to their joint-possession, dwelling together stood the Darling's Mothers.  Ascending to the lofty height of Order, the bands of singers 'sip the sweets of Amṛta.

10.123.d: जानन्तो रूपमक्र्पन्त विप्रा मर्गस्य घोषं महिषस्य हिग्मन | रतेन यन्तो अधि सिन्धुमस्थुर्विदद गन्धर्वोम्र्तानि नाम ||
10.123.e: Knowing his form, the sages yearned to meet him: they have come nigh to hear the wild Bull's bellow.  Performing sacrifice they reached the river: for the Gandharva found the immortal waters.

10.123.d: अप्सरा जारमुपसिष्मियाणा योषा बिभर्ति परमे वयोमन | चरत परियस्य योनिषु परियः सन सीदत पक्षे हिरण्ययेस वेनः ||
10.123.e: The Apsaras, the Lady, sweetly smiling, supports her Lover in sublimest heaven.  In his Friend's dwelling as a Friend he wanders: he, Vena, rests him on his golden pinion.

10.123.d: नाके सुपर्णमुप यत पतन्तं हर्दा वेनन्तो अभ्यचक्षतत्वा | हिरण्यपक्षं वरुणस्य दूतं यमस्य योनौशकुनं भुरण्युम ||
10.123.e: They gaze on thee with longing in their spirit, as on a strong-winged bird that mounteth sky-ward;  On thee with wings of gold, Varuṇa's envoy, the Bird that hasteneth to the home of Yama.

10.123.d: ऊर्ध्वो गन्धर्वो अधि नाके अस्थात परत्यं चित्रा बिभ्रदस्यायुधानि | वसानो अत्कं सुरभिं दर्शे कं सवर्णनाम जनत परियाणि ||
10.123.e: Erect, to heaven hath the Gandharva mounted, pointing at us his many-coloured weapons;  Clad in sweet raiment beautiful to look on, for he, as light, produceth forms that please us.

10.123.d: दरप्सः समुद्रमभि यज्जिगाति पश्यन गर्ध्रस्य चक्षसाविधर्मन | भानुः शुक्रेण शोचिषा चकानस्त्र्तीये चक्रेरजसि परियाणि ||
10.123.e: When as a spark he cometh near the ocean, still looking with a vulture's eye to heaven,  His lustre, joying in its own bright splendour, maketh dear glories in the lowest region.

10.124.d: इमं नो अग्न उप यज्ञमेहि पञ्चयामं तरिव्र्तंसप्ततन्तुम | असो हव्यवाळ उत नः पुरोगा जयोगेवदीर्घं तम आशयिष्ठाः ||
10.124.e: COME to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions.  Be our oblation-bearer and preceder: thou hast lain long enough in during darkness.

10.124.d: अदेवाद देवः परचता गुहा यन परपश्यमानो अम्र्तत्वमेमि | शिवं यत सन्तमशिवो जहामि सवात सख्यादरणींनाभिमेमि ||
10.124.e: I come a God foreseeing from the godless to immortality by secret pathways,  While I, ungracious one, desert the gracious, leave mine own friends and seek the kin of strangers.

10.124.d: पश्यन्नन्यस्या अतिथिं वयाया रतस्य धाम वि मिमेपुरूणि | शंसामि पित्रे असुराय शेवमयज्ञियाद्यज्ञियं भागमेमि ||
10.124.e: 1, looking to the guest of other lineage, have founded many a rule of Law and Order.  I bid farewell to the Great God, the Father, and, for neglect, obtain my share of worship.

10.124.d: बह्वीः समा अकरमन्तरस्मिन्निन्द्रं वर्णानः पितरंजहामि | अग्निः सोमो वरुणस्ते चयवन्ते पर्यावर्द्राष्ट्रं तदवाम्यायन ||
10.124.e: I tarried many a year within this altar: I leave the Father, for my choice is Indra.  Away pass Agni, Varuṇa and Soma. Rule ever changes: this I come to favour.

10.124.d: निर्माया उ तये असुरा अभूवन तवं च मा वरुण कामयासे | रतेन राजन्नन्र्तं विविञ्चन मम राष्ट्रस्याधिपत्यमेहि ||
10.124.e: These Asuras have lost their powers of magic. But thou, O Varuṇa, if thou dost love me,  O King, discerning truth and right from falsehood, come and be Lord and Ruler of my kingdom.

10.124.d: इदं सवरिदमिदास वाममयं परकाश उर्वन्तरिक्षम | हनाव वर्त्रं निरेहि सोम हविष टवा सन्तं हविषायजाम ||
10.124.e: Here is the light of heaven, here allis lovely; here there is radiance, here is air's wide region.  Let us two slaughter Vṛtra. Forth, O Soma! Thou art oblation: we therewith will serve thee.

10.124.d: कविः कवित्वा दिवि रूपमासजदप्रभूती वरुणो निरपः सर्जत | कषेमं कर्ण्वाना जनयो न सिन्धवश ता अस्यवर्णं शुचयो भरिभ्रति ||
10.124.e: The Sage hath fixed his form by wisdom in the heavens: Varuṇa with no violence let the waters flow.  Like women-folk, the floods that bring prosperity have eau lit his hue and colour as they gleamed and shone.

10.124.d: ता अस्य जयेष्ठमिन्द्रियं सचन्ते ता ईमा कषेतिस्वधया मदन्तीः | ता इं विशो न राजानं वर्णानाबीभत्सुवो अप वर्त्रादतिष्ठन ||
10.124.e: These wait upon his loftiest power and vigour: he dwells in these who triumph in their Godhead;  And they, like people who elect their ruler, have in abhorrence turned away from Vṛtra.

10.124.d: बीभत्सूनां सयुजं हंसमाहुरपां दिव्यानांसख्ये चरन्तम | अनुष्टुभमनु चर्चूर्यमाणमिन्द्रं निचिक्युः कवयो मनीषा ||
10.124.e: They call him Swan, the abhorrent floods' Companion, moving in friendship with celestial Waters.  The poets in their thought have looked on Indra swiftly approaching when Anustup calls him.

10.125.e: I TRAVEL with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Ādityas and All-Gods I wander.  I hold aloft both Varuṇa and Mitra, Indra and Agni, and the Pair of Aśvins.

10.125.d: अहं सोममाहनसं बिभर्म्यहं तवष्टारमुतपूषणं भगम | अहं दधामि दरविणं हविष्मतेसुप्राव्ये यजमानाय सुन्वते ||
10.125.e: I cherish and sustain high-swelling Soma, and Tvaṣṭar I support, Pūṣan, and Bhaga.  I load with wealth the zealous sdcrificer who pours the juice and offers his oblation

10.125.d: अहं राष्ट्री संगमनी वसूनां चिकितुषी परथमायज्ञियानाम | तां मा देवा वयदधुः पुरुत्राभूरिस्थात्रां भूर्यावेशयन्तीम ||
10.125.e: I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those who merit worship.  Thus Gods have stablished me in many places with many homes to enter and abide in.

10.125.d: मया सो अन्नमत्ति यो विपश्यति यः पराणिति य ईंश्र्णोत्युक्तम | अमन्तवो मां त उप कषियन्ति शरुधिश्रुत शरद्धिवं ते वदामि ||
10.125.e: Through me alone all eat the food that feeds them,—each man who sees, brewhes, hears the word outspoken  They know it not, but yet they dwell beside me. Hear, one and all, the truth as I declare it.

10.125.d: अहमेव सवयमिदं वदामि जुष्टं देवेभिरुतमानुषेभिः | यं कामये तं-तमुग्रं कर्णोमि तम्ब्रह्माणं तं रषिं तं सुमेधाम ||
10.125.e: 1, verily, myself announce and utter the word that Gods and men alike shall welcome.  I make the man I love exceeding mighty, make him a sage, a Ṛṣi, and a Brahman.

10.125.d: अहं रुद्राय धनुरा तनोमि बरह्मद्विषे शरवे हन्तवाु | अहं जनाय समदं कर्णोम्यहं दयावाप्र्थिवी आविवेश ||
10.125.e: I bend the bow for Rudra that his arrow may strike and slay the hater of devotion.  I rouse and order battle for the people, and I have penetrated Earth and Heaven.

10.125.d: अहं सुवे पितरमस्य मूर्धन मम योनिरप्स्वन्तः समुद्रे | ततो वि तिष्ठे भुवनानु विश्वोतामूं दयांवर्ष्मणोप सप्र्शामि ||
10.125.e: On the world's summit I bring forth the Father: my home is in the waters, in the ocean.  Thence I extend o’er all existing creatures, and touch even yonder heaven with my forehead.

10.125.d: अहमेव वात इव पर वाम्यारभमाणा भुवनानि विश्वा | परो दिवा पर एना पर्थिव्यैतावती महिना सं बभूव ||
10.125.e: I breathe a strong breath like the wind and tempest, the while I hold together all existence.  Beyond this wide earth and beyond the heavens I have become so mighty in my grandeur.

10.126.d: न तमंहो न दुरितं देवासो अष्ट मर्त्यम | सजोषसोयमर्यमा मित्रो नयन्ति वरुणो अति दविषः ||
10.126.e: No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man,  Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varima, of one accord, beyond his foes.

10.126.d: तद धि वयं वर्णीमहे वरुण मित्रार्यमन | येना निरंहसो यूयं पाथ नेथा च मर्त्यमति दविषः ||
10.126.e: This very thing do we desire, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,  Whereby ye guhrd the mortal man from sore distress, and lead him safe beyond his foes.

10.126.d: ते नूनं नो.अयमूतये वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा | नयिष्था उनो नेषणि पर्षिष्ठा उ नः पर्षण्यति दविषः ||
10.126.e: These are, each one, our present helps, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.  Best leaders, best deliverers to lead us on and bear as safe beyond our foes.

10.126.d: यूयं विश्वं परि पाथ वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा | युष्माकंशर्मणि परिये सयाम सुप्रणीतयो.अति दविषः ||
10.126.e: Ye compass round and guard each man, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman:  In your dear keeping may we be, ye who are excellent as guides beyond our foes.

10.126.d: आदित्यासो अति सरिधो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा | उग्रं मरुद्भीरुद्रं हुवेमेन्द्रमग्निं सवस्तये.अति दविषः ||
10.126.e: Ādityas are beyond all foes,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman:  Strong Rudra with the Marut host, Indra, Agni let us call for weal beyond our foes.

10.126.d: नेतार ऊ षु णस्तिरो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा | अति विश्वानिदुरिता राजानश्चर्षणीनामति दविषः ||
10.126.e: These lead us safely over all, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,  These who are Kings of living men, over all troubles far away beyond our foes.

10.126.d: शुनमस्मभ्यमूतये वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा | शर्म यछन्तुसप्रथ आदित्यासो यदीमहे अति दविषः ||
10.126.e: May they give bliss to aid us well, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman:  May the Ādityas, when we pray, grant us wide shelter and defence beyond our foes.

10.126.d: यथा ह तयद वसवो गौर्यं चित पदि षिताममुञ्चतायजत्राः | एवो षवस्मन मुञ्चता वयंहः पर तार्यग्नेप्रतरं न आयुः ||
10.126.e: As in this place, O Holy Ones, ye Vasus freed even the Gaud when her feet were fettered.  So free us now from trouble and affliction: and let our life be lengthened still, O Api.

10.127.d: रात्री वयख्यदायती पुरुत्रा देव्यक्षभिः | विश्वाधि शरियो.अधित ||
10.127.e: WITH all her eyes the Goddess Night looks forth approaching many a spot:  She hath put all her glories on.

10.127.d: ओर्वप्रा अमर्त्या निवतो देव्युद्वतः | जयोतिषा बाधतेतमः ||
10.127.e: Immortal. she hath filled the waste, the Goddess hath filled height and depth:  She conquers darkness with her light.
The Goddess as she comes hath set the Dawn her Sister in her place:  And then the darkness vanishes.

10.127.d: सा नो अद्य यस्या वयं नि ते यामन्न्नविक्ष्महि | वर्क्षेन वसतिं वयः ||
10.127.e: So favour us this night, O thou whose pathways we have visited  As birds their nest upon the tree.

10.127.d: नि गरामासो अविक्षत नि पद्वन्तो नि पक्षिणः | निश्येनासश्चिदर्थिनः ||
10.127.e: The villagers have sought their homes, and all that walks and all that flies,  Even the falcons fain for prey.

10.127.d: यावया वर्क्यं वर्कं यवय सतेनमूर्म्ये | अथा नःसुतरा भव ||
10.127.e: Keep off the she-wolf and the wolf, O Urmya, keep the thief away;  Easy be thou for us to pass.

10.127.d: उप मा पेपिशत तमः कर्ष्णं वयक्तमस्थित | उष रणेवयातय ||
10.127.e: Clearly hath she come nigh to me who decks the dark with richest hues:  O Morning, cancel it like debts.

10.127.d: उप ते गा इवाकरं वर्णीष्व दुहितर्दिवः | रात्रि सतोमंन जिग्युषे ||
10.127.e: These have I brought to thee like kine. O Night, thou Child of Heaven, accept  This laud as for a conqueror.

10.128.d: ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्वस्तु वयं तवेन्धानास्तन्वम्पुषेम | मह्यं नमन्तां परदिशश्चतस्रस्त्वयाध्यक्षेणप्र्तना जयेम ||
10.128.e: LET me win glory, Agni, in our battles: enkindling thee, may we support our bodies.  May the four regions bend and bow before me: with thee for guardian may we win in combat.

10.128.d: मम देवा विहवे सन्तु सर्व इन्द्रवन्तो मरुतो विष्णुरग्निः | ममान्तरिक्षमुरुलोकमस्तु मह्यं वातः पवतांकामे अस्मिन ||
10.128.e: May all the Gods be on my side in battle, the Maruts led by Indra, Viṣṇu, Agni.  Mine be the middle air's extended region, and may the wind blow favouring these my wishes.

10.128.d: मयि देवा दरविणमा यजन्तां मय्याशीरस्तु मयिदेवहूतिः | दैव्या होतारो वनुषन्त पूर्वे.अरिष्टाःस्याम तन्वा सुवीराः ||
10.128.e: May the Gods grant me riches; may the blessing and invocation of the Gods assist me.  Foremost in fight be the divine Invokers: may we, unwounded, have brave heroes round us.

10.128.d: मह्यं यजन्तु मम यानि हव्याकूतिः सत्या मनसो मे अस्तु | एनो मा नि गां कतमच्चनाहं विश्वे देवासो अधिवोचता नः ||
10.128.e: For me let them present all mine oblations, and let my mind's intention be accomplished.  May I he guiltless of the least transgression: and, all ye Gods, do ye combine to bless us.

10.128.d: देवीः षळ उर्वीरुरु नः कर्णोत विश्वे देवास इहवीरयध्वम | मा हास्महि परजया मा तनूभिर्मा रधामद्विषते सोम राजन ||
10.128.e: Ye six divine Expanses, grant us freedom: here, all ye Gods, acquit yourselves like heroes.  Let us not lose our children or our bodies: let us not benefit the foe, King Soma!

10.128.d: अग्ने मन्युं परतिनुदन परेषामदब्धो गोपाः परि पाहि नस्त्वम | परत्यञ्चो यन्तु निगुतः पुनस्ते.अमैषां चित्तम्प्रबुधां वि नेशत ||
10.128.e: Baffling the wrath of our opponents, Agni, guard us as our infallible Protector.  Let these thy foes turn back and seek their houses, and let their thought who watch at home be ruined.

10.128.d: धाता धातॄणां भुवनस्य यस पतिर्देवं तरातारमभिमातिषाहम | इमं यज्ञमश्विनोभा बर्हस्पतिर्देवाः पान्तु यजमानं नयर्थात ||
10.128.e: Lord of the world, Creator of creators the saviour God who overcomes the foeman.  May Gods, Bṛhaspati, both Aśvins shelter from ill this sacrifice and sacrificer.

10.128.d: उरुव्यचा नो महिषः शर्म यंसदस्मिन हवे पुरुहूतःपुरुक्षुः | स नः परजायै हर्यश्व मर्ळयेन्द्र मा नोरीरिषो मा परा दाः ||
10.128.e: Foodful, and much-invoked, at this our calling may the great Bull vouchsafe us wide protection.  Lord of Bay Coursers, Indra, blew our children: harm us not, give us not as prey to others.

10.128.d: ये नः सपत्ना अप ते भवन्त्विन्द्राग्निभ्यामव बाधामहेतान | वसवो रुद्रा आदित्या उपरिस्प्र्शं मोग्रं चेत्तारमधिराजमक्रन ||
10.128.e: Let those who are our foemen stay. afar from us: with Indra and with Agni we will drive them off.  Vasus, Ādityas, Rudras have exalted me, made me far-reaching, mighty, thinker, sovran lord.

10.129.d: नासदासीन नो सदासीत तदानीं नासीद रजो नो वयोमापरो यत | किमावरीवः कुह कस्य शर्मन्नम्भः किमासीद गहनं गभीरम ||
10.129.e: THEN was not non-existent nor existent: there was no realm of air, no sky beyond it.  What covered in, and where? and what gave shelter? Was water there, unfathomed depth of water?

10.129.d: न मर्त्युरासीदम्र्तं न तर्हि न रात्र्या अह्न आसीत्प्रकेतः | आनीदवातं सवधया तदेकं तस्माद्धान्यन न परः किं चनास ||
10.129.e: Death was not then, nor was there aught immortal: no sign was there, the day's and night's divider.  That One Thing, breathless, breathed by its own nature: apart from it was nothing whatsoever.

10.129.d: तम आसीत तमसा गूळमग्रे.अप्रकेतं सलिलं सर्वमािदम | तुछ्येनाभ्वपिहितं यदासीत तपसस्तन्महिनाजायतैकम ||
10.129.e: Darkness there was: at first concealed in darkness this All was indiscriminated chaos.  All that existed then was void and form less: by the great power of Warmth was born that Unit.

10.129.d: कामस्तदग्रे समवर्तताधि मनसो रेतः परथमं यदासीत | सतो बन्धुमसति निरविन्दन हर्दि परतीष्याकवयो मनीषा ||
10.129.e: Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire, the primal seed and germ of Spirit.  Sages who searched with their heart's thought discovered the existent's kinship in the non-existent.

10.129.d: तिरश्चीनो विततो रश्मिरेषामधः सविदासी.अ.अ.अत | रेतोधाासन महिमान आसन सवधा अवस्तात परयतिः परस्तात ||
10.129.e: Transversely was their severing line extended: what was above it then, and what below it?  There were begetters, there were mighty forces, free action here and energy up yonder

10.129.d: को अद्धा वेद क इह पर वोचत कुत आजाता कुत इयंविस्र्ष्टिः | अर्वाग देवा अस्य विसर्जनेनाथा को वेद यताबभूव ||
10.129.e: Who verily knows and who can here declare it, whence it was born and whence comes this creation?  The Gods are later than this world's production. Who knows then whence it first came into being?

10.129.d: इयं विस्र्ष्टिर्यत आबभूव यदि वा दधे यदि वा न | यो अस्याध्यक्षः परमे वयोमन सो अङग वेद यदि वा नवेद ||
10.129.e: He, the first origin of this creation, whether he formed it all or did not form it,  Whose eye controls this world in highest heaven, he verily knows it, or perhaps he knows not.

10.130.d: यो यज्ञो विश्वतस्तन्तुभिस्तत एकशतं देवकर्मेभिरायतः | इमे वयन्ति पितरो य आययुः पर वयाप वयेत्यासते तते ||
10.130.e: THE sacrifice drawn out with threads on every side, stretched by a hundred sacred ministers and one,—  This do these Fathers weave who hitherward are come: they sit beside the warp and cry, Weave forth, weave back.

10.130.d: पुमानेनं तनुत उत कर्णत्ति पुमान वि तत्ने अधि नाकेस्मिन | इमे मयूखा उप सेदुरू सदः सामानि चक्रुस्तसराण्योतवे ||
10.130.e: The Man extends it and the Man unbinds it: even to this vault of heaven hath he outspun, it.  These pegs are fastened to the seat of worship: they made the Sāma-hymns their weaving shuttles.

10.130.d: कासीत परमा परतिमा किं निदानमाज्यं किमासीत्परिधिः क आसीत | छन्दः किमासीत परौगं किमुक्थंयद देवा देवमयजन्त विश्वे ||
10.130.e: What were the rule, the order and the model? What were the wooden fender and the butter?  What were the hymn, the chant, the recitation, when to the God all Deities paid worship?

10.130.d: अग्नेर्गायत्र्यभवत सयुग्वोष्णिहया सविता सं बभूव | अनुष्टुभा सोम उक्थैर्महस्वान बर्हस्पतेर्ब्र्हती वाचमावत ||
10.130.e: Closely was Gāyatrī conjoined with Agni, and closely Savitar combined with Usnih.  Brilliant with Ukthas, Soma joined Anustup: Bṛhaspati's voice by Brhati was aided.

10.130.d: विराण मित्रावरुणयोरभिश्रीरिन्द्रस्य तरिष्टुब इहभागो अह्नः | विश्वान देवाञ जगत्या विवेश तेनचाक्ळिप्र रषयो मनुष्याः ||
10.130.e: Virāj adhered to Varuṇa and Mitra: here Triṣṭup day by day was Indra's portion.  Jagatī entered all the Gods together: so by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis.

10.130.d: चाक्ळिप्रे तेन रषयो मनुष्या यज्ञे जाते पितरो नःपुराणे | पश्यन मन्ये मनसा चक्षसा तान य इमंयज्ञमयजन्त पूर्वे ||
10.130.e: So by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis, when ancient sacrifice sprang up, our Fathers.  With the mind's eye I think that I behold them who first performed this sacrificial worship.

10.130.d: सहस्तोमाः सहछन्दस आव्र्तः सहप्रमा रषयः सप्तदैव्याः | पूर्वेषां पन्थामनुद्र्श्य धीरा अन्वालेभिरेरथ्यो न रश्मीन ||
10.130.e: They who were versed in ritual and metre, in hymns and rules, were the Seven Godlike Ṛṣis.  Viewing the path of those of old, the sages have taken up the reins like chariot-drivers.

10.131.d: अप पराच इन्द्र विश्वानमित्रानपापाचो अभिभूते नुदस्व | अपोदीचो अप शूराधराच उरौ यथा तव शर्मन्मदेम ||
10.131.e: DRIVE all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Conqueror, and the eastern.  Hero, drive off our northern foes and southern, that we in thy wide shelter may be joyful.

10.131.d: कुविदङग यवमन्तो यवं चिद यथा दान्त्यनुपूर्वंवियूय | इहेहैषां कर्णुहि भोजनानि ये बर्हिषोनमोव्र्क्तिं न जग्मुः ||
10.131.e: What then? As men whose fields are full of barley reap the ripe corn removing it in order,  So bring the food of those men, bring it hither, who went not to prepare the grass for worship.

10.131.d: नहि सथूर्य रतुथा यातमस्ति नोत शरवो विविदेसंगमेषु | गव्यन्त इन्द्रं सख्याय विप्रा अश्वायन्तोव्र्षणं वाजयन्तः ||
10.131.e: Men come not with one horse at sacred seasons; thus they obtain no honour in assemblies.  Sages desiring herds of kine and horses strengthen the mighty Indra for his friendship.

10.131.d: युवं सुराममश्विना नमुचावासुरे सचा | विपिपानाशुभस पती इन्द्रं कर्मस्वावतम ||
10.131.e: Ye, Aśvins, Lords of Splendour, drank full draughts of grateful Soma juice,  And aided Indra in his work with Namuci of Asura birth.

10.131.d: पुत्रमिव पितरावश्विनोभेन्द्रावथुः काव्यैर्दंसनाभिः | यत सुरामं वयपिबः शचीभिः सरस्वतीत्वा मघवन्नभिष्णक ||
10.131.e: As parents aid a son, both Aśvins, Indra, aided thee with their wondrous Powers and wisdom.  When thou, with might. hadst drunk the draught that gladdens, Sarasvatī, O Maghavan, refreshed thee.

10.131.d: इन्द्रः सुत्रामा सववानवोभिः सुम्र्ळीको भवतुविश्ववेदाः | बाधतां दवेषो अभयं कर्णोतु सुवीर्यस्यपतयः सयाम ||
10.131.e: Indra is strong to save, rich in assistance may he, possessing all, be kind and gracious.  May he disperse our foes and give us safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigou r.

10.131.d: तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे सयाम | स सुत्रामा सववानिन्द्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद दवेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ||
10.131.e: May we enjoy his favour, his the Holy may we enjoy his blessed loving kindness.  May this rich Indra, as our good Protector, drive off and keep afar all those who hate us.

10.132.d: ईजानमिद दयौर्गूर्तावसुरीजानं भूमिरभिप्रभूषणि | ईजानं देवावश्विनावभि सुम्नैरवर्धताम ||
10.132.e: MAY Dyaus the Lord of lauded wealth, and Earth stand by the man who offers sacrifice,  And may the Aśvins, both the Gods, strengthen the worshipper with bliss.

10.132.d: ता वां मित्रावरुणा धारयत्क्षिती सुषुम्नेषितत्वतायजामसि | युवोः कराणाय सख्यैरभि षयाम रक्षसः ||
10.132.e: As such we honour you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with hasty zeal, most blest, you who sustain the folk.  So may we, through your friendship for the worshipper, subdue the fiends.

10.132.d: अधा चिन नु यद दिधिषामहे वामभि परियं रेक्णःपत्यमानाः | दद्वान वा यत पुष्यति रेक्णः सं वारन्नकिरस्य मघानि ||
10.132.e: And when we seek to win your love and friendship, weẉho have precious wealth in our possession,  Or when the worshipper augments his riches let not his treasures be shut up

10.132.d: असावन्यो असुर सूयत दयौस्त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासिराजा | मूर्धा रथस्य चाकन नैतावतैनसान्तकध्रुक ||
10.132.e: That other, Asura! too was born of Heaven. thou art, O Varuṇa, the King of all men.  The chariot's Lord was well content, forbearing to anger Death by sin so great.

10.132.d: अस्मिन सवेतच्छकपूत एनो हिते मित्रे निगतान हन्ति वीरान | अवोर्वा यद धात तनूष्ववः परियासु यज्ञियास्वर्वा ||
10.132.e: This sin hath Sakaputa here committed. Heroes who fled to their dear friend he slayeth,  When the Steed bringeth down your grace and favour in bodies dear and worshipful.

10.132.d: युवोर्हि मातादितिर्विचेतसा दयौर्न भूमिः पयसापुपूतनि | अव परिया दिदिष्टन सूरो निनिक्त रश्मिभिः ||
10.132.e: Your Mother Aditi, ye wise, was purified with water even as earth is purified from heaven.  Show love and kindness here below: wash her in rays of heavenly light.

10.132.d: युवं हयप्नराजावसीदतं तिष्ठद रथं नधूर्षदं वनर्षदम | ता नः कणूकयन्तीर्न्र्मेधस्तत्रे अंहसः सुमेधस्तत्रे अंहसः ||
10.132.e: Ye Twain have seated you as Lords of Wealth, as one who mounts a car to him who sits upon the pole, upon the wood.  These our disheartened tribes Nrmedhas saved from woe, Sumedhas saved from Woe.

10.133.d: परो षवस्मै पुरोरथमिन्द्राय शूषमर्चत | अभीके चिदुलोकक्र्त संगे समत्सु वर्त्रहास्माकं बोधि चोदितानभन्तामन्यकेषां जयाका अधि धन्वसु ||
10.133.e: SING strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place.  Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encourager. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.

10.133.d: तवं सिन्धून्रवास्र्जो.अधराचो अहन्नहिम | अशत्रुरिन्द्रजज्ञिषे विश्वं पुष्यसि वार्यं तं तवा परि षवजामहेनभन्तामन्यकेषां जयाका अधि धन्वसु ||
10.133.e: Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to earth.  Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.

10.133.d: वि षु विश्वा अरातयो.अर्यो नशन्त नो धियः | अस्तासिशत्रवे वधं यो न इन्द्र जिघांसति या ते रातिर्ददिर्वसु नभन्तामन्यकेषां जयाका अधि धन्वसु ||
10.133.e: Destroyed be all malignities and all our enemy's designs.  Thy bolt thou castest, at the foe, O Indra, who would srnite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth.

10.133.d: यो न इन्द्राभितो जनो वर्कायुरादिदेशति | अधस्पदं तमीं कर्धि विबाधो असि सासहिर्नभन्तामन्यकेषां जयाकाधि धन्वसु ||
10.133.e: The robber people round about, Indra, who watch and aim at us,—  Trample them down beneath thy foot; a conquering scatterer art thou.

10.133.d: यो न इन्द्राभिदासति सनाभिर्यश्च निष्ट्यः | अव तस्यबलं तिर महीव दयौरध तमना नभन्तामन्यकेषांज्याका अधि धन्वसु ||
10.133.e: Whoso assails us, Indra, be the man a stranger or akin,  Bring down, thyself, his strength although it be as vast as are the heavens.

10.133.d: वयमिन्द्र तवायवः सखित्वमा रभामहे | रतस्य नःपथा नयाति विश्वानि दुरिता नभन्तामन्यकेषांज्याका अधि धन्वसु ||
10.133.e: Close to thy friendship do we cling, O Indra, and depend, or, thee.  Lead us beyond all pain and grief along the path of holy Law.

10.133.d: अस्मभ्यं सु तवमिन्द्र तां शिक्ष या दोहते परति वरंजरित्रे | अछिद्रोध्नी पीपयद यथा नः सहस्रधारापयसा मही गौः ||
10.133.e: Do thou bestow upon us her, O Indra, who yields according to the singer's longing,  That the great Cow may, with exhaustless udder, pouring a thousand streams, give milk to feed us.

10.134.d: उभे यदिन्द्र रोदसी आपप्राथोषा इव | महान्तं तवामहीनां सम्राजं चर्षणीनां देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र्यजीजनत ||
10.134.e: As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven.  So as the Mighty One, great King of all the mighty world of men, the Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.

10.134.d: अव सम दुर्हणायतो मर्तस्य तनुहि सथिरम | अधस्पदं तमीं कर्धि यो अस्मानादिदेशति देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद भद्राजनित्र्यजीजनत ||
10.134.e: Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness.  Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.

10.134.d: अव तया बर्हतीरिषो विश्वश्चन्द्रा अमित्रहन | शचीभिःशक्र धूनुहीन्द्र विश्वाभिरूतिभिर्देवी जनित्र्य ... ||
10.134.e: Shake down, O Slayer of the foe, those great all splendid enemies.  With all thy powers, O Śakra, all thine helps, O Indra, shake them down:

10.134.d: अव यत तवं शतक्रतविन्द्र विश्वानि धूनुषे | रयिंन सुन्वते सचा सहस्रिणीभिरूतिभिर्देवी जनित्र्य ... ||
10.134.e: As thou, O Śatakratu, thou, O Indrv, shakest all things down  As wealth for him who sheds the juice, with thine assistance thousandfold.

10.134.d: अव सवेदा इवाभितो विष्वक पतन्तु दिद्यवः | दूर्वाया इवतन्तवो वयस्मदेतु दुर्मतिर्देवी जनीत्र्य ... ||
10.134.e: Around, on every side like drops of sweat let lightning-flashes fall.  Let all malevolence pass away from us like threads of Darva grass.

10.134.d: दीर्घं हयङकुशं यथा शक्तिं बिभर्षि मन्तुमः | पूर्वेण मघवन पदाजो वयां यथा यमो देवी जनित्र्य... ||
10.134.e: Thou bearest in thine hand a lance like a long hook, great Counsellor!  As with his foremost foot a goat, draw down the branch, O Maghavan.

10.134.d: नकिर्देवा मिनीमसि नकिरा योपयामसि मन्त्रश्रुत्यंचरामसि | पक्षेभिरपिकक्षेभिरत्राभि सं रभामहे ||
10.134.e: Never, O Gods, do we offend, nor are we ever obstinate: we walk as holy texts command.  Closely we clasp and cling to you, cling to your sides, beneath your arms.

10.135.d: यस्मिन वर्क्षे सुपलाशे देवैः सम्पिबते यमः | अत्रा नोविश्पतिः पिता पुराणाननु वेनति ||
10.135.e: IN the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods,  The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires.

10.135.d: पुराणाननुवेनन्तं चरन्तं पापयामुया | असूयन्नभ्यचाक्षं तस्मा अस्प्र्हयं पुनः ||
10.135.e: I looked reluctantly on him who cherishes those men of old,  On him who treads that evil path, and then I yearned for this again.

10.135.d: यं कुमार नवं रथमचक्रं मनसाक्र्णोः | एकेषंविश्वतः पराञ्चमपश्यन्नधि तिष्ठसि ||
10.135.e: Thou mountest, though thou dost not see, O Child, the new and wheel-less car  Which thou hast fashioned mentally, onepoled but turning every way.

10.135.d: यं कुमार परावर्तयो रथं विप्रेभ्यस परि | तंसामानु परावर्तत समितो नाव्याहितम ||
10.135.e: The car which thou hast made to roll hitherward from the Sages, Child!  This hath the Sāman followed close, hence, laid together on a ship.

10.135.d: कः कुमारमजनयद रथं को निरवर्तयत | कः सवित तदद्य नो बरूयादनुदेयी यथाभवत ||
10.135.e: Who was the father of the child? Who made the chariot roll away?  Who will this day declare to us how the funeral gift was made?

10.135.d: यथाभवदनुदेयी ततो अग्रमजायत | पुरस्ताद बुध्नाततः पश्चान निरयणं कर्तम ||
10.135.e: When the funeral gift was placed, straightway the point of flame appeared.  A depth extended in the front: a passage out was made behind.

10.135.d: इदं यमस्य सादनं देवमानं यदुच्यते | इयमस्यधम्यते नाळीरयं गीर्भिः परिष्क्र्तः ||
10.135.e: Here is the seat where Yama dwells, that which is called the Home of Gods:  Here minstrels blow the flute for him here he is glorified with songs.

10.136.d: केश्यग्निं केशी विषं केशी बिभर्ति रोदसी | केशीविश्वं सवर्द्र्शे केशीदं जयोतिरुच्यते ||
10.136.e: HE with the long loose locks supports Agni, and moisture, heaven, and earth:  He is all sky to look upon: he with long hair is called this light.

10.136.d: मुनयो वातरशनाः पिशङगा वसते मला | वातस्यानुध्राजिं यन्ति यद देवासो अविक्षत ||
10.136.e: The Munis, girdled with the wind, wear garments soiled of yellow hue.  They, following the wind's swift course go where the Gods have gone before.

10.136.d: उन्मदिता मौनेयन वाताना तस्थिमा वयम | शरीरेदस्माकं यूयं मर्तासो अभि पश्यथ ||
10.136.e: Transported with our Munihood we have pressed on into the winds:  You therefore, mortal men. behold our natural bodies and no more.

10.136.d: अन्तरिक्षेण पतति विश्वा रूपावचाकशत | मुनिर्देवस्य-देवस्य सौक्र्त्याय सखा हितः ||
10.136.e: The Muni, made associate in the holy work of every God,  Looking upon all varied forms flies through the region of the air.

10.136.d: वातस्याश्वो वायोः सखाथो देवेषितो मुनिः | उभौसमुद्रावा कषेति यश्च पूर्व उतापरः ||
10.136.e: The Steed of Vāta, Vāyu's friend, the Muni, by the Gods impelled,  In both the oceans hath his home, in eastern and in western sea.

10.136.d: अप्सरसां गन्धर्वाणां मर्गाणां चरणे चरन | केशीकेतस्य विद्वान सखा सवादुर्मदिन्तमः ||
10.136.e: Treading the path of sylvan beasts, Gandharvas, and Apsarases,  He with long locks, who knows the wish, is a sweet most delightful friend

10.136.d: वायुरस्मा उपामन्थत पिनष्टि समा कुनन्नमा | केशीविषस्य पात्रेण यद रुद्रेणापिबत सह ||
10.136.e: Vāyu hath churned for him: for him he poundeth things most hard to bend,  When he with long loose locks hath drunk, with Rudra, water from the cup.

10.137.d: उत देवा अवहितं देवा उन नयथा पुनः | उतागश्चक्रुषं देवा देवा जीवयथा पुनः ||
10.137.e: YE Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low.  O Gods, restore to life again the man who hatb committed sin.

10.137.d: दवाविमौ वातौ वात आ सिन्धोरा परावतः | दक्षन्ते अन्य आ वातु परान्यो वातु यद रपः ||
10.137.e: Two several winds are blowing here, from Sindhu, from a distant land.  May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow disease away.

10.137.d: आ वात वाहि भेषजं वि वात वाहि यद रपः | तवं हिविश्वभेषजो देवानां दूत ईयसे ||
10.137.e: Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow all disease away, thou Wind;  For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods.

10.137.d: आ तवागमं शन्तातिभिरथो अरिष्टतातिभिः | दक्षन्ते भद्रमाभार्षं परा यक्ष्मं सुवामि ते ||
10.137.e: I am come nigh to thee with balms to give thee rest and keep thee safe.  I bring thee blessed strength, I drive thy weakening malady away.

10.137.d: तरायन्तामिह देवास्त्रायतां मरुतां गणः | तरायन्तां विश्वा भूतानि यथायमरपा असत ||
10.137.e: Here let the Gods deliver him, the Maruts’ band deliver him:  All things that be deliver him that he be freed from his disease.
