10.137.d: आप इद वा उ भेषजीरापो अमीवचातनीः | आपःसर्वस्य भेषजीस्तास्ते कर्ण्वन्तु भेषजम ||
10.137.e: The Waters have their healing power, the Waters drive disease away.  The Waters have a balm for all: let them make medicine for thee.

10.137.d: हस्ताभ्यां दशशाखा भयां जिह्वा वाचः पुरोगवी | अनामयित्नुभ्यां तवा तभ्यां तवोप सप्र्शामसि ||
10.137.e: The tongue that leads the voice precedes. Then with our ten-fold branching hands,  With these two chasers of disease we stroke thee with a gentle touch.

10.138.d: तव तय इन्द्र सख्येषु वह्नय रतं मन्वाना वयदर्दिरुर्वलम | यत्रा दशस्यन्नुषसो रिणन्नपः कुत्सायमन्मन्नह्यश्च दंसयः ||
10.138.e: ALLIED with thee in friendship, Indra, these, thy priests, remembering Holy Law, rent Vṛtra limb from limb,  When they bestowed the Dawns and let the waters flow, and when thou didst chastise dragons at Kutsa's call.

10.138.d: अवास्र्जः परस्वः शवञ्चयो गिरिनुदाज उस्रा अपिबोमधु परियम | अवर्धयो वनिनो अस्य दंससा शुशोचसूर्य रतजातया गिरा ||
10.138.e: Thou sentest forth productive powers, clavest the hills, thou dravest forth the kine, thou drankest pleasant meath.  Thou gavest increase through this Tree's surpassing might. The Sun shone by the hymn that sprang from Holy Law.

10.138.d: वि सूर्यो मध्ये अमुचद रथं दिवो विदद दासय परतिमानमार्यः | दर्ळानि पिप्रोरसुरस्य मायिन इन्द्रो वयास्यच्चक्र्वान रजिश्वना ||
10.138.e: In the mid-way of heaven the Sun unyoked his car: the Ārya found a match to meet his Dam foe.  Associate with Ṛjiśvan Indra overthrew the solid forts of Pipru, conjuring Asura.

10.138.d: अनाध्र्ष्टानि धर्षितो वयास्यन निधीन्रदेवानम्र्णदयास्यः | मासेव सूर्यो वसु पुर्यमा ददे गर्णानःशत्रून्रश्र्णाद विरुक्मता ||
10.138.e: He boldly cast down forts which none had e’er assailed: unwearied he destroycd the godless treasure-stores.  Like Sun and Moon he took the stronghold's wealth away, and, praised in song, demolished foes with flashing dart.

10.138.d: अयुद्धसेनो विभ्वा विभिन्दता दाशद वर्त्रहा तुज्यानि तेजते | इन्द्रस्य वज्रादबिभेदभिश्नथः पराक्रामच्छुन्ध्युरजहदुष अनः ||
10.138.e: Armed with resistless weapons, with vast power to cleave, the Vṛtra-slayer whets his darts and deals fordi wounds.  Bright Uṣas was afraid of Indra's slaughtering bolt: she went upon her way and left her chariot there.

10.138.d: एता तया ते शरुत्यानि केवला यदेक एकमक्र्णोरयज्ञम | मासां विधानमदधा अधि दयवि तवया विभिन्नम्भरति परधिं पिता ||
10.138.e: These are thy famous exploits, only thine, when thou alone hast left the other reft of sacrifice.  Thou in the heavens hast set the ordering of the Moons: the Father bears the felly portioned out by thee.

10.139.d: सूर्यरश्मिर्हरिकेशः पुरस्तात सविता जयोतिरुदयानजस्रम | तस्य पूषा परसवे याति विद्वान सम्पश्यन्विश्वा भुवनानि गोपाः ||
10.139.e: SAVITAR, golden-haired, hath lifted eastward, bright With the sunbeams, his eternal lustre;  He in whose energy wise Pūṣan marches, surveying all existence like a herdsman.

10.139.d: नर्चक्षा एष दिवो मध्य आस्त आपप्रिवान रोदसीन्तरिक्षम | स विश्वाचीरभि चष्टे घर्ताचीरन्तरापूर्वमपरं च केतुम ||
10.139.e: Beholding men he sits amid the heaven filling the two world-halves and air's wide region.  He looks upon the rich far-spreading pastures between the eastern and the western limit.

10.139.d: रायो बुध्नः संगमनो वसूनां विश्वा रूपाभि चष्टेशचीभिः | देव इव सविता सत्यधर्मेन्द्रो न तस्थौसमरे धनानाम ||
10.139.e: He, root of wealth, the gatherer-up of treasures, looks with his might on every form and figure.  Savitar, like a Godẉhose Law is constant, stands in the battle for the spoil like Indra.

10.139.d: विश्वावसुं सोम गन्धर्वमापो दद्र्शुषीस्तद रतेना वयायन | तदन्ववैदिन्द्रो रारहाण आसां परि सुर्यस्यपरिधिन्रपश्यत ||
10.139.e: Waters from sacrifice came to the Gandharva Visvavasu, O Soma, when they saw him.  Indra, approaching quickly, marked their going, and looked around upon the Sun's enclosures.

10.139.d: विश्वावसुरभि तन नो गर्णातु दिव्यो गन्धर्वो रजसोविमानः | यद वा घा सत्यमुत यन न विद्म धियोहिन्वानो धिय इन नो अव्याः ||
10.139.e: This song Visvavasu shall sing us, meter of air's mid-realm celestial Gandharva,  That we may know aright both truth and falsehood: may he inspire our thoughts and help our praises.

10.139.d: सस्निमविन्दच्चरणे नदीनामपाव्र्णोद दुरो अश्मव्रजानाम | परासां गन्धर्वो अम्र्तानि वोचदिन्द्रो दक्षं परि जानादहीनाम ||
10.139.e: In the floods' track he found the bootyseeker: the rocky cow-pen's doors he threw wide open.  These, the Gandharva told him, Rowed with Amṛta. Indra knew well the puissancc of the dragons.
